types.name: SetTenantConfigRequest

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: Tenant
message.description:
Tenant is the core identity record for a tenant in the cluster.
 `name` is unique, immutable, and becomes the tenant's SPIFFE segment:
   spiffe://<trust-domain>/tenants/<name>/...

fields.name: constraints
fields.description:
constraints is the ancestor-set limits (entitlements ceiling now; domain

message.name: Constraints
message.description:
Constraints are the limits an ancestor places on a tenant. They live on the
 Tenant record (set at CreateTenant), are mutable only by an ancestor, and are
 immutable to the tenant itself — so the tenant genuinely cannot raise its own

 entitled to administer the tenant — is NOT a field here: it is an always-on
 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

 Tenant record (set at CreateTenant), are mutable only by an ancestor, and are
 immutable to the tenant itself — so the tenant genuinely cannot raise its own
 limits. Validated on CreateTenant and SetTenantConfig.

 (The "min-admin-credential" rule — config must always contain >=1 cred_pair
 entitled to administer the tenant — is NOT a field here: it is an always-on
 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

fields.name: entitlements_ceiling
fields.description:
entitlements_ceiling is the maximum set of entitlements anyone inside this
 tenant may ever hold. Every cred_pair's entitlements ⊆ this; a sub-tenant's
 ceiling ⊆ this. Replaces the former standalone Tenant.entitlements field.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

rpcs.description:
MintServiceToken — self-mint. An internal service exchanges its Kubernetes
 token / cloud proof (bootstrap) or a kernel-signed refresh/access token for a
 token bearing its OWN identity (sub = caller SPIFFE). Never calls OPA;
 S2S tokens are identity-only. Signs Ed25519.
 auth_disabled: the caller authenticates via credentials in the request body
 (kubernetes_token / cloud_proof / kernel-signed input_token), not a bearer header.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintUserToken — on-behalf-of (AZP). A broker (oauth/saml) presents the
 user's already-IDP-validated claims; kernel runs OPA EvalEntitlement on
 them, then signs a user token with sub = user and azp = the broker's
 identity (the broker attests the claims; kernel trusts azp). Restricted to
 auth brokers. Signs Ed25519.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintDelegatedToken — standing delegation (Grant) mint. A delegate presents
 its OWN kernel-issued S2S bearer token (verified identity) plus a Grant id
 it holds. Kernel looks up the Grant, confirms the caller's verified identity
 equals grant.delegate_name, replays grant.claims into OPA fresh via the same
 EvalEntitlement path MintUserToken uses, intersects the result with
 grant.authorized_scope, and mints a short-lived access-only token: sub =
 grant.subject, act = grant.delegate_name, azp = kernel (AZP_KERNEL — kernel
 mints this directly, not on a broker's attestation). No refresh/offline
 token is issued; the delegate re-mints per use from the same Grant id.
 auth_services: ["*"] because any registered delegate may hold a grant (not
 just oauth/saml); the identity check that matters is grant.delegate_name,
 done inside the handler, exactly as doMintUserToken checks the caller
 against a Delegate today.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintToken — exchange (RT→AT→ST). The caller presents a kernel-signed token;
 kernel VERIFIES it and mints the next tier per the 3-tier rules (a refresh
 can't directly mint a service token, etc.). service_auds mints AT + N ST in
 one call. azp is preserved from the presented token onto every issued
 token. Signs Ed25519. This IS the real exchange (replaces the former
 standalone TokenExchange service).
 auth_disabled: the token to exchange is carried in the request body.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintExternalToken — WIF. A proxy presents the user token plus opaque routing
 metadata; kernel runs OPA EvalProxyPolicy, then mints an external token
 (token_use = EXTERNAL, azp = proxy) carrying the policy's aud/extra_claims,
 and returns the resolved dst_url. The PROXY — not kernel — performs the
 off-cluster api.anthropic.com exchange. Signs ES256 (WIF rejects EdDSA).
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintClientToken — cred_pair bootstrap. A client (schematicctl, CI, admins)
 presents a JWT signed by its cred_pair private key; kernel verifies the
 signature against the cred_pair PUBLIC keys held in the per-namespace config
 (ConfigState below; the root namespace's config holds the root admin
 cred_pairs seeded from Config.root_cred_pairs), and mints a bearer token
 with the resolved SPIFFE subject. S2S here; the gateway fronts this as C2S so
 pre-tenant external clients (schematic CLI, CI pipelines) can reach it.
 auth_disabled: the request body carries its own proof (no bearer header).
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintX509Cert signs an X.509 certificate under a per-service intermediate CA.
 Authentication via bearer token in the Authorization header or input_token
 in the request body (for gateway-mediated calls). auth_disabled: handler
 validates authentication internally — accepts both bearer tokens and
 request body credentials.

 On each call, kernel:
   1. Extracts the service SPIFFE identity from the token's sub claim.
   2. Gets or creates an intermediate CA for that identity
      (signed by root CA, pathlen:0).
   3. Signs the caller-provided public key (cert_request.key) under the
      intermediate CA, with the SPIFFE URI as a URI SAN.
   4. Returns X509CertChain: leaf cert + intermediate CA cert in chain.

 The intermediate CA is unique per service, providing per-service trust
 isolation — only nodes of the same service verify each other.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintWorkload mints a child workload identity. Caller must be authenticated
 (bearer token). The child's SPIFFE ID is the caller's SPIFFE ID + "/" +
 workload_name. Kernel validates: caller is not terminal.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
RevokeWorkload revokes a child workload's identity. Only the parent (or an
 ancestor in the SPIFFE path) can revoke. The revocation is recorded in
 WorkloadState and checked on refresh.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; invalidates credential/session/grant semantics without deleting a resource.

rpcs.description:
RevokeGrant revokes a standing delegation (Grant) at runtime. Only a party
 to the grant may revoke it: the user it acts for (caller sub ==
 grant.subject) or the delegate holding it (caller identity ==
 grant.delegate_name) — both are withdrawing authority they already hold,
 so neither needs a broader authorization model, exactly as RevokeWorkload
 restricts revocation to the identity's own ancestor. The grant record is
 marked (revoked_at_ms), not deleted, and the write is persisted to the
 kernel disk snapshot so it survives a restart. Every mint from the grant
 and every exchange of a token already minted from it is denied from that
 moment on.
 auth_services: ["*"] for the same reason MintDelegatedToken uses it — any
 registered delegate may hold a grant; the identity check that matters is
 done inside the handler against the grant record itself.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; invalidates credential/session/grant semantics without deleting a resource.

rpcs.description:
Acquire attempts to take the lock named by key on behalf of holder_id.
 Non-blocking: a key already held by a DIFFERENT holder returns
 granted = false rather than parking the call. Re-acquiring a key the same
 holder_id already holds is idempotent and returns the token it already
 has, so a retried Acquire after a lost response does not deadlock the
 holder against itself.
 auth_services: ["*"] — any service identity may take a lock; the key
 namespace is the caller's to partition (callers key by their own identity
 plus a discriminator), exactly as any service may mint its own token.
rpcs.verb_definition: Take exclusive hold of a named lock, returning a fencing token.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; a hold is not durable resource state the caller owns, and it may legitimately not be granted — a refused Acquire returns granted=false, not an error. NOT Mint; the token is an index into server-held state, not a self-contained credential.

rpcs.description:
Release drops the lock named by key. The caller must present the
 fencing_token it was granted; a token that is not the current one releases
 nothing and returns ok = false. That is the stale-holder case — a holder
 that lost the lock (or never had it) must not be able to release the
 holder that has it now.
rpcs.verb_definition: Give up a lock held under a fencing token.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; drops a hold without deleting the lock's key. NOT Revoke; the holder gives up its own hold rather than invalidating someone else's credential.

rpcs.verb_definition: Coordinate a mediated exchange between two parties.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Proxy; owns matching, relay, or completion semantics rather than transparently forwarding one backend call.

rpcs.description:
CreateTenant creates the tenant named by tenant_namespace (e.g. "/acme", or
 "/acme/sub" for a sub-tenant) with the given immutable constraints. The
 tenant must not already exist. Two-step: existence only — it returns the
 Tenant and nothing else (no config, no key material); bootstrap it via
 SetTenantConfig. Caller must be at-or-above tenant_namespace (ROOT "/" to
 create a top-level tenant).
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Revoke; removes resource state rather than invalidating a credential or grant.

services.name: Mint
services.description:
Mint is the platform's sole token authority and signing service, hosted by
 kernel — the cluster trust root. Kernel signs all tokens (S2S, U2S, refresh,
 external/WIF) and all X.509 certificates / workload identities. S2S-only
 (gateway fronts the client-reachable methods as C2S); kernel makes no
 off-cluster calls.

 This is the CLEAN consolidated surface (one service, was 4): the former
 kernel.Mint / kernel.MintClient / kernel.ExternalTokenMint / kernel.TokenExchange
 are unified here. azp is set ONCE at MintUserToken (azp = the broker's
 identity) and preserved unchanged through every derived token (AT from RT,
 ST from AT, and any re-mint/exchange via TokenMint).

 Tokens are signed Ed25519 (internal) except MintExternalToken, which signs
 ES256 for WIF assertion verification (Anthropic WIF rejects EdDSA).

rpcs.description:
MintServiceToken — self-mint. An internal service exchanges its Kubernetes
 token / cloud proof (bootstrap) or a kernel-signed refresh/access token for a
 token bearing its OWN identity (sub = caller SPIFFE). Never calls OPA;
 S2S tokens are identity-only. Signs Ed25519.
 auth_disabled: the caller authenticates via credentials in the request body
 (kubernetes_token / cloud_proof / kernel-signed input_token), not a bearer header.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintUserToken — on-behalf-of (AZP). A broker (oauth/saml) presents the
 user's already-IDP-validated claims; kernel runs OPA EvalEntitlement on
 them, then signs a user token with sub = user and azp = the broker's
 identity (the broker attests the claims; kernel trusts azp). Restricted to
 auth brokers. Signs Ed25519.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintDelegatedToken — standing delegation (Grant) mint. A delegate presents
 its OWN kernel-issued S2S bearer token (verified identity) plus a Grant id
 it holds. Kernel looks up the Grant, confirms the caller's verified identity
 equals grant.delegate_name, replays grant.claims into OPA fresh via the same
 EvalEntitlement path MintUserToken uses, intersects the result with
 grant.authorized_scope, and mints a short-lived access-only token: sub =
 grant.subject, act = grant.delegate_name, azp = kernel (AZP_KERNEL — kernel
 mints this directly, not on a broker's attestation). No refresh/offline
 token is issued; the delegate re-mints per use from the same Grant id.
 auth_services: ["*"] because any registered delegate may hold a grant (not
 just oauth/saml); the identity check that matters is grant.delegate_name,
 done inside the handler, exactly as doMintUserToken checks the caller
 against a Delegate today.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintToken — exchange (RT→AT→ST). The caller presents a kernel-signed token;
 kernel VERIFIES it and mints the next tier per the 3-tier rules (a refresh
 can't directly mint a service token, etc.). service_auds mints AT + N ST in
 one call. azp is preserved from the presented token onto every issued
 token. Signs Ed25519. This IS the real exchange (replaces the former
 standalone TokenExchange service).
 auth_disabled: the token to exchange is carried in the request body.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintExternalToken — WIF. A proxy presents the user token plus opaque routing
 metadata; kernel runs OPA EvalProxyPolicy, then mints an external token
 (token_use = EXTERNAL, azp = proxy) carrying the policy's aud/extra_claims,
 and returns the resolved dst_url. The PROXY — not kernel — performs the
 off-cluster api.anthropic.com exchange. Signs ES256 (WIF rejects EdDSA).
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintClientToken — cred_pair bootstrap. A client (schematicctl, CI, admins)
 presents a JWT signed by its cred_pair private key; kernel verifies the
 signature against the cred_pair PUBLIC keys held in the per-namespace config
 (ConfigState below; the root namespace's config holds the root admin
 cred_pairs seeded from Config.root_cred_pairs), and mints a bearer token
 with the resolved SPIFFE subject. S2S here; the gateway fronts this as C2S so
 pre-tenant external clients (schematic CLI, CI pipelines) can reach it.
 auth_disabled: the request body carries its own proof (no bearer header).
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintX509Cert signs an X.509 certificate under a per-service intermediate CA.
 Authentication via bearer token in the Authorization header or input_token
 in the request body (for gateway-mediated calls). auth_disabled: handler
 validates authentication internally — accepts both bearer tokens and
 request body credentials.

 On each call, kernel:
   1. Extracts the service SPIFFE identity from the token's sub claim.
   2. Gets or creates an intermediate CA for that identity
      (signed by root CA, pathlen:0).
   3. Signs the caller-provided public key (cert_request.key) under the
      intermediate CA, with the SPIFFE URI as a URI SAN.
   4. Returns X509CertChain: leaf cert + intermediate CA cert in chain.

 The intermediate CA is unique per service, providing per-service trust
 isolation — only nodes of the same service verify each other.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintWorkload mints a child workload identity. Caller must be authenticated
 (bearer token). The child's SPIFFE ID is the caller's SPIFFE ID + "/" +
 workload_name. Kernel validates: caller is not terminal.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
RevokeWorkload revokes a child workload's identity. Only the parent (or an
 ancestor in the SPIFFE path) can revoke. The revocation is recorded in
 WorkloadState and checked on refresh.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; invalidates credential/session/grant semantics without deleting a resource.

rpcs.description:
RevokeGrant revokes a standing delegation (Grant) at runtime. Only a party
 to the grant may revoke it: the user it acts for (caller sub ==
 grant.subject) or the delegate holding it (caller identity ==
 grant.delegate_name) — both are withdrawing authority they already hold,
 so neither needs a broader authorization model, exactly as RevokeWorkload
 restricts revocation to the identity's own ancestor. The grant record is
 marked (revoked_at_ms), not deleted, and the write is persisted to the
 kernel disk snapshot so it survives a restart. Every mint from the grant
 and every exchange of a token already minted from it is denied from that
 moment on.
 auth_services: ["*"] for the same reason MintDelegatedToken uses it — any
 registered delegate may hold a grant; the identity check that matters is
 done inside the handler against the grant record itself.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; invalidates credential/session/grant semantics without deleting a resource.

services.name: FencedLock
services.description:
============================================================================
 FencedLock — the platform's only distributed mutual-exclusion primitive
 ============================================================================

 Kernel is the one service that embeds Apache Ratis; every other service that
 needs a lock calls this s2s surface rather than running its own Raft group
 (decisions/kernel-convergent-only-plus-fenced-lock-2026-08-31.md). This is
 deliberately NOT a state boundary: kernel state is CONVERGENT-only, and
 mutual exclusion is a different concern from how a map replicates — the
 conflation of the two is what produced the unreal CONSISTENCY_ATOMIC mode
 that was deleted before this was written.

 A fencing token is the Raft log index of the granting Acquire. It is
 therefore strictly monotonic across the whole lock service, never reused,
 and never decreases across leader changes. A resource owner stores the
 highest token it has seen and rejects any write carrying a lower one: that,
 not the lock itself, is what makes a paused/partitioned stale holder safe.
 A lock with no fencing token only narrows the race window; it does not close
 it.

rpcs.description:
Acquire attempts to take the lock named by key on behalf of holder_id.
 Non-blocking: a key already held by a DIFFERENT holder returns
 granted = false rather than parking the call. Re-acquiring a key the same
 holder_id already holds is idempotent and returns the token it already
 has, so a retried Acquire after a lost response does not deadlock the
 holder against itself.
 auth_services: ["*"] — any service identity may take a lock; the key
 namespace is the caller's to partition (callers key by their own identity
 plus a discriminator), exactly as any service may mint its own token.
rpcs.verb_definition: Take exclusive hold of a named lock, returning a fencing token.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; a hold is not durable resource state the caller owns, and it may legitimately not be granted — a refused Acquire returns granted=false, not an error. NOT Mint; the token is an index into server-held state, not a self-contained credential.

rpcs.description:
Release drops the lock named by key. The caller must present the
 fencing_token it was granted; a token that is not the current one releases
 nothing and returns ok = false. That is the stale-holder case — a holder
 that lost the lock (or never had it) must not be able to release the
 holder that has it now.
rpcs.verb_definition: Give up a lock held under a fencing token.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; drops a hold without deleting the lock's key. NOT Revoke; the holder gives up its own hold rather than invalidating someone else's credential.

services.name: CliTokenBroker
services.description:
============================================================================
 CLI Token Broker — kernel-mediated nonce matching for CLI auth
 ============================================================================

 Each oauth instance opens a BrokerStream on startup. The protocol:
   1. OAuth sends Register (instance_id) — identifies this stream
   2. CLI auth starts: OAuth sends RegisterNonce (nonce)
   3. Browser completes auth: OAuth sends CompleteNonce (nonce, subject, claims)
   4. Kernel matches nonces, mints token, sends TokenDelivery back to the
      oauth instance that registered the nonce
   5. OAuth delivers the token to the CLI over the Session bidi stream

 Nonce registry is in-memory. Kernel restarts clear it (CLI retries).

rpcs.verb_definition: Coordinate a mediated exchange between two parties.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Proxy; owns matching, relay, or completion semantics rather than transparently forwarding one backend call.

services.name: TenantAdmin
services.description:
TenantAdmin is kernel's tenant/project control plane. There is no separate
 cluster-admin service: the namespace tree is uniform (ROOT "/" + tenants +
 projects) and every RPC is ordinary C2S, gated by the single generated
 entitlement authorizer, which enforces the level-or-below rule (caller must be
 at-or-above the target namespace) declaratively via each method's
 target_namespace_field. A caller entitled at ROOT manages top-level tenants; a
 tenant admin manages its own subtree. Handlers trust the inbound namespace
 strings (authorization already happened in the interceptor).

rpcs.description:
CreateTenant creates the tenant named by tenant_namespace (e.g. "/acme", or
 "/acme/sub" for a sub-tenant) with the given immutable constraints. The
 tenant must not already exist. Two-step: existence only — it returns the
 Tenant and nothing else (no config, no key material); bootstrap it via
 SetTenantConfig. Caller must be at-or-above tenant_namespace (ROOT "/" to
 create a top-level tenant).

rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

types.name: Config
types.description: Config is rendered by operator and mounted into kmaker at startup.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description: cluster_name is the logical Schematic cluster this kmaker signs for.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for kmaker.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO

fields.name: api_key_hint_chars
fields.description:
api_key_hint_chars is how many trailing characters of a stored key the read
 surface may echo back, so a person can tell WHICH key is saved without the
 key being retrievable. Config rather than a constant because it is a

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is (spec.principal): the generated wrapper resolves the authenticated
 caller's subject and stamps it when empty, accepts it when it matches, and
 refuses with INVALID_ARGUMENT when it differs. A caller therefore cannot
 read someone else's settings, and the handler does not check.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is (spec.namespace): the same stamp/accept/refuse control on the
 caller's tenant claim. Declared on a READ, like mailbox.ListHeldMailRequest
 and for the same reason: this handler selects a row out of kernel state by
 predicate rather than handing a list to the egress filter, and the
 predicate needs the caller's verified tenant.

fields.name: settings
fields.description:
settings is 0 or 1 rows. Bounded at 1 because more than one settings row
 for one principal is not a large response, it is a broken store.

message.name: LlmProviderSettings
message.description:
LlmProviderSettings is ONE person's LLM API settings. It is both the stored row and
 the read response's item type, deliberately: `(spec.store_principal)` and
 `(spec.store_namespace)` filter repeated fields OF THIS TYPE on the way out,
 so a bespoke response row would be a read path with the generated backstops
 switched off (mailbox.ListHeldMailResponse says the same thing).

 Returning the stored type is only safe because `api_key` carries
 (spec.redact) — see there.

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is the collection key AND the row's owning principal.

 (spec.indexed) makes it the state collection's key, so there is exactly one
 row per person by construction rather than by a uniqueness check somebody
 has to remember to write. (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's
 reads to their own row: the generated wrapper filters every repeated
 LlmProviderSettings field in a response down to rows the caller owns, so the
 handler does not check and there is nothing left for it to get wrong.

fields.name: endpoint_url
fields.description:
endpoint_url is the LLM API base URL.

 HTTPS ONLY, and that is not tidiness: this field's companion is a bearer
 secret, and the service that eventually calls this endpoint would put that
 secret in an Authorization header. Permitting http:// here would let a
 person configure their own key's exfiltration. (spec.assert_url) is the
 generated check — nothing in the handler parses a URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: api_key
fields.description:
api_key is the secret, and (spec.redact) REDACT_MODE_DROP is what makes
 storing it here safe.

 DROP is the hard floor: the generated sanitize transform clears this field
 on EVERY egress copy and no runtime entitlement can loosen it, so the value
 is write-only from a caller's point of view. That transform is emitted into
 the generated service wrapper for unary responses, not into this service's
 handler — the handler could not leak the key by forgetting to clear it,
 because it is not the thing doing the clearing.

 tacplus also injects a companion `api_key_redacted` bool alongside this
 field and sets it on the sanitized copy. It is NOT the "is a key saved"
 signal a form needs: the transform sets it unconditionally, so it is true
 on every response whether or not anything is stored. That question is
 answered by api_key_set below.

fields.name: api_key_set
fields.description:
api_key_set says whether a key is stored, and exists because the redacted
 field cannot say so — a dropped value and an absent one are both the empty
 string on the wire. Maintained by the handler on write.

 It is what lets the form render "a key is saved — replace it?" rather than
 an empty box that silently means either thing.

fields.name: api_key_hint
fields.description:
api_key_hint is the last Config.api_key_hint_chars characters of the stored
 key, so a person with several keys can tell WHICH one is saved. Not
 redacted: it is a deliberate, bounded disclosure, and the bound is the
 config knob rather than this field's own max_size so that lowering the knob
 takes effect on the next write instead of needing a proto change.

 8 is the ceiling Config.api_key_hint_chars enforces; this bound restates it
 so an oversized value is rejected by generated validation even if a future
 handler computes it wrong.

fields.name: updated_at_ms
fields.description: updated_at_ms is when the row was last written. Server-assigned.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by exact string equality against the
 reader's namespace claim. (spec.store_namespace) generates the read-side
 egress filter on every surface returning this row; the write half is
 UpdateLlmSettingsRequest.namespace's (spec.namespace).

types.name: LlmProviderSettingsEntitlement
LlmSettingsState
types.description:
LlmSettingsState is the service's state root, hosted by kernel.

 Kernel state rather than a Stratum record, and the reason is the same one
 mailbox.proto gives: this is read-modify-write by key with read-back on the
 very next call. A record reaches the store through an EventBus publish and an
 asynchronous ingest, so a settings form that saved and then re-read would
 race its own write. Records are for append-shaped history; this is one
 mutable row per person.

fields.name: api_key_hint_chars
fields.description:
api_key_hint_chars is how many trailing characters of a stored key the read
 surface may echo back, so a person can tell WHICH key is saved without the

 redeploy. 0 disables the hint entirely.

types.name: SortField
UpdateLlmSettingsRequest

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is (spec.principal) — see ListMyLlmSettingsRequest. It is what makes
 "save MY settings" unable to name anybody else's row, before the handler
 runs.

fields.name: endpoint_url
fields.description:
endpoint_url is required on every save: it is the half of the settings that
 is not a secret, so there is no "leave it alone" case to represent — a
 caller that wants it unchanged sends back what it just read.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: api_key
fields.description:
api_key is OPTIONAL on a save, and empty means LEAVE THE STORED KEY ALONE.

 That asymmetry with endpoint_url is forced by the redaction: a client never
 holds the current key, so it cannot send it back unchanged the way it can
 an endpoint. Empty therefore has to mean "no change" — the alternative,
 clearing on empty, would delete a person's key every time they edited only
 the URL.

 Removing a key is consequently not something this RPC can express. Nothing
 needs it yet, and inventing a clear_api_key flag before something does
 would be inventing product; see questions.md.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is (spec.namespace) — the write half of the tenant pair. This RPC
 writes rows, so the marker is doing its primary job here: binding the value
 the handler then stamps onto LlmProviderSettings.namespace.

types.name: UpdateLlmSettingsResponse

fields.name: updated_at_ms
fields.description:
updated_at_ms is the timestamp the saved row now carries.

 The row itself is NOT echoed back. A singular `LlmProviderSettings settings` field
 here would be the shape the (spec.store_namespace) egress backstop skips —
 it is generated only for repeated fields — so echoing one would be the one
 response in this file with the tenant filter switched off. The client
 re-reads through ListMyLlmSettings, which has it.

rpcs.description:
ListMyLlmSettings returns the calling principal's own LLM settings: zero
 rows when nothing has been saved, one when something has. The api_key is
 never among them.

 LIST, NOT GET, and the verb is not a style choice. The response carries a
 repeated field, tacplus classifies that as a collection read, and its
 closed verb registry refuses a collection read spelled Get. The response is
 repeated in the first place because that is the only shape the
 (spec.store_namespace) egress backstop is generated for — it skips any
 field that is not repeated, so a singular `LlmProviderSettings settings` would
 carry the annotation and generate no backstop at all, silently. Same
 finding as scottyagent.ListMyAgentStateResponse.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdateLlmSettings saves the caller's endpoint and, when one is supplied, a
 new API key.

 Update rather than Create, and there is no Create: a person's settings row
 is upsert-shaped — the first save and the fifth are the same operation, and
 a Create/Update pair would make the client ask "does my row exist yet"
 before it could save. `Set` is a registered synonym of Update, so this is
 the canonical spelling of that verb.

NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.
NOT Revoke; removes resource state rather than invalidating a credential or grant.

services.name: LlmSettings
services.description:
LlmSettings is user-facing: it accepts user tokens minted from a browser
 login. There is no s2s read surface on it yet, and that is not an oversight —
 nothing calls an LLM in this fleet today. The service that eventually does
 declares `(spec.grpc_s2s_client)` for it and this file grows one s2s rpc.

fields.name: sweep_interval_seconds
fields.description:
sweep_interval_seconds is how often the eviction-eligibility sweep runs.

 The sweep is a RECONCILER, not the primary path: UpdateHeldMail marks a row
 eligible inline when it retrieves it. The sweep exists because that inline
 mark can be missed — a publish that hit backpressure, or a row retrieved by
 an instance that died before the publish landed — and because a non-zero
 retrieved_grace_seconds below defers the mark by construction. Held in
 config rather than as a constant for the same reason
 messaging.Config.max_recipients is: changing it in kernel must change
 behaviour with no redeploy.

fields.name: retrieved_grace_seconds
fields.description:
retrieved_grace_seconds is how long after retrieval a row stays
 NEVER-evict before the sweep marks it WINDOW.

 Zero — the default — is the decision doc's ruling taken literally:
 "retrieved_at_ms is the point item 4's eviction eligibility starts counting
 from". Marking at grace 0 makes the row's `(spec.store_epoch)`, which is
 what the residency window is measured against, equal to the retrieval
 instant, so the window counts from retrieval and from nothing else.

 It is a knob rather than a constant because a client that acks and then
 immediately re-reads is a real pattern, and a non-zero grace keeps the row
 resident across that gap. It can never make an UNRETRIEVED row evictable:
 the sweep's predicate is status == RETRIEVED before it is anything else.
