message.name: MailboxEntry
message.description:
MailboxEntry is ONE DELIVERY'S mailbox state, keyed by the SAME delivery_id
 as the `messaging.Message` it tracks.

 Joinable by identity, not by a second lookup: an entry and its message share
 a key, so "fetch the body of the mail I was just told about" is one Message
 read with an id the client already holds.

 IT HOLDS NO BODY. `messaging.Message.text` is never copied here — that is the
 decision doc's rejected alternative ("Mailbox stores full message content"),
 and it stands. What IS carried is the inbox SUMMARY LINE the doc's own
 ListHeldMail spec enumerates (sender, subject, sent_at_ms): a mail client
 renders a list before anything is opened, and those three fields are the only
 way to serve that list without a second round trip per row. A summary line is
 not a second copy of the message, and the field that would make it one —
 `text` — is absent, as are `recipients` and `ticket_id`.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.description:
delivery_id is the record key and messaging.Message.delivery_id verbatim.
 Bounded identically (512) — a shorter bound here would silently drop the
 deliveries whose recipient subject is long.

fields.name: message_id
fields.description:
message_id groups the N entries of one submission, the same way it groups
 the N Messages. EQ-filterable for the same reason it is there.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is whose mailbox this is, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL — the
 same field, carrying the same annotation, as messaging.Message.recipient.
 The generated egress filter holds a caller's reads to their own rows, so
 ListHeldMail cannot return one person's mail to another even if this
 service's own predicate were wrong.

 spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 mailbox's own service identity, stamped by eventbus — so it is the wrong
 field to filter a user's reads on, exactly as it is on Message.

enum_values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_HELD
enum_values.description:
HELD: the delivery arrived on the topic and nobody has pulled it. The row
 must not be evicted in this state at any age — an unread message aging out
 defeats the entire point of a mailbox.

enum_values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_RETRIEVED
enum_values.description:
RETRIEVED: the recipient acknowledged pulling it. This is what starts
 eviction eligibility, and nothing else does.

fields.name: held_since_ms
fields.description:
held_since_ms is when this consumer group's copy landed — the residency
 clock in the doc's phrasing, and the timestamp retention above measures
 from. It is NOT what eviction eligibility counts from; see retrieved_at_ms.

 RANGE-filterable because "what has been sitting in my mailbox since last
 week" is a question about this field.

fields.name: retrieved_at_ms
fields.description:
retrieved_at_ms is unset until retrieved, and is the point eviction
 eligibility starts counting from. The decision doc rejects held_since_ms
 for this in as many words: "a message nobody has pulled yet must not be
 evicted just because it is old."

fields.name: sender
fields.description:
sender is messaging.Message.sender — the authenticated principal that sent
 it, never a caller-written string on either side.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: subject is the subject line. Bounded identically to Message.subject.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is the sender's clock, carried through so an inbox can sort by
 when a message was SENT rather than by when this consumer group happened to
 process it. The two differ by broker latency and by any replay.

fields.name: ejectionable
fields.description:
ejectionable is item 4's marker and this record's whole reason to exist —
 the first per-row use of it in the fleet.

 The values are not decoration and are not derivable from `status` by the
 store: the store does not know what HELD means, and UNSPECIFIED is defined
 as never-evict precisely so a marker an author forgets keeps the row.

   HELD      -> EJECTIONABLE_NEVER   (explicitly, not left at UNSPECIFIED:
                the row is stating a policy, not omitting one)
   RETRIEVED -> EJECTIONABLE_WINDOW  (set by UpdateHeldMail inline, or by
                the sweep when a grace period deferred it)

 it evicts the row FROM MEMORY. It does not delete it. `Residency`'s own
 definition — "a warm row evicted from memory is still complete and
 queryable on disk" — is the semantics, and deletion is retention's job
 above, ninety days from arrival. There is deliberately no EVICTED status
 and no delete path here: a status this service wrote would be a claim about
 the store's memory that this service cannot observe.

enum_values.name: EJECTIONABLE_NEVER
enum_values.description:
NEVER: the residency window does not apply to this row. It stays resident
 for as long as the type's rows are retained at all. The explicit spelling
 of an absent value, the same way RetentionPolicy.forever is.

enum_values.name: EJECTIONABLE_WINDOW
enum_values.description:
WINDOW: the residency window applies to this row as declared — it is
 evicted from memory once its (spec.store_epoch) is older than the window,
 and served from disk thereafter.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is the row's LAST WRITE, stamped by the generated wrapper
 and never by this service. It is what the residency window is actually
 measured against, which is why marking a row WINDOW is a WRITE: the mark
 and the clock it starts are the same event.

 RANGE per (spec.store_epoch)'s own contract — it is the predicate a
 two-leg memory/disk query partitions on.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner, and the name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's
 topic discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type
 when deciding which topics get publisher-identity stamping.

 It holds MAILBOX'S OWN service identity — this service is the publisher.
 `recipient` above is where the person is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by EXACT string equality against the
 caller's namespace claim. MANDATORY: tacplus fails generation for any

 nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 authenticated caller's subject and stamps it when empty, accepts it when it

 audit rpc which omits it, because this handler does not merely return rows
 for the generated egress filter to police — it selects them out of kernel
 state by predicate, and the predicate needs the caller's verified tenant.

types.name: MailboxState
types.description:
MailboxState is this service's state root, stored in kernel's cluster.

 WHY KERNEL STATE AND NOT A REPLAY OF ITS OWN RECORD TOPIC. mailbox's rows are
 mutable (HELD -> RETRIEVED) and it needs to read its own rows back to serve
 ListHeldMail. Two paths were available and one of them does not work:

   - Read them back from the record store. The record query plane's S2S half
     (RecordMap) authorizes exactly one peer audience, declared in the app's
     `(spec.trait)` file, and that audience is the record store itself — a
     deliberately closed door since 2026-09-01, when the placeholder `argus`
     it had named was deleted with the service. mailbox cannot read stratum
     without an edit to a different repo's trait declaration, which is an
     authorization change this task has no mandate to make.
   - Rebuild an in-memory index by replaying its own topic. EventBus honours
     `start_from: earliest` with a real `seekToBeginning` on every assignment
     (KafkaSubscriber.applyStartPosition), so the replay itself would work —
     but the Message topic replays too, concurrently, and a Message replay that
     lands after the MailboxEntry replay for the same delivery_id would write a
     RETRIEVED row back to HELD. There is no "caught up" signal to order them.

 Kernel state has neither problem: it is durable, it is read-modify-write by
 key, and `sm.state_clients()` is the generated path to it. This is scotty's
 shape — a state root in kernel holding the service's own rows, with a record
 published alongside them — and it is used here for the same reason.

sent_at_ms is the sender's clock, carried through so an inbox can sort by
 when a message was SENT rather than by when this consumer group happened to
 process it. The two differ by broker latency and by any replay.

fields.name: ejectionable
fields.description:
ejectionable is item 4's marker and this record's whole reason to exist —
 the first per-row use of it in the fleet.

 The values are not decoration and are not derivable from `status` by the
 store: the store does not know what HELD means, and UNSPECIFIED is defined
 as never-evict precisely so a marker an author forgets keeps the row.

   HELD      -> EJECTIONABLE_NEVER   (explicitly, not left at UNSPECIFIED:
                the row is stating a policy, not omitting one)
   RETRIEVED -> EJECTIONABLE_WINDOW  (set by UpdateHeldMail inline, or by
                the sweep when a grace period deferred it)

 WHAT "EVICT" DOES, stated plainly because the decision doc left it open:
 it evicts the row FROM MEMORY. It does not delete it. `Residency`'s own
 definition — "a warm row evicted from memory is still complete and
 queryable on disk" — is the semantics, and deletion is retention's job
 above, ninety days from arrival. There is deliberately no EVICTED status
 and no delete path here: a status this service wrote would be a claim about
 the store's memory that this service cannot observe.

enum_values.name: EJECTIONABLE_NEVER
enum_values.description:
NEVER: the residency window does not apply to this row. It stays resident
 for as long as the type's rows are retained at all. The explicit spelling
 of an absent value, the same way RetentionPolicy.forever is.

enum_values.name: EJECTIONABLE_WINDOW
enum_values.description:
WINDOW: the residency window applies to this row as declared — it is
 evicted from memory once its (spec.store_epoch) is older than the window,
 and served from disk thereafter.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is the row's LAST WRITE, stamped by the generated wrapper
 and never by this service. It is what the residency window is actually
 measured against, which is why marking a row WINDOW is a WRITE: the mark
 and the clock it starts are the same event.

 RANGE per (spec.store_epoch)'s own contract — it is the predicate a
 two-leg memory/disk query partitions on.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner, and the name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's
 topic discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type
 when deciding which topics get publisher-identity stamping.

 It holds MAILBOX'S OWN service identity — this service is the publisher.
 `recipient` above is where the person is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by EXACT string equality against the
 caller's namespace claim. MANDATORY: tacplus fails generation for any
 (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record
 nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 Its value is copied from the Message that produced this entry rather than
 resolved again: the tenant of a mailbox entry IS the tenant of the delivery
 it tracks, and re-deriving it from mailbox's own service token would stamp
 the SERVICE's tenant onto a USER's row.

 Not a (spec.query_field): the field exists to be the egress boundary, and a
 boundary a caller can name in a predicate is not one.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is (spec.principal) — see ListHeldMailRequest. It is what makes
 "retrieve MY mail" unable to name anybody else's delivery, before the
 handler runs.

fields.name: delivery_ids
fields.description:
delivery_ids are the deliveries being acknowledged. Bounded to the page
 ListHeldMail hands out, because acking a page you were just given is the
 shape this RPC is for.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is (spec.namespace) — the write half of the tenant pair. This RPC
 WRITES rows, so the marker is doing its primary job here: binding the value
 the handler then holds a row's own stamped namespace against.

types.name: UpdateHeldMailResponse

fields.name: retrieved_delivery_ids
fields.description:
retrieved_delivery_ids is what this call actually changed from HELD to
 RETRIEVED — a SUBSET of the request's ids, and the difference is the point.
 An id that was already retrieved, or that names no entry of the caller's,
 is absent here rather than an error, so a client can tell "I acked this
 just now" from "this was already acked" without either being a failure.

fields.name: retrieved_at_ms
fields.description:
retrieved_at_ms is the timestamp stamped on the entries this call retrieved
 — one clock for the call, the same way messaging takes one sent_at_ms for a
 whole submission. Zero when the call retrieved nothing.

rpcs.description:
ListHeldMail returns the deliveries still HELD for the calling recipient.

 It is the "do I have new mail" poll, and it returns no message body — only
 enough to know what to fetch from messaging. See MailboxEntry's comment.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdateHeldMail marks deliveries RETRIEVED, which is what makes them
 eviction-eligible.

 NOT `RetrieveMail`, which is what the decision doc calls it. The RPC verb
 registry is CLOSED (tacplus/pkg/internal/common/verbs/registry.json) and
 `Retrieve` is neither a registered verb nor a folded synonym of one, so
 that name does not generate at all — verbs.Classify hard-fails any c2s
 method whose leading verb is unregistered. This is the same trap item 5 hit
 with `Submit` (resolved there to `Send`). `Update` is the registered verb
 whose definition is this operation — "modify an existing resource" — and
 the rows it modifies are the ones `ListHeldMail` just returned, so the pair
 reads as one noun with two verbs. Nothing about the semantics the doc
 settled changes: the operation, its idempotency and its effect on
 `retrieved_at_ms` are exactly as specified there.

 IDEMPOTENT. Naming an id that is already RETRIEVED is a no-op, not an
 error: a client polling on reconnect must not fail on ids it already acked,
 and the FIRST retrieval's timestamp is the one that stands — a second call
 must not push the eviction clock forward.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.
NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.
NOT Revoke; removes resource state rather than invalidating a credential or grant.
NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.
NOT Send; fan-out to topic subscribers.

rpcs.verb_definition: Open a long-lived domain stream that is not a collection WATCH envelope.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Watch; use Watch only for generated collection snapshot/upsert/delete streams.
NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

enums.name: MailboxEntryStatus
enums.description:
MailboxEntryStatus is the two-state life of an entry. There is no EVICTED
 state, and that absence is the design: see MailboxEntry.ejectionable.

 TOP-LEVEL, not nested inside MailboxEntry, and that is not style. A nested
 enum is the ONE shape in this fleet nothing had used — every enum in
 platform/proto and scotty/proto is top-level — and generating one emits Rust
 helpers referring to a type `MailboxEntry_Status` that prost never declares
 (it renders `mailbox_entry::Status`), so the model crate does not compile.
 Reported in workers/big8-p1-mailbox-questions.md rather than patched around
 in the generator, which this task has no mandate to change. The naming
 follows scotty.SkillClassification: the enum's own name as the value prefix.

values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_HELD
values.description:
HELD: the delivery arrived on the topic and nobody has pulled it. The row
 must not be evicted in this state at any age — an unread message aging out
 defeats the entire point of a mailbox.

values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_RETRIEVED
values.description:
RETRIEVED: the recipient acknowledged pulling it. This is what starts
 eviction eligibility, and nothing else does.

 tells it what they have taken.

types.name: AgentReceivedReceipt
types.description:
AgentReceivedReceipt is the delivery ACK — the agent (scotty, the mailbox
 service) took the record off the topic and processed it. Written by the
 consumer, never by the sender or by this service.

 It is the ACK, not a copy of it: there is one event here, not a delivery ACK
 plus a receipt derived from it.

fields.name: received_at_ms
fields.description:
received_at_ms is when the consuming agent completed processing — the same
 instant it commits its consumer-group offset, since committing before
 processing is exactly the discipline the queue semantics forbid.

fields.name: received_by
fields.description: received_by is the SPIFFE identity of the consuming agent instance.

types.name: Config
types.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_recipients
fields.description:
max_recipients bounds the recipient fan-out of ONE submission, and it is a
 resource limit on the service, not a business rule: N recipients means N
 publishes, so an unbounded list is an unbounded amount of work bought with
 one RPC. Held in config rather than as a constant for the same reason
 tasks.Config.max_open_tasks is — changing it in kernel must change
 behaviour with no redeploy.

 It must not exceed SendMessageRequest.recipients' assert_max_size (256):
 the two describe the same cap and the generated request validation is the
 hard edge, so a config above it could never take effect.

types.name: EventBusRecordMeta
HumanViewedReceipt
types.description:
HumanViewedReceipt fires when the actual person looked at the message. A
 distinct signal from AgentReceivedReceipt above: an agent can have ACKed a
 message hours before a human sees it, and business-hours-deferred
 presentation makes that gap the normal case rather than the exception.

 Presentation is a passive pull label — the reader is told "viewed", never
 pushed a notification. That is the design already built for tickets
 (decisions/ticket-read-receipts-2026-08-30.md), relocated to where it
 belongs.

fields.name: viewed_at_ms
fields.description: viewed_at_ms is when the person actually looked.

fields.name: viewed_by
fields.description:
viewed_by is the principal subject of the person who looked. It is normally
 equal to Message.recipient — a delivery is viewed by its addressee — but it
 is stored rather than assumed, because a delegate viewing on someone's
 behalf is a real case and an inferred value could not tell the two apart.

types.name: MapEmpty
Message
types.description:
Message is ONE DELIVERY: one message, to one recipient.

 It is NOT one row per submission. A submission naming three recipients
 becomes three `Message` rows sharing a `message_id`, differing in
 `delivery_id` and `recipient`, each independently consumable and
 independently ACKable. See the fan-out note at the top of this file for why
 EventBus cannot do that split itself.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 MessageBus with topic ref messaging.MessageBus.stream. Do NOT hand-write that
 wrapper.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.description:
delivery_id is the record key: "<message_id>/<recipient>". One per
 (message, recipient) pair, which is what makes the N publishes of one
 submission N separately-keyed records rather than N copies of one.

 Derived rather than random ON PURPOSE: the value a caller would need to
 reconstruct to ACK a delivery is exactly (which message, for whom), so
 deriving it means an agent that knows both never has to have been told the
 id. It is also what makes the fan-out replay-safe — a retried submission
 regenerates the same delivery ids rather than a second set of rows.

fields.name: message_id
fields.description:
message_id groups the N deliveries of ONE submission. EQ-filterable,
 because "every delivery of the message I sent" is the question a sender
 asks, and it is the only way back from a delivery to its siblings.

fields.name: sender
fields.description:
sender is who sent it — the authenticated principal subject bound by the
 (spec.principal) field on SendMessageRequest below, never a caller-written
 string.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is THE recipient this delivery is for — one of `recipients`
 below, and the half of delivery_id that varies across the fan-out.

 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s
 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 eventbus stamps messaging's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. `sender` is the
 other candidate and is the wrong one: a mailbox read is "messages addressed
 to me", so the field the generated egress filter holds a caller's reads to
 must be the addressee.

 The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a SENDER cannot read their own
 sent messages through this record's c2s plane, because only one field may
 carry (spec.store_principal) and this is it. Sent-items is a mailbox
 concern and the mailbox service is Phase 1 item 8, undesigned; inventing a
 second read path for it here would be inventing that service's shape.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: recipients
fields.description:
recipients is the full To: line — every recipient of the submission, the
 SAME list on all N deliveries. `recipient` above says which one this row is
 for; this says who else got it.

 Carrying it is not redundancy. Without it a recipient cannot see who else
 was addressed, which is information the sender chose to disclose by
 addressing them together — the same reason a To: header exists and a Bcc:
 one does not. (This file models no Bcc; nothing has asked for one.)

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_recipients' ceiling above.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: subject is the message's subject line.

fields.name: text
fields.description: text is the message body. Free text, and nothing parses it — see ticket_id.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
ticket_id OPTIONALLY references the ticket this message pertains to.

 A dedicated field, never a value embedded in `text`. Routing and status
 display have to associate a message with its ticket to act, and the
 standing rule is that anything that must be parsed to be acted on should
 have been a field. Optional because most messages pertain to no ticket, and
 EQ-filterable because "every message about this ticket" is the question the
 field exists to answer.

 This is the ONLY ticket-shaped thing on Message, and it is an opaque id.
 Ticket's own churn — advice sealing, decision chains, amend/reconsider —
 stays entirely inside Ticket. That is what keeps this type stable.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is the business clock — when the sender submitted — and the
 RANGE criterion, because "my messages from last week" is the question a
 mailbox asks. It is what retention above measures age from.

 Identical across all N deliveries of one submission: they were one act.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off.

 It holds MESSAGING'S OWN service identity, not the sender's, because the
 publish is s2s from this service — that is the direct consequence of the
 SUPERSEDED ruling. `sender` above is where the human is.

fields.name: spiffe_actor
fields.description:
spiffe_actor is the ORIGIN signal: the delegate that made the call, stamped
 by EventBus from the publishing token's `act` claim at publish time.

   "a message is marked as originating from the user directly or from the
    user's Scotty acting on their behalf... A message sent by
    Scotty-for-Dennis carries `act` populated; one Dennis sends directly
    doesn't." — decisions/messaging-vs-ticketing-2026-08-31.md

 The service does not set it and must not: like spiffe_id above, a value
 written here would be a claim about identity that nothing verified.
 Provenance only — sys/spec.proto forbids wiring it into a principal.

 GAP, STATED NOT PAPERED OVER. That quote describes the pre-supersession
 model, where the user published to EventBus DIRECTLY and EventBus saw the
 user's own delegated token. Under the corrected model the publish is s2s
 from messaging, so the token EventBus stamps from is messaging's own
 service token and carries no `act` claim at all — this field will be empty
 in the ordinary case, including for a genuine Scotty-for-Dennis send. The
 annotation is declared anyway, and correctly: the seam is the right one and
 the field is where the value belongs the moment the delegated-publish path
 exists. Closing it needs an s2s publish that carries the caller's exchanged
 token, which the generated publisher does not offer today. Written up in
 workers/big8-p1-messaging-questions.md rather than hand-rolled around.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that sent
 this message" is one predicate asked of two record types.

 Empty is legitimate: a call with no authenticated Caller has none to read.

fields.name: agent_received
fields.description:
agent_received is the delivery ACK, written by the consuming agent after it
 processes this delivery. Unset at publish — this service never writes it.

message.name: AgentReceivedReceipt
message.description:
AgentReceivedReceipt is the delivery ACK — the agent (scotty, the mailbox
 service) took the record off the topic and processed it. Written by the
 consumer, never by the sender or by this service.

 It is the ACK, not a copy of it: there is one event here, not a delivery ACK
 plus a receipt derived from it.

fields.name: received_at_ms
fields.description:
received_at_ms is when the consuming agent completed processing — the same
 instant it commits its consumer-group offset, since committing before
 processing is exactly the discipline the queue semantics forbid.

fields.name: received_by
fields.description: received_by is the SPIFFE identity of the consuming agent instance.

fields.name: human_viewed
fields.description:
human_viewed is the separately-typed human signal. Unset at publish, and
 unset for as long as the person has not looked, which is the normal state
 of a delivered message.

message.name: HumanViewedReceipt
message.description:
HumanViewedReceipt fires when the actual person looked at the message. A
 distinct signal from AgentReceivedReceipt above: an agent can have ACKed a
 message hours before a human sees it, and business-hours-deferred
 presentation makes that gap the normal case rather than the exception.

 Presentation is a passive pull label — the reader is told "viewed", never
 pushed a notification. That is the design already built for tickets
 (decisions/ticket-read-receipts-2026-08-30.md), relocated to where it
 belongs.

fields.name: viewed_at_ms
fields.description: viewed_at_ms is when the person actually looked.

fields.name: viewed_by
fields.description:
viewed_by is the principal subject of the person who looked. It is normally
 equal to Message.recipient — a delivery is viewed by its addressee — but it
 is stored rather than assumed, because a delegate viewing on someone's
 behalf is a real case and an inferred value could not tell the two apart.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by EXACT string equality against the
 caller's namespace claim (never the level-or-below containment the
 administrative namespace rule uses). It is the tenant half of the identity
 `recipient` carries the subject half of: that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant".

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 TWO DIFFERENT ENFORCEMENTS, and they are not the same failure:
   - WRITE (this record's publish path). eventbus's PublishHandler stamps
     this field from the publishing token's namespace claim and REFUSES the
     publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none. Stamp-or-
     refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty: a row published with an empty
     namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read.
   - READ (stratum's record query plane, c2s half). The generated egress
     filter holds every row to the reader's own claim, and a row that fails
     the comparison HALTS THE JVM rather than failing the one call — the
     filter is the backstop behind the store's own query, so it firing means
     that query is broken.

 Bounded like every other string here. Not a (spec.query_field): the field
 exists to be the egress boundary, and making it a caller-supplied predicate
 is not what a boundary is.

 service token and carries no `act` claim at all — this field will be empty

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that sent
 this message" is one predicate asked of two record types.

 Empty is legitimate: a call with no authenticated Caller has none to read.

fields.name: agent_received
fields.description:
agent_received is the delivery ACK, written by the consuming agent after it
 processes this delivery. Unset at publish — this service never writes it.

message.name: AgentReceivedReceipt
message.description:
AgentReceivedReceipt is the delivery ACK — the agent (scotty, the mailbox
 service) took the record off the topic and processed it. Written by the
 consumer, never by the sender or by this service.

 It is the ACK, not a copy of it: there is one event here, not a delivery ACK
 plus a receipt derived from it.

fields.name: received_at_ms
fields.description:
received_at_ms is when the consuming agent completed processing — the same
 instant it commits its consumer-group offset, since committing before
 processing is exactly the discipline the queue semantics forbid.

fields.name: received_by
fields.description: received_by is the SPIFFE identity of the consuming agent instance.

fields.name: human_viewed
fields.description:
human_viewed is the separately-typed human signal. Unset at publish, and
 unset for as long as the person has not looked, which is the normal state
 of a delivered message.

message.name: HumanViewedReceipt
message.description:
HumanViewedReceipt fires when the actual person looked at the message. A
 distinct signal from AgentReceivedReceipt above: an agent can have ACKed a
 message hours before a human sees it, and business-hours-deferred
 presentation makes that gap the normal case rather than the exception.

 pushed a notification. That is the design already built for tickets
 (decisions/ticket-read-receipts-2026-08-30.md), relocated to where it
 belongs.

fields.name: viewed_at_ms
fields.description: viewed_at_ms is when the person actually looked.

fields.name: viewed_by
fields.description:
viewed_by is the principal subject of the person who looked. It is normally
 equal to Message.recipient — a delivery is viewed by its addressee — but it
 is stored rather than assumed, because a delegate viewing on someone's
 behalf is a real case and an inferred value could not tell the two apart.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by EXACT string equality against the
 caller's namespace claim (never the level-or-below containment the
 administrative namespace rule uses). It is the tenant half of the identity
 `recipient` carries the subject half of: that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant".

 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

   - WRITE (this record's publish path). eventbus's PublishHandler stamps
     this field from the publishing token's namespace claim and REFUSES the
     publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none. Stamp-or-
     refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty: a row published with an empty
     namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read.
   - READ (stratum's record query plane, c2s half). The generated egress
     filter holds every row to the reader's own claim, and a row that fails
     the comparison HALTS THE JVM rather than failing the one call — the
     filter is the backstop behind the store's own query, so it firing means
     that query is broken.

 Bounded like every other string here. Not a (spec.query_field): the field
 exists to be the egress boundary, and making it a caller-supplied predicate
 is not what a boundary is.

message.name: Message
message.description:
Message is ONE DELIVERY: one message, to one recipient.

 It is NOT one row per submission. A submission naming three recipients
 becomes three `Message` rows sharing a `message_id`, differing in
 `delivery_id` and `recipient`, each independently consumable and
 independently ACKable. See the fan-out note at the top of this file for why
 EventBus cannot do that split itself.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 MessageBus with topic ref messaging.MessageBus.stream. Do NOT hand-write that
 wrapper.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.description:
delivery_id is the record key: "<message_id>/<recipient>". One per
 (message, recipient) pair, which is what makes the N publishes of one
 submission N separately-keyed records rather than N copies of one.

 Derived rather than random ON PURPOSE: the value a caller would need to
 reconstruct to ACK a delivery is exactly (which message, for whom), so
 deriving it means an agent that knows both never has to have been told the
 id. It is also what makes the fan-out replay-safe — a retried submission
 regenerates the same delivery ids rather than a second set of rows.

fields.name: message_id
fields.description:
message_id groups the N deliveries of ONE submission. EQ-filterable,
 because "every delivery of the message I sent" is the question a sender
 asks, and it is the only way back from a delivery to its siblings.

fields.name: sender
fields.description:
sender is who sent it — the authenticated principal subject bound by the
 (spec.principal) field on SendMessageRequest below, never a caller-written
 string.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is THE recipient this delivery is for — one of `recipients`
 below, and the half of delivery_id that varies across the fan-out.

 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 eventbus stamps messaging's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. `sender` is the
 other candidate and is the wrong one: a mailbox read is "messages addressed
 to me", so the field the generated egress filter holds a caller's reads to
 must be the addressee.

 The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a SENDER cannot read their own
 sent messages through this record's c2s plane, because only one field may
 carry (spec.store_principal) and this is it. Sent-items is a mailbox
 concern and the mailbox service is Phase 1 item 8, undesigned; inventing a
 second read path for it here would be inventing that service's shape.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: recipients
fields.description:
recipients is the full To: line — every recipient of the submission, the
 SAME list on all N deliveries. `recipient` above says which one this row is
 for; this says who else got it.

 Carrying it is not redundancy. Without it a recipient cannot see who else
 was addressed, which is information the sender chose to disclose by
 addressing them together — the same reason a To: header exists and a Bcc:
 one does not. (This file models no Bcc; nothing has asked for one.)

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_recipients' ceiling above.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: subject is the message's subject line.

fields.name: text
fields.description: text is the message body. Free text, and nothing parses it — see ticket_id.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
ticket_id OPTIONALLY references the ticket this message pertains to.

 A dedicated field, never a value embedded in `text`. Routing and status
 display have to associate a message with its ticket to act, and the
 standing rule is that anything that must be parsed to be acted on should

fields.name: sent_at_ms

types.name: MessagingConfigState
types.description:
MessagingConfigState is the state boundary for messaging service configuration.
 Auto-injected by tacplus from (spec.grpc_config) annotation.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_recipients
fields.description:
max_recipients bounds the recipient fan-out of ONE submission, and it is a
 resource limit on the service, not a business rule: N recipients means N
 publishes, so an unbounded list is an unbounded amount of work bought with
 one RPC. Held in config rather than as a constant for the same reason
 tasks.Config.max_open_tasks is — changing it in kernel must change
 behaviour with no redeploy.

 It must not exceed SendMessageRequest.recipients' assert_max_size (256):
 the two describe the same cap and the generated request validation is the
 hard edge, so a config above it could never take effect.

types.name: SendMessageRequest

fields.name: sender
fields.description:
sender is (spec.principal): the generated wrapper resolves the
 authenticated caller's subject and stamps it when the field is empty,
 accepts it when it matches, and refuses with INVALID_ARGUMENT when it
 differs. A caller therefore cannot send AS someone else, and the handler
 does not check — there is nothing left to check.

fields.name: recipients
fields.description:
recipients is who the message is for. Every entry becomes its own delivery
 and its own publish.

 Bounded at 256 here and at Config.max_recipients (default 64) at runtime;
 this is the hard edge and that is the tunable one, which is why the config
 field may not exceed this number.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
ticket_id optionally associates this message with a ticket. See
 Message.ticket_id — a field, never parsed out of `text`.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is (spec.namespace): the ingest twin of Message.namespace's
 (spec.store_namespace), and the WRITE half of the namespace paired control.
 The generated wrapper resolves the caller's verified namespace claim and
   - stamps it when this field is empty,
   - accepts it when it matches,
   - REFUSES with INVALID_ARGUMENT when it differs.
 An unauthenticated caller on a namespace-bearing RPC is UNAUTHENTICATED.

 So a caller cannot address a send into another tenant, and the refusal
 happens before the handler runs. That is the write-side behaviour; the
 read-side backstop crashes instead, and the difference is deliberate — see
 Message.namespace.

types.name: SendMessageResponse

fields.name: message_id
fields.description: message_id groups the deliveries this call produced.

fields.name: delivery_ids
fields.description:
delivery_ids is one id per recipient, in the order the recipients were
 given, and its LENGTH is the fan-out count. Returning them rather than just
 the message_id is what lets a caller (or a test) assert that N recipients
 produced N separately-keyed deliveries without reading the topic.

rpcs.description:
SendMessage submits one message and fans it out to its recipients.

 Send, not Submit: the RPC verb registry is CLOSED
 (tacplus/pkg/internal/common/verbs/registry.json) and Submit is not in it,
 with no synonym mapping. Send is the registered verb for point-to-point
 delivery, and its boundary note — "NOT Publish; one intended recipient or
 channel endpoint" — is exactly right here: the recipients are named
 parties, and the fan-out across them is the N point-to-point deliveries
 this RPC produces. Publish would name the OTHER axis, the topic one, which
 is EventBus's and not this RPC's. The decision doc's "(e.g. `Submit`)" was
 an illustration, not a name.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Publish; one intended recipient or channel endpoint.
NOT Send; fan-out to topic subscribers.

rpcs.verb_definition: Open a long-lived domain stream that is not a collection WATCH envelope.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Watch; use Watch only for generated collection snapshot/upsert/delete streams.
NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

 client connections — same posture as stratum — so there is no direct-publish
 path to fall back to.

types.name: AuthorizeRequest
types.description: AuthorizeRequest initiates an OAuth2 flow.

fields.name: provider_index
fields.description: provider_index selects which configured provider to use.

fields.name: callback_url
fields.description:
callback_url is where the user is sent after successful authentication.
 This is the originating microservice's URL (e.g. "https://sentinel:9000/").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: session_id
fields.description:
session_id is set when the OAuth flow was initiated by a CLI client.
 If present, the callback handler writes the minted token to OAuthState
 for delivery to the matching bidi stream.

types.name: AuthorizeResponse
types.description: AuthorizeResponse contains the IDP redirect URL.

fields.name: redirect_url
fields.description: redirect_url is the full OAuth2 authorization URL to redirect the user to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

types.name: CallbackRequest
types.description: CallbackRequest handles the OAuth2 authorization code callback.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the authorization code from the IDP.

fields.name: state
fields.description: state is the anti-CSRF state parameter.

types.name: CallbackResponse
types.description: CallbackResponse contains the minted tokens and the callback destination.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.description: refresh_token is the long-lived refresh token signed by kernel.

fields.name: access_token
fields.description: access_token is the short-lived access token for immediate use.

fields.name: callback_url
fields.description: callback_url is the original URL to redirect the user back to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: access_token_expires_in
fields.description: access_token_expires_in is the access token lifetime in seconds.

fields.name: refresh_token_expires_in
fields.description: refresh_token_expires_in is the refresh token lifetime in seconds.

types.name: ClaimMatcher
types.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

types.name: ClusterOAuthConfig
types.description:
ClusterOAuthConfig holds cluster-level shared IDP configuration.
 Configured once by a cluster admin; shared across all tenants.
 Delivered to the oauth service alongside per-tenant OAuthTenantConfig slices.

message.name: ClusterOAuthProvider
message.description:

 to all tenants. Tenants route users from these IDPs via ClaimMatcher entries.

fields.name: client_id

fields.description: client_secret is the sensitive OAuth app secret; supplied by cluster admin.

fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this cluster IDP.

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables OAuth2 authentication.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
scopes are the default OAuth2 scopes requested from all providers.
 If empty, defaults to ["openid", "profile", "email"].

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers is the list of OAuth2 identity provider configurations.

types.name: SessionRequest

fields.name: offline_access
fields.description:
offline_access requests an Offline Token (OT) for CLI/daemon sessions.

 local daemon; access and service tokens remain derived, short-lived, and
 memory-only.

types.description: SessionResponse is sent by the server on the bidi stream.

fields.name: token

 auth flow), or when the service proactively refreshes in daemon mode.

fields.name: error
fields.description: error signals a terminal error (session timeout, auth failure, etc.).

types.name: Config
types.description:
OperatorConfig is the top-level operator configuration.

 Lifecycle:
   1. operator init ca                   — generate root CA → crypto.yaml
   2. operator init cluster --ca <path>  — generate cluster PKI + write operator.yaml
   3. operator                           — run (IN_CLUSTER) or generate charts (GENERATE_ONLY)

 When deployed to Kubernetes:
   operator.yaml  → ConfigMap  (schematic-operator-config)
   crypto.yaml    → Secret     (schematic-operator-crypto)
 Both are mounted and merged by the operator at startup.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: How the operator runs.

enum_values.name: IN_CLUSTER
enum_values.description:
IN_CLUSTER is the default: the operator runs inside Kubernetes and
 continuously reconciles the desired cluster state by managing Helm releases.
 gateway_nodes is automatically set to the number of schedulable nodes.

enum_values.name: GENERATE_ONLY
enum_values.description:
GENERATE_ONLY: one-shot CLI mode. Generates Helm charts, writes them to
 output_dir, and exits. Does not communicate with the Kubernetes API.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description: Public FQDN for the cluster (e.g. "api.example.com").

fields.name: port
fields.description: HTTPS gateway port. Default 443 for production; 8443 for local testing.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Kubernetes namespace to deploy all schematic services into.

fields.name: topology
fields.description: Service replica topology.

message.name: Topology
message.description:
Topology declares the desired replica count for each service.

 gateway_nodes is special: when set to 0 and mode = IN_CLUSTER, the operator
 automatically sets it to the number of schedulable Kubernetes nodes at each
 reconciliation cycle (one gateway per node). When mode = GENERATE_ONLY,
 gateway_nodes must be set explicitly.

fields.name: gateway_nodes
fields.description:
Set to 0 to auto-derive from schedulable node count (IN_CLUSTER only).
 When enabled proxy services (anthropic, openai, gitlab, github) also
 scale to one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: oauth_nodes
fields.description: oauth_nodes is used when optional_services.oauth = true (default).

fields.name: saml_nodes
fields.description: saml_nodes is used when optional_services.saml = true.

fields.name: kmaker_nodes
fields.description:
kmaker_nodes is the number of bootstrap certificate authority replicas.
 Kernel instances contact kmaker with Kubernetes projected service account
 tokens to obtain kernel certificates before kernel itself is available.

fields.name: echo_nodes
fields.description:
echo_nodes is used when optional_services.echo = true.
 Defaults to 1 rather than 3: the sample service is stateless and exists to
 be poked at, so a second replica proves nothing and costs a pod.

fields.name: app_services
fields.description:
app_services declares replica counts for services that are NOT part of the
 platform: an application's own services, defined in the application's proto
 repo and merged into the build.

 Every field above is a PLATFORM service with a fixed field number. That is
 fine for the platform, whose service set is what "the platform" means — but
 it made the platform unable to host anything else. An application could not
 declare a service without editing this file, and proto3 gives no way to add
 a field to a message from another repo, so "schematic is reusable" was not
 true: echo, a sample service, had to take field 17 here to be deployable.

 Keyed by service name, so an app adds a service by naming it in its own
 config and this file never changes. Presence with a count > 0 IS the
 enablement — an app service needs no parallel optional_services flag.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
TLS configuration — letsencrypt or custom CA.
 Validation: if tls.letsencrypt = false, tls.ca must be set.

message.name: TLSConfig
message.description:
TLSConfig controls how edge-facing TLS certificates are obtained.
 When letsencrypt = true, the operator deploys one letsencrypt service replica.

fields.name: letsencrypt
fields.description:
When true, Let's Encrypt is used for edge TLS and one letsencrypt service
 replica is deployed. The gateway must be reachable on port 443 from the
 public internet.
 When false, ca must be populated with a valid CA chain.

fields.name: ca
fields.description:
Custom CA chain for edge TLS certificates.
 Required when letsencrypt = false. Ignored when letsencrypt = true.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: pki
fields.description: PKI material. Loaded from crypto.yaml and merged at runtime.

message.name: PKI
message.description:
PKI holds all PKI material for the cluster.

 root_ca is generated once per organization via 'operator init ca'.
 All other fields are generated per-cluster via 'operator init cluster'.
 PKI material lives in crypto.yaml and is merged into OperatorConfig at
 load time. The crypto.yaml file must be kept secret.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description: Shared root CA across all clusters (cert + private key).

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description: Cluster intermediate CA, signed by root_ca.

fields.name: node_tls
fields.description: Per-node TLS server certificates (one per kernel/sentinel replica).

fields.name: node_signing_ca
fields.description: Per-node signing CAs for token issuance (one per kernel replica).

fields.name: edge_tls
fields.description:
Edge TLS certificates for gateway and oauth.
 Not used when tls.letsencrypt = true.

fields.name: edge_signing_ca
fields.description: Edge signing CAs.

fields.name: kmaker_signing_ca
fields.description:
Kmaker signing CA, signed by cluster_ca and constrained to issue only
 kernel bootstrap leaf certificates.

fields.name: optional_services
fields.description: Optional add-on services.

message.name: OptionalServices
message.description: OptionalServices controls which optional services are enabled.

fields.name: saml
fields.description:
SAML identity provider bridge — saml_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default.

fields.name: oauth
fields.description:
OAuth2/OIDC broker — oauth_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Enabled by default.

fields.name: keycloak
fields.description:
Keycloak IDP — production identity provider.
 Replaces mockidp. Enabled by default.

fields.name: echo
fields.description:
Echo sample service — echo_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default: it is a diagnostic/reference service, not something a
 production cluster should carry.

fields.name: output_dir
fields.description:
Filesystem path where generated Helm charts are written.
 Only used in GENERATE_ONLY mode. Default: "charts".

fields.name: web_root
fields.description:
Filesystem path to the web UI build, mounted read-only into gateway.
 Leave empty to use the gateway's embedded webapp.

fields.name: patch
fields.description:
patch is the service image patch number to deploy.
 When 0 (default), the operator auto-tracks the latest patch and polls the
 registry for upgrades (every hour for stable, every 60s for dev builds).
 When set, the operator pins to that exact patch and does no polling.

fields.name: dev
fields.description:
dev selects dev builds when true, stable builds when false (default).
 Affects both the image tag suffix and the polling interval.

fields.name: gitlab_registry_token
fields.description:
gitlab_registry_token is an OAuth2 personal access token (read_registry scope)
 used to pull images from registry.gitlab.com. When set, the operator creates a
 "gitlab-registry" docker-registry Secret in the schematic namespace as part of
 the generated Helm chart. Keep this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
SPIFFE trust-domain prefix for identity URIs. Every workload identity is
 formed as `spiffe://${spiffe_prefix}/${service_name}` — this powers token
 subject claims, mTLS URI SANs, and (post-B-end-state) SPIFFE-aware client
 cert verification. Operator propagates this value to kernel's bootstrap
 AND to every service configmap so all components agree on the trust
 domain at boot, without a runtime SCS round-trip.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, loaded from
 operator.yaml. The operator renders them into kernel's Helm-deployed config
 (kernel.Config.root_cred_pairs); kernel installs them into the root
 namespace's TenantConfig so they can provision tenants via TenantAdmin.
 Ordinary C2S CredPairs at the root namespace; only public halves are carried.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

fields.name: cluster_oauth
fields.description:
cluster_oauth holds shared (cluster-level) IDP providers — Google, GitHub, etc.
 Configured once by a cluster admin. Delivered to the oauth service for
 initial token validation; tenant routing happens via ClaimMatcher entries
 in each tenant's OAuthTenantConfig.

message.name: ClusterOAuthConfig
message.description:
ClusterOAuthConfig holds cluster-level shared IDP configuration.
 Configured once by a cluster admin; shared across all tenants.
 Delivered to the oauth service alongside per-tenant OAuthTenantConfig slices.

message.name: ClusterOAuthProvider
message.description:
ClusterOAuthProvider describes a shared IDP (e.g. Google, GitHub) available
 to all tenants. Tenants route users from these IDPs via ClaimMatcher entries.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer (e.g. "https://accounts.google.com").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the shared OAuth app client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the sensitive OAuth app secret; supplied by cluster admin.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this cluster IDP.

fields.name: kmaker
fields.description:
kmaker owns cluster bootstrap certificate signing for kernel. Operator
 renders this into kmaker's mounted runtime config and owns the Secret that
 carries kmaker.Config.signing_ca.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is rendered by operator and mounted into kmaker at startup.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description: cluster_name is the logical Schematic cluster this kmaker signs for.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for kmaker.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
cluster_ca
fields.description: cluster_ca holds trust anchors that kernel nodes should trust.

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.
 The private key is present in the mounted kmaker config and must be backed
 by a Kubernetes Secret owned by operator.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
spiffe_prefix is the deployment prefix for kernel SPIFFE URI SANs.
 Certificates minted here receive spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/kernel.

fields.name: token_audience
fields.description: token_audience is the required Kubernetes TokenReview audience.

fields.name: kernel_service_accounts
fields.description:
kernel_service_accounts are Kubernetes service accounts allowed to request
 kernel certificates. Empty means namespace=schematic, name=kernel.

fields.name: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds caps issued kernel certificate lifetimes.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the optional serving certificate for kmaker's own gRPC listener.
 When unset, kmaker starts without transport TLS for local/dev only.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kmaker's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kmaker.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

fields.name: llm_credential
fields.description:
llm_credential is a shared secret (e.g. an Anthropic API key) fanned out
 into the generated bootstrap config of every app service named in
 llm_credential_services, under the YAML key "llm_credential" — so it is
 configured once here rather than duplicated per app service. The
 receiving app service's own Config must declare a matching field. Keep
 this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: llm_credential_services
fields.description:
llm_credential_services names the app services (by AppServiceNames key)
 that should receive llm_credential in their generated bootstrap config.
