 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: pki
fields.description: PKI material. Loaded from crypto.yaml and merged at runtime.

message.name: PKI
message.description:
PKI holds all PKI material for the cluster.

 root_ca is generated once per organization via 'operator init ca'.
 All other fields are generated per-cluster via 'operator init cluster'.
 PKI material lives in crypto.yaml and is merged into OperatorConfig at
 load time. The crypto.yaml file must be kept secret.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description: Shared root CA across all clusters (cert + private key).

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description: Cluster intermediate CA, signed by root_ca.

fields.name: node_tls
fields.description: Per-node TLS server certificates (one per kernel/sentinel replica).

fields.name: node_signing_ca
fields.description: Per-node signing CAs for token issuance (one per kernel replica).

fields.name: edge_tls
fields.description:
Edge TLS certificates for gateway and oauth.
 Not used when tls.letsencrypt = true.

fields.name: edge_signing_ca
fields.description: Edge signing CAs.

fields.name: kmaker_signing_ca
fields.description:
Kmaker signing CA, signed by cluster_ca and constrained to issue only
 kernel bootstrap leaf certificates.

fields.name: optional_services
fields.description: Optional add-on services.

message.name: OptionalServices
message.description: OptionalServices controls which optional services are enabled.

fields.name: saml
fields.description:
SAML identity provider bridge — saml_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default.

fields.name: oauth
fields.description:
OAuth2/OIDC broker — oauth_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Enabled by default.

fields.name: keycloak
fields.description:
Keycloak IDP — production identity provider.
 Replaces mockidp. Enabled by default.

fields.name: echo
fields.description:
Echo sample service — echo_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default: it is a diagnostic/reference service, not something a
 production cluster should carry.

fields.name: output_dir
fields.description:
Filesystem path where generated Helm charts are written.
 Only used in GENERATE_ONLY mode. Default: "charts".

fields.name: web_root
fields.description:
Filesystem path to the web UI build, mounted read-only into gateway.
 Leave empty to use the gateway's embedded webapp.

fields.name: patch
fields.description:
patch is the service image patch number to deploy.
 When 0 (default), the operator auto-tracks the latest patch and polls the
 registry for upgrades (every hour for stable, every 60s for dev builds).
 When set, the operator pins to that exact patch and does no polling.

fields.name: dev
fields.description:
dev selects dev builds when true, stable builds when false (default).
 Affects both the image tag suffix and the polling interval.

fields.name: gitlab_registry_token
fields.description:
gitlab_registry_token is an OAuth2 personal access token (read_registry scope)
 used to pull images from registry.gitlab.com. When set, the operator creates a
 "gitlab-registry" docker-registry Secret in the schematic namespace as part of
 the generated Helm chart. Keep this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
SPIFFE trust-domain prefix for identity URIs. Every workload identity is
 formed as `spiffe://${spiffe_prefix}/${service_name}` — this powers token
 subject claims, mTLS URI SANs, and (post-B-end-state) SPIFFE-aware client
 cert verification. Operator propagates this value to kernel's bootstrap
 AND to every service configmap so all components agree on the trust
 domain at boot, without a runtime SCS round-trip.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, loaded from
 operator.yaml. The operator renders them into kernel's Helm-deployed config
 (kernel.Config.root_cred_pairs); kernel installs them into the root
 namespace's TenantConfig so they can provision tenants via TenantAdmin.
 Ordinary C2S CredPairs at the root namespace; only public halves are carried.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

fields.name: cluster_oauth
fields.description:
cluster_oauth holds shared (cluster-level) IDP providers — Google, GitHub, etc.
 Configured once by a cluster admin. Delivered to the oauth service for
 initial token validation; tenant routing happens via ClaimMatcher entries
 in each tenant's OAuthTenantConfig.

message.name: ClusterOAuthConfig
message.description:
ClusterOAuthConfig holds cluster-level shared IDP configuration.
 Configured once by a cluster admin; shared across all tenants.
 Delivered to the oauth service alongside per-tenant OAuthTenantConfig slices.

message.name: ClusterOAuthProvider
message.description:
ClusterOAuthProvider describes a shared IDP (e.g. Google, GitHub) available
 to all tenants. Tenants route users from these IDPs via ClaimMatcher entries.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer (e.g. "https://accounts.google.com").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the shared OAuth app client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the sensitive OAuth app secret; supplied by cluster admin.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this cluster IDP.

fields.name: kmaker
fields.description:
kmaker owns cluster bootstrap certificate signing for kernel. Operator
 renders this into kmaker's mounted runtime config and owns the Secret that
 carries kmaker.Config.signing_ca.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is rendered by operator and mounted into kmaker at startup.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description: cluster_name is the logical Schematic cluster this kmaker signs for.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for kmaker.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
cluster_ca
fields.description: cluster_ca holds trust anchors that kernel nodes should trust.

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.
 The private key is present in the mounted kmaker config and must be backed
 by a Kubernetes Secret owned by operator.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
spiffe_prefix is the deployment prefix for kernel SPIFFE URI SANs.
 Certificates minted here receive spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/kernel.

fields.name: token_audience
fields.description: token_audience is the required Kubernetes TokenReview audience.

fields.name: kernel_service_accounts
fields.description:
kernel_service_accounts are Kubernetes service accounts allowed to request
 kernel certificates. Empty means namespace=schematic, name=kernel.

fields.name: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds caps issued kernel certificate lifetimes.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the optional serving certificate for kmaker's own gRPC listener.
 When unset, kmaker starts without transport TLS for local/dev only.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kmaker's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kmaker.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

fields.name: llm_credential
fields.description:
llm_credential is a shared secret (e.g. an Anthropic API key) fanned out
 into the generated bootstrap config of every app service named in
 llm_credential_services, under the YAML key "llm_credential" — so it is
 configured once here rather than duplicated per app service. The
 receiving app service's own Config must declare a matching field. Keep
 this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: llm_credential_services
fields.description:
llm_credential_services names the app services (by AppServiceNames key)
 that should receive llm_credential in their generated bootstrap config.

types.name: Topology
types.description:
Topology declares the desired replica count for each service.

 gateway_nodes is special: when set to 0 and mode = IN_CLUSTER, the operator
 automatically sets it to the number of schedulable Kubernetes nodes at each
 reconciliation cycle (one gateway per node). When mode = GENERATE_ONLY,
 gateway_nodes must be set explicitly.

fields.name: gateway_nodes
fields.description:
Set to 0 to auto-derive from schedulable node count (IN_CLUSTER only).
 When enabled proxy services (anthropic, openai, gitlab, github) also
 scale to one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: oauth_nodes
fields.description: oauth_nodes is used when optional_services.oauth = true (default).

fields.name: saml_nodes
fields.description: saml_nodes is used when optional_services.saml = true.

fields.name: kmaker_nodes
fields.description:
kmaker_nodes is the number of bootstrap certificate authority replicas.
 Kernel instances contact kmaker with Kubernetes projected service account
 tokens to obtain kernel certificates before kernel itself is available.

fields.name: echo_nodes
fields.description:
echo_nodes is used when optional_services.echo = true.
 Defaults to 1 rather than 3: the sample service is stateless and exists to
 be poked at, so a second replica proves nothing and costs a pod.

fields.name: app_services
fields.description:
app_services declares replica counts for services that are NOT part of the
 platform: an application's own services, defined in the application's proto
 repo and merged into the build.

 Every field above is a PLATFORM service with a fixed field number. That is
 fine for the platform, whose service set is what "the platform" means — but
 it made the platform unable to host anything else. An application could not
 declare a service without editing this file, and proto3 gives no way to add
 a field to a message from another repo, so "schematic is reusable" was not
 true: echo, a sample service, had to take field 17 here to be deployable.

 Keyed by service name, so an app adds a service by naming it in its own
 config and this file never changes. Presence with a count > 0 IS the
 enablement — an app service needs no parallel optional_services flag.

values.name: GENERATE_ONLY
values.description:
GENERATE_ONLY: one-shot CLI mode. Generates Helm charts, writes them to
 output_dir, and exits. Does not communicate with the Kubernetes API.

{
  "name": "Config",

      "required": true,

      ],

          "bool_value": true,
          "source": "annotation"
        },
        {

          "target": "field",
          "value_kind": "enum",
          "enum_value": "URL_SCHEME_HTTPS",
          "source": "annotation"
        },
        {
          "rule": "default_max_size",
          "target": "field",
          "value_kind": "int",
          "int_value": 32768,
          "defaulted": true,
          "unit": "bytes",
          "source": "default_bound"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "base_url",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "base_url is the public HTTPS base URL of this service.\n Used to construct ACS, SSO, SLO, and metadata endpoint URLs.\n Example: \"https://saml.example.com\"",
      "required": true,

entity_id is the globally unique URI that identifies this SAML entity.
 It appears in the EntityDescriptor and in every assertion we issue.
 Example: "https://saml.example.com/saml"

types.name: GetDescriptorRequest
types.description: GetDescriptorRequest asks for a named IDP's EntityDescriptor.

fields.name: idp_name
fields.description: idp_name matches the name field of an IdpConfig.

types.name: GetDescriptorResponse
types.description: GetDescriptorResponse returns the parsed IDP descriptor fields.

fields.name: entity_descriptor
fields.description: entity_descriptor is the parsed EntityDescriptor fields.

message.name: SamlEntityDescriptor
message.description:
SamlEntityDescriptor represents a SAML 2.0 EntityDescriptor metadata document.
 Used both to describe our own endpoints (SP or IDP role) and to parse external
 IDP metadata fetched during federation setup.

 Parallel to OIDC's /.well-known/openid-configuration discovery document.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: EntityId is the globally unique identifier for this SAML entity (a URI)

fields.name: signing_cert
fields.description:
SigningCert is the X.509 certificate whose private key signs assertions or
 AuthnRequests for this entity. Embedded as base64 DER in metadata XML.
 For IDP role: the key that signs assertions we issue.
 For SP role: the key that signs AuthnRequests we send (optional).

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: sso_services
fields.description:
SsoServices lists SingleSignOnService endpoints (IDP role only).
 External SPs use these URLs to send AuthnRequests.

message.name: SamlEndpoint
message.description:
SamlEndpoint describes a single SAML protocol endpoint with its binding and URL.
 Used in EntityDescriptor metadata to advertise service locations.

fields.name: binding
fields.description: Binding is the SamlBinding URI for this endpoint

fields.name: location
fields.description: Location is the endpoint URL

fields.name: index
fields.description:
Index is the endpoint index for indexed endpoints (e.g. AssertionConsumerService).
 Zero-valued for non-indexed endpoints such as SingleSignOnService.

fields.name: acs_urls
fields.description:
AcsUrls lists AssertionConsumerService endpoints (SP role only).
 IDPs POST SAMLResponses to these URLs.

fields.name: slo_services
fields.description: SloServices lists SingleLogoutService endpoints for both IDP and SP roles.

fields.name: want_authn_requests_signed
fields.description:
WantAuthnRequestsSigned indicates (IDP role) whether this IDP requires
 incoming AuthnRequests to be signed.

fields.name: authn_requests_signed
fields.description:
AuthnRequestsSigned indicates (SP role) whether this SP will sign its
 outgoing AuthnRequests.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this IDP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Okta", "Azure AD").

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the IDP's SAML entity ID (must match the Issuer element).

fields.name: metadata_url
fields.description:
metadata_url is the URL of the IDP's SAML EntityDescriptor XML.
 When set, the signing cert is fetched from this URL at startup.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: signing_cert_pem
fields.description:
signing_cert_pem is a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate used to verify
 assertion signatures from this IDP. If metadata_url is set, this is
 derived from the metadata. At least one of these must be provided.

fields.name: acs_path
fields.description:
acs_path is the relative path of our ACS endpoint for this IDP.
 Example: "/saml/acs/okta"
 Defaults to "/saml/acs" if empty.

fields.name: attribute_map
fields.description:
attribute_map maps IDP attribute names to Schematic claim names.
 Keys are SAML attribute names (e.g. "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress").
 Values are the Schematic claim names to pass to kernel (e.g. "email").
 If the "email" key is absent after mapping, the NameID is used as the subject.

fields.name: domains
fields.description: domains maps email domains to this IDP. Used for IDP selection hints.

types.name: ListSPsRequest
types.description: ListSPsRequest (empty — returns all enabled SPs).

types.name: ListSPsResponse
types.description: ListSPsResponse contains public SP information.

message.name: SpInfo
message.description: SpInfo is the public-facing information about a configured outbound SP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the display name.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the SP's SAML entity ID.

fields.name: sp_index
fields.description: sp_index identifies this SP in subsequent MintAssertion calls.

types.name: MapEmpty
MetadataRequest
types.description: MetadataRequest (empty — the service infers which entity descriptor to serve).

types.name: MetadataResponse
types.description: MetadataResponse contains the EntityDescriptor XML.

fields.name: xml
fields.description: xml is the EntityDescriptor XML document (UTF-8 encoded).

types.name: MintAssertionRequest
types.description: MintAssertionRequest asks SAML to issue a SAML assertion for a named SP.

fields.name: sp_index
fields.description: sp_index selects which configured SP to target.

fields.name: in_response_to
fields.description:
in_response_to is the ID of the SP's AuthnRequest, if SP-initiated.
 Empty for IDP-initiated flows.

types.name: MintAssertionResponse
types.description: MintAssertionResponse contains the issued SAML assertion.

fields.name: saml_response
fields.description:
saml_response is the base64-encoded signed <samlp:Response> XML.
 The caller should POST this to acs_url as the SAMLResponse form field.

fields.name: acs_url
fields.description: acs_url is the SP's AssertionConsumerService URL to POST to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: relay_state
fields.description:
relay_state is the relay_state to include in the POST (typically empty
 for IDP-initiated flows).

types.name: SamlAuthorizeRequest
types.description: SamlAuthorizeRequest initiates an SP-initiated SAML flow.

fields.name: idp_index
fields.description: idp_index selects which configured IDP to use.

fields.name: relay_state
fields.description: relay_state is the callback state to restore after authentication.

types.name: SamlAuthorizeResponse
types.description: SamlAuthorizeResponse contains the IDP redirect URL.

fields.name: redirect_url
fields.description: redirect_url is the full IDP SSO URL with embedded AuthnRequest.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

claim_text is the claim as stated ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Prose, and it

types.name: BusinessHours
types.description:
BusinessHours is when this person is taken to be working. It is KNOWLEDGE in
 §1's sense — "what was learned" — not a setting, and nothing in the API lets
 a caller author it.

 TWO LAYERS, and `source` says which one produced the values in this message:

   PRIOR    — an industry+geography default, which is what a brand-new record
              with zero history has. It is a guess, and it is marked as one.
   OBSERVED — refined from the person's own recorded activity once there is
              enough of it to say anything.

 Only the PRIOR layer is WRITTEN today. The observed layer is shape here and
 nothing else, deliberately: the naive refinement (widen the window to cover
 every hour a read was seen at) would defeat the thing the deferral exists to
 protect — one 11pm read would make 11pm business hours. That is a question
 about what evidence of "working" means, not an implementation detail, and it
 is written up rather than guessed. See
 loopers/schematic/decisions/business-hours-inferred-not-configured.md.

 SINGLE CONCEPT. This is the same "business hours" feature-ideas.md's loop
 cadence needs ("looped more frequently Mon-Fri during business hours"). Do
 not add a second notion of it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_PRIOR
enum_values.description: PRIOR: an industry+geography default. No activity data went into it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_OBSERVED
enum_values.description: OBSERVED: refined from this person's own recorded activity.

fields.name: start_of_day_minutes
fields.description:
Minutes past LOCAL midnight, start < end. Nothing validates these on the
 way in because nothing writes them but the service itself; a stored row
 that does not describe a usable window is ignored on the read path in
 favour of the prior, rather than being repaired in place.

fields.name: working_days
fields.description:
The days that are working days. Repeated rather than a mask so the value
 reads as itself in a dump. An empty set is not a usable window, and is
 treated the same way an inverted start/end is — see above.

fields.name: utc_offset_minutes
fields.description:
utc_offset_minutes is the GEOGRAPHY half of the prior, in the crudest form
 that is still correct for the thing it is used for: a fixed offset, no
 DST and no tz database. A Texas crew reading a thread at 23:03 local is
 23:03 whether or not the offset moved an hour in March, and the label the
 deferral produces is a date-and-time, not an instant anyone schedules
 against. A real tz identifier is future work, noted in the decision doc.

fields.name: observed_event_count
fields.description:
observed_event_count is how much activity the OBSERVED layer was refined
 from, and is 0 while source is PRIOR. It is on the message so that "how
 confident is this" is answerable from the row rather than from a guess
 about how old it is.

types.name: CollectionQuery
Config
types.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_open_tickets
fields.description:
max_open_tickets bounds how many tickets may be open at once, and exists
 for the same reason tasks.Config.max_open_tasks does: to give the service a
 rule that comes from CONFIG rather than from code, so changing it in kernel
 changes behaviour with no redeploy.

 NOT a written policy. §2 is explicit that "an entitlement makes an action
 impossible, a written policy makes it inadvisable" — a config bound that
 hard-fails a create is neither, it is a resource limit on the service. No
 business rule may be expressed here.

fields.name: max_chain_hops
fields.description:
max_chain_hops is the CIRCUIT BREAKER on AI-mediated negotiation, and it is
 a HOP COUNT, not a duration. A chain's hop count is the number of turns
 taken in it — every Ticket, TicketAdvice and TicketComment sharing a
 chain_id — and when it reaches this bound Scotty stops adding its own
 judgement to that chain. Jody, 2026-08-30: "it escalates to the human at
 the same level. It just keeps LLMs from getting stuck in a loop."

 Config for the same reason max_open_tickets is: it is a resource-shaped
 bound on the service, changeable in kernel with no redeploy, and it is NOT
 a written policy — nothing here decides anything about a request.

 A wall-clock TTL was proposed for this and explicitly discarded; see
 loopers/schematic/decisions/ticket-ttl-hop-count-circuit-breaker-2026-08-30.md.

fields.name: llm_credential
fields.description:
llm_credential is the Anthropic API key, fanned out by operator into this
 service's generated bootstrap config under the YAML key "llm_credential"
 (see platform/proto/services/operator.proto's Config.llm_credential and
 .llm_credential_services, and operator.yaml's own llm_credential_services
 list, which must include "scotty" for the fan-out to reach here). Field
 name and type must match what operator's bootstrap.go writes, or the
 service fails to unmarshal its own generated config.

fields.description:
credential_type carries the RELIABILITY CLASS of the claim, which
 feature-ideas.md calls out as the reason one field would not do: a state
 licence number and a company's own judgement are "different reliability
 classes of fact and worth treating that way".

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_STATE_LICENSE
enum_values.description:
A state occupational licence (electrical, plumbing) — tied to permitting
 and code inspection.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_INDUSTRY_CERT
enum_values.description:
An industry certification (AWS, NCCER) — how welding and heavy equipment
 operation are actually governed.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_COMPANY_ASSERTED
enum_values.description:
The company's own judgement about autonomy/experience, with no papers
 behind it.

fields.name: trade
fields.description:
trade is the trade the credential is in (welder, electrician, operator).
 Prose for now, deliberately: §5 "prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known", and the trade taxonomy is not settled. It must never be parsed —
 "if anything has to parse it to act on it, it should have been a field".

fields.name: issuing_body
fields.description: issuing_body is empty for COMPANY_ASSERTED, which has no issuer.

fields.name: credential_number
fields.description:
credential_number is the licence/certificate number. Empty for
 COMPANY_ASSERTED for the same reason.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description:
expires_at_ms is 0 for a credential that does not expire. Credential
 expiry tracking is listed in §9 as its own typed capability ("a ticket that
 lapses") and is NOT built here — this field is the fact, not the mechanism.

fields.name: verified_by_human_id
fields.description:
verified_by_human_id is who stood behind the claim. For COMPANY_ASSERTED it
 is the whole of the credential's authority, which is why it is a Human id
 rather than a free-text name.

message.name: IdentityLink
message.description: IdentityLink binds one external auth identity to this Human.

fields.name: subject
fields.description:
subject is the provider's own subject claim. It is opaque and must never be
 parsed for meaning.

types.name: CreateHumanResponse

message.name: Human
message.description:
Human is the durable identity record.

 The load-bearing principle, from architecture-sketch.md §4 and reaffirmed by
 the design record: "the Human record is the durable source of truth;
 OAuth/SAML claims are ephemeral proof of 'this session is really this
 person', never themselves the store of who someone is or what they're
 allowed to do."

 DELIBERATELY ABSENT — every one of these appears in the architecture sketch's
 draft and is contradicted or unsettled by the later design record:
   - org_unit_id / reports_through: §2 "Hierarchy" says these as single
     strings "do not express this", because a chain can differ per job.
   - rule_auth_level: "rule" was retired in favour of "written policy", and
     the sketch derived this field FROM org_unit_id, which is the field above.
   - personal_scotty_id: agent-instance binding is not settled as a type.
 See the schematic looper's decisions/human-hierarchy-fields-omitted-not-invented.md
 (pre-split snoopy history, not in this repo).

 Human carries NO (spec.store_principal). On tasks.Task that option filters
 every read down to the creating caller — correct for a personal task list and
 wrong here, because a Human record exists precisely to be read by people
 other than whoever typed it in. Read authorization for Human is entitlement
 work and is not done; see the schematic looper's
 decisions/scotty-read-authorization-not-wired.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

fields.name: human_id
fields.description:
human_id is the collection key: indexed, required, non-empty — the
 state-collection convention.

fields.name: email
fields.description:
email and phone are AUTHORED facts in the §1 sense — "a phone number, a
 written policy, a stated deadline — are not distilled from anything" — so a
 write to either has to leave an artifact, which requires_artifact_on_write
 above enforces.

 Not (spec.assert_email): an empty string is a legitimate value here (an
 unskilled labourer who rolls up through someone else may have no address on
 file at all), and assert_email would reject it.

fields.name: skill
fields.description:
skill is the SETTLED axis. feature-ideas.md: "CONFIRMED by Dennis
 (2026-08-11): agreed skilled labor interfaces with the system directly,
 unskilled labor rolls up through someone else." It replaces the
 Director/Foreman/Worker hierarchy the earlier drafts used.

enum_values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_SKILLED
enum_values.description: SKILLED: interfaces with the system directly.

enum_values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_UNSKILLED
enum_values.description: UNSKILLED: rolls up through whoever they are working under.

fields.name: credentials
fields.description:
credentials is plural and typed because a single `license` field was
 explicitly rejected: "Credentialing needs to support multiple types (state
 license number, industry cert, company-asserted judgment), not one field."

message.name: Credential
message.description: Credential is one credential a Human holds.

fields.name: credential_type
fields.description:
credential_type carries the RELIABILITY CLASS of the claim, which
 feature-ideas.md calls out as the reason one field would not do: a state
 licence number and a company's own judgement are "different reliability
 classes of fact and worth treating that way".

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_STATE_LICENSE
enum_values.description:
A state occupational licence (electrical, plumbing) — tied to permitting
 and code inspection.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_INDUSTRY_CERT
enum_values.description:
An industry certification (AWS, NCCER) — how welding and heavy equipment
 operation are actually governed.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_COMPANY_ASSERTED
enum_values.description:
The company's own judgement about autonomy/experience, with no papers
 behind it.

fields.name: trade
fields.description:
trade is the trade the credential is in (welder, electrician, operator).
 Prose for now, deliberately: §5 "prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known", and the trade taxonomy is not settled. It must never be parsed —
 "if anything has to parse it to act on it, it should have been a field".

fields.name: issuing_body
fields.description: issuing_body is empty for COMPANY_ASSERTED, which has no issuer.

fields.name: credential_number
fields.description:
credential_number is the licence/certificate number. Empty for
 COMPANY_ASSERTED for the same reason.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description:
expires_at_ms is 0 for a credential that does not expire. Credential
 expiry tracking is listed in §9 as its own typed capability ("a ticket that
 lapses") and is NOT built here — this field is the fact, not the mechanism.

fields.name: verified_by_human_id
fields.description:
verified_by_human_id is who stood behind the claim. For COMPANY_ASSERTED it
 is the whole of the credential's authority, which is why it is a Human id
 rather than a free-text name.

fields.name: identity_links
fields.description:
identity_links are the external subjects that map ONTO this record. The
 direction is the whole point: links point at the Human, never the reverse.

message.name: IdentityLink
message.description: IdentityLink binds one external auth identity to this Human.

fields.name: subject
fields.description:
subject is the provider's own subject claim. It is opaque and must never be
 parsed for meaning.

fields.name: business_hours
fields.description:
business_hours is INFERRED KNOWLEDGE, not configuration, and it is stamped
 by the server — CreateHumanRequest has no field for it and no RPC updates
 it. Jody, 2026-08-30: "business hours are really something we can figure
 out on our own... not a setting."

 It sits on Human rather than on an org type because there is no org type:
 §2 "Hierarchy" leaves org structure unsettled and this file does not invent
 it. Per-person is also the finer of the two grains the ruling allowed, so a
 later per-org layer is a source of the PRIOR, not a move of this field.

message.name: BusinessHours
message.description:
BusinessHours is when this person is taken to be working. It is KNOWLEDGE in
 §1's sense — "what was learned" — not a setting, and nothing in the API lets
 a caller author it.

 TWO LAYERS, and `source` says which one produced the values in this message:

   PRIOR    — an industry+geography default, which is what a brand-new record
              with zero history has. It is a guess, and it is marked as one.
   OBSERVED — refined from the person's own recorded activity once there is
              enough of it to say anything.

 Only the PRIOR layer is WRITTEN today. The observed layer is shape here and
 nothing else, deliberately: the naive refinement (widen the window to cover
 every hour a read was seen at) would defeat the thing the deferral exists to
 protect — one 11pm read would make 11pm business hours. That is a question
 about what evidence of "working" means, not an implementation detail, and it
 is written up rather than guessed. See
 loopers/schematic/decisions/business-hours-inferred-not-configured.md.

 SINGLE CONCEPT. This is the same "business hours" feature-ideas.md's loop
 cadence needs ("looped more frequently Mon-Fri during business hours"). Do
 not add a second notion of it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_PRIOR
enum_values.description: PRIOR: an industry+geography default. No activity data went into it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_OBSERVED
enum_values.description: OBSERVED: refined from this person's own recorded activity.

fields.name: start_of_day_minutes
fields.description:
Minutes past LOCAL midnight, start < end. Nothing validates these on the
 way in because nothing writes them but the service itself; a stored row
 that does not describe a usable window is ignored on the read path in
 favour of the prior, rather than being repaired in place.

fields.name: working_days
fields.description:
The days that are working days. Repeated rather than a mask so the value
 reads as itself in a dump. An empty set is not a usable window, and is
 treated the same way an inverted start/end is — see above.

fields.name: utc_offset_minutes
fields.description:
utc_offset_minutes is the GEOGRAPHY half of the prior, in the crudest form
 that is still correct for the thing it is used for: a fixed offset, no
 DST and no tz database. A Texas crew reading a thread at 23:03 local is
 23:03 whether or not the offset moved an hour in March, and the label the
 deferral produces is a date-and-time, not an instant anyone schedules
 against. A real tz identifier is future work, noted in the decision doc.

fields.name: observed_event_count
fields.description:
observed_event_count is how much activity the OBSERVED layer was refined
 from, and is 0 while source is PRIOR. It is on the message so that "how
 confident is this" is answerable from the row rather than from a guess
 about how old it is.

types.name: CreatePolicyVersionRequest

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description:
policy_id empty means "a new policy": the server allocates an id and this
 becomes version 1. Non-empty means "amend that policy": the server reads
 the highest existing version and writes N+1. The caller never chooses the
 version number, so two concurrent authors cannot both write version 4.

fields.name: effective_from_ms
fields.description: effective_from_ms of 0 means "effective now".

fields.name: weight
fields.description:
weight is required from the caller — §2: "Weight is authored, never
 inferred." assert_enum_defined makes an omitted weight an error rather than
 a silent SOFT.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_SOFT
enum_values.description: Soft — push back once, capture the reason, comply, notify.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_HEAVY
enum_values.description:
Heavy — override requires SOMEONE ELSE's entitlement; the actor cannot
 self-clear.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY
enum_values.description:
Statutory — not overridable in-system by anyone. Ships with the product as
 trade knowledge: "Dennis shouldn't have to know to write the 811 policy."

types.name: CreatePolicyVersionResponse

message.name: PolicyVersion
message.description:
PolicyVersion is ONE version of one written policy, and it is immutable.

 §2, and the word doing the work is "written": "A written policy has a
 document, an author and a date, so policy is quotable or it isn't policy —
 which converts 'Scotty invented a company policy' from a prompt problem into
 a structural one."

 So all four properties are fields, not conventions: body (the document),
 authored_by_human_id (the author), authored_at_ms (the date) and
 effective_from_ms + version (the "at the time" axis). There is no
 UpdatePolicyVersion RPC anywhere in this file. Amending a policy means
 creating version N+1; that is what makes "what did the policy say on the day
 Dennis acted" answerable at all.

 DELIBERATELY ABSENT: any scope/binding field ("who does this bind"). §2 is
 explicit that the answer is a query over (person, context), not a field, and
 that the hierarchy which would feed it is unsettled. Inventing a scope field
 here would silently settle it. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/written-policy-scope-omitted.md (pre-split snoopy history, not in
 this repo).

fields.name: policy_version_id
fields.description: policy_version_id is the collection key — one row per (policy_id, version).

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description:
policy_id is stable ACROSS versions. It is what "policy P version 3
 effective D" (§4's definition of a finding as a citation) names.

fields.name: version
fields.description:
version starts at 1 and increments. Server-assigned, so two authors cannot
 both write version 4.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
body is the document itself — the thing that makes the policy quotable. It
 is prose by nature and must never be parsed to act on.

fields.name: authored_by_human_id
fields.description:
authored_by_human_id is the ATTRIBUTION. §2's known gap turns on this
 field: "Joe overrides a policy Alicia wrote; Dennis is notified, Alicia
 isn't... authorship and override-visibility come apart, and an author
 should know that going in." Recording the author is what makes that gap
 stateable rather than invisible.

 May be empty for POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY, which "isn't authored by anyone
 in the org, so it isn't in the hierarchy at all". Who a statutory policy is
 attributed to is an open product question — see the schematic looper's
 decisions/statutory-policy-authorship-open.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

fields.name: effective_from_ms
fields.description:
effective_from_ms is when this version began to bind. There is no
 effective_to: a version is superseded by the next version's
 effective_from_ms, which cannot drift out of agreement with itself the way
 a separately-written end date can.

fields.name: weight
fields.description:
weight is AUTHORED, never inferred — §2, stated as a rule. It is an enum so
 an undefined weight cannot be stored at all.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_SOFT
enum_values.description: Soft — push back once, capture the reason, comply, notify.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_HEAVY
enum_values.description:
Heavy — override requires SOMEONE ELSE's entitlement; the actor cannot
 self-clear.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY
enum_values.description:
Statutory — not overridable in-system by anyone. Ships with the product as
 trade knowledge: "Dennis shouldn't have to know to write the 811 policy."

types.name: CreateTicketAdviceRequest

message.name: AssertedFact
message.description: AssertedFact is one claim offered to move advice.

fields.name: claim_text
fields.description:
claim_text is the claim as stated ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Prose, and it
 can be wrong — that is the point of recording it.

fields.name: asserted_by_human_id
fields.description: asserted_by_human_id is who is on the hook for it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the caller's own TENANT, and it is the WRITE half of the
 isolation pair. (spec.namespace) binds it in the generated wrapper exactly
 as (spec.principal) binds a subject: left empty it is stamped from the
 token's namespace claim, sent equal it is accepted, sent DIFFERENT the call
 is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a caller carrying no namespace claim
 at all is UNAUTHENTICATED. The field exists so a forged tenant has
 something to be refused at, rather than being silently overwritten.

 The handler copies it onto the row it writes; TicketAdvice.namespace
 is the read half.

types.name: CreateTicketAdviceResponse

message.name: TicketAdvice
message.description:
TicketAdvice is Scotty's advice, SEALED.

 §3: "The advice is sealed when given, not composed at decision time.
 Otherwise a Scotty built to serve Dennis softens a warning it knows he's
 about to override — nobody would have to instruct it to." And: "Immutable to
 Dennis_Scotty too, not only to Dennis."

 Sealing here is STRUCTURAL, not a flag. There is no UpdateTicketAdvice RPC in
 the Scotty service, so no caller — human or agent — has a mutation path to
 reach. A `sealed: bool` would be decoration; an absent RPC is not.

 Advice may be given more than once on a ticket ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Each
 giving is a new sealed row, and the LAST one is the final advice. The design
 record says the ticket carries "the final advice PLUS the asserted facts that
 moved it, not the deliberation" — the append chain is that, with the
 intermediate rows retained rather than discarded. See
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md.

fields.name: advice_text
fields.description:
advice_text is what Scotty advised. Prose, and untrusted at the context
 seam exactly as request_text is — §5 puts "policy text authored by Alicia,
 an override reason from Joe, and a summary distilled by Scotty" in the same
 shape with very different standing, and the standing lives in the
 attribution, not the string.

fields.name: asserted_facts
fields.description:
asserted_facts are the CLAIMS that moved the advice. §3: "Dennis can move
 his Scotty with claims, which land on the record and can be wrong, never
 with vibes." Their landing on the record is the entire mechanism — a claim
 that is not recorded cannot later be found to have been false.

message.name: AssertedFact
message.description: AssertedFact is one claim offered to move advice.

fields.name: claim_text
fields.description:
claim_text is the claim as stated ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Prose, and it
 can be wrong — that is the point of recording it.

fields.name: asserted_by_human_id
fields.description: asserted_by_human_id is who is on the hook for it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketAdviceRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

types.name: CreateTicketCommentRequest

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the caller's own TENANT, and it is the WRITE half of the
 isolation pair. (spec.namespace) binds it in the generated wrapper exactly
 as (spec.principal) binds a subject: left empty it is stamped from the
 token's namespace claim, sent equal it is accepted, sent DIFFERENT the call
 is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a caller carrying no namespace claim
 at all is UNAUTHENTICATED. The field exists so a forged tenant has
 something to be refused at, rather than being silently overwritten.

 The handler copies it onto the row it writes; TicketComment.namespace
 is the read half.

types.name: CreateTicketCommentResponse

message.name: TicketComment
message.description:
TicketComment is a decider's own comment, appended. §3: "Dennis can add his
 own comments... Dennis's comment APPENDS as a separate record, same primitive
 as a field-log correction."

 It is visible to the requester where advice is not — "Joe sees the decision
 and Dennis's comment. Not the advice."

fields.name: authored_by
fields.description: authored_by is the authenticated principal, stamped from the token.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketCommentRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

types.name: CreateTicketDecisionRequest

enum_values.name: TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED
enum_values.description:
AMEND_REQUESTED: this ask, as written, is not being granted, and the
 decider is inviting a revised one. The requester answers it by opening a
 new ticket with amends_ticket_id set to this one, which carries the chain
 forward. Tag 3 is NEW — 1 and 2 keep their wire values.

fields.name: decided_by
fields.description:
decided_by is (spec.principal): empty is stamped from the token, equal is
 accepted, different is refused.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the caller's own TENANT, and it is the WRITE half of the
 isolation pair. (spec.namespace) binds it in the generated wrapper exactly
 as (spec.principal) binds a subject: left empty it is stamped from the
 token's namespace claim, sent equal it is accepted, sent DIFFERENT the call
 is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a caller carrying no namespace claim
 at all is UNAUTHENTICATED. The field exists so a forged tenant has
 something to be refused at, rather than being silently overwritten.

 The handler copies it onto the row it writes; TicketDecision.namespace
 is the read half.

types.name: CreateTicketDecisionResponse

message.name: TicketDecision
message.description:
TicketDecision is the authorise/decline. §3: "when Dennis authorizes or
 declines the request the ticket shows what Scottys advice is and its
 immutable to Dennis."

 Append-only for the same structural reason advice is: no Update RPC. A
 reversal is a new decision row, which keeps "what was decided, and when" from
 being overwritten by "what is decided now".

fields.name: outcome
fields.description:
outcome is authorise, decline or amend-requested. All three are TERMINAL
 for the ticket they are recorded against — an amend request does not
 reopen this ticket, it invites a NEW one carrying the same chain_id. The
 absence of a decision row still means the ask is unresolved, which §3 calls
 "the highest-value finding".

enum_values.name: TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED
enum_values.description:
AMEND_REQUESTED: this ask, as written, is not being granted, and the
 decider is inviting a revised one. The requester answers it by opening a
 new ticket with amends_ticket_id set to this one, which carries the chain
 forward. Tag 3 is NEW — 1 and 2 keep their wire values.

fields.name: decided_by
fields.description:
decided_by is the authenticated principal that decided, stamped from the
 token by the generated wrapper. It is ALWAYS the human — Scotty never
 decides as itself.

fields.name: decided_by_actor
fields.description:
decided_by_actor is the token's `act` claim: the delegate that actually
 made the call, when the human's Scotty made it under a standing policy
 rather than the human making it directly. EMPTY is the ordinary case and
 means the human decided in person; it is not an error or an unknown.

 The distinction is only worth recording if the REQUESTER can see it, which
 is why it is on this row and therefore on GetTicketResponse.decisions,
 rather than only on the artifact envelope. "Dennis authorized this" and
 "Dennis's Scotty authorized this under a policy Dennis wrote" are different
 answers to the question the requester is actually asking.

 NOT (spec.principal) and NOT (spec.store_principal) — the principal is
 decided_by above and stays that way. sys/spec.proto says the same of its
 event-envelope counterpart (spec.identity_spiffe_actor): actor is
 provenance, never the owning principal. There is no store-side annotation
 for it on a state row, so the service stamps it from the generated token
 accessor; see the decision doc for that generator gap.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketDecisionRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

types.name: CreateTicketRequest

fields.name: requested_by
fields.description:
requested_by is the caller's own principal. (spec.principal) binds it to
 the authenticated subject in the generated wrapper: left empty it is
 stamped from the token, sent equal it is accepted, sent different the
 create is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT. The field exists so a client CAN
 supply a principal and the refusal has something to refuse — a forged value
 must not be silently dropped.

fields.name: amends_ticket_id
fields.description:
amends_ticket_id, when set, makes this ticket the next turn in an existing
 chain: the server reads that ticket and copies its chain_id onto this one.
 Empty opens a new chain whose chain_id is this ticket's own id.

 There is deliberately NO chain_id field here. A caller-supplied chain_id
 could disagree with the predecessor's, and the server would then have to
 choose between two answers to "which conversation is this" — so the caller
 is never given the chance to say.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the caller's own TENANT, and it is the WRITE half of the
 isolation pair. (spec.namespace) binds it in the generated wrapper exactly
 as (spec.principal) binds a subject: left empty it is stamped from the
 token's namespace claim, sent equal it is accepted, sent DIFFERENT the call
 is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a caller carrying no namespace claim
 at all is UNAUTHENTICATED. The field exists so a forged tenant has
 something to be refused at, rather than being silently overwritten.

 The handler copies it onto the row it writes; Ticket.namespace
 is the read half.

types.name: CreateTicketResponse

message.name: Ticket
message.description:
Ticket is the IMMUTABLE CORE of a request. §3: "The ticket is a general
 primitive, not a time-off feature — request, routed, advised, decided,
 commented, immutable, appendable, accounted. It covers overrides, permits and
 approvals generally, and it exercises the entire stack."

 NO STATUS FIELD, and that is not an omission. "Immutable" and "a lifecycle
 enum this row keeps up to date" are contradictory, and the lifecycle is
 already fully derivable: a ticket is decided iff a TicketDecision exists for
 it, advised iff a TicketAdvice does. Storing it twice creates a state that
 can disagree with the records it summarises. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/ticket-status-derived-not-stored.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

 NO KIND/CATEGORY FIELD either. §5: "Prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known; a field never degrades to prose because it got inconvenient."
 Time-off, override and permit tickets have not yet shown a common structure,
 so classifying them now would be inventing the taxonomy. request_text carries
 it as attributed prose until the pattern is known. See the schematic
 looper's decisions/ticket-kind-field-deliberately-absent.md (pre-split
 snoopy history, not in this repo).

 NO (spec.store_principal), unlike tasks.Task. That option filters reads to
 the row's creating caller, which would make a routed ticket unreadable BY THE
 PERSON IT IS ROUTED TO — the one read the primitive exists to serve.

fields.name: requested_by
fields.description:
requested_by is the authenticated PRINCIPAL that opened the ticket, stamped
 from the token by the generated wrapper (see CreateTicketRequest). It is
 the token subject, not a Human id, because it has to be the thing the
 platform can actually vouch for.

fields.name: subject_human_id
fields.description:
subject_human_id is the Human the request is ABOUT. Usually the requester
 ("can I take off early Friday"), but not necessarily — a foreman opens a
 ticket about a crew member who has no direct access at all, which is
 exactly the unskilled-rolls-up-through-someone case.

 Its relationship to requested_by is the open half: the design settles that
 the Human record is the source of truth and the token is ephemeral proof,
 but not how a principal is resolved to a Human id at the seam. See
 decisions/principal-to-human-id-resolution-open.md.

fields.name: routed_to_human_id
fields.description:
routed_to_human_id is whose decision is being sought — the "routes to
 Dennis_Scotty" half of §3. One recipient, not a list: §2's propagation rule
 is "escalation is exceptional, and ONE LEVEL ONLY. You do not ask your
 boss's boss", and a repeated field would quietly permit the thing that rule
 forbids.

fields.name: request_text
fields.description:
request_text is the ask, in the requester's own words. It is UNTRUSTED
 INPUT by construction — §5: "Ticket routing puts one person's text into
 another person's agent's context by design; that is a prompt-injection
 channel created by the feature." The two defences are structural and both
 apply here: authority never derives from this string (every authorisation
 in this file is an entitlement or a typed field), and it is attributed at
 the context seam — "Joe wrote:", never a directive.

fields.name: chain_id
fields.description:
chain_id groups every ticket of ONE negotiation. Jody, 2026-08-30:
 "the requestor should be able to ask for reconsideration by amending
 request... you want the entire chain."

 A resubmission after TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED is a NEW
 ticket row, never a mutation of the old one — this row is immutable and the
 rest of the design is append-only for the reasons
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md gives. chain_id is what
 makes the several rows one conversation.

 SERVER-ASSIGNED, and the caller cannot supply it: CreateTicketRequest
 carries amends_ticket_id only, and the server copies the predecessor's
 chain_id. Only the FIRST ticket of a chain has chain_id == ticket_id.

 Not (spec.indexed): that option marks the COLLECTION KEY, which is
 ticket_id. "The entire chain" is ListTickets filtered by this field, the
 same shape routed_to_human_id already has, and it is a service-side filter
 over the collection read — see
 decisions/ticket-decision-chain-2026-08-30.md for the cost.

fields.name: amends_ticket_id
fields.description:
amends_ticket_id names the IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR, and is empty for the
 first ticket in a chain. It is kept alongside chain_id rather than instead
 of it because the two answer different questions: this one is "what did
 this ticket revise", chain_id is "what conversation is this", and reading
 the whole chain off chain_id is one filtered read instead of a walk.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, and the read half of the isolation
 pair this retrofit adds. Its twin is (spec.namespace) on the Create request
 above: that one binds the field to the caller's namespace claim on the way
 IN (stamp when empty, accept when equal, INVALID_ARGUMENT when different);
 this one is what the generated wrapper filters egress rows against on the
 way OUT, by EXACT string equality — never the level-or-below containment
 the administrative namespace rule uses, because "users and data always has
 to land in a leaf".

 A row that has to be dropped by that filter ABORTS THE PROCESS rather than
 failing the one call. Reaching it means kernel handed this service another
 tenant's row, which is a leak the filter exists to make impossible, and the
 decision record settles that a crash is the cheaper failure against it.

 Bounded like ScottyActivity.namespace, and deliberately NOT a query field:
 the field is the egress boundary, and a boundary a caller can name as a
 predicate is not one.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_COMPANY_ASSERTED

trade is the trade the credential is in (welder, electrician, operator).

fields.name: credential_number
fields.description:
credential_number is the licence/certificate number. Empty for
