types.name: Predicate
PredicateGroup
QueryValue
ScottyActivity
types.description:
ScottyActivity is the ARTIFACT left by every write into knowledge.

 §1: "Nothing reaches knowledge without leaving an artifact. Authored facts —
 a phone number, a written policy, a stated deadline — are not distilled from
 anything, so if current state could change with no immutable record, the
 authored half is unrecoverable." ScottyState's requires_artifact_on_write
 enforces that this type exists; this is that type.

 §4 is the reason it is a generated RECORD rather than something the service
 writes for itself: "Scotty must not be the writer of the accounting. If it
 were, 'doesn't rat Dennis out' becomes 'can omit'... Accounting is a
 byproduct of the call path, stamped at the generated seam." The neutral
 auditor reads THIS, and this carries what was DONE — entity kind, entity id,
 principal, request id — never what was said.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 ScottyActivityBus with topic ref scotty.ScottyActivityBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: activity_id
fields.description: activity_id is the record key: one row per WRITE, not one per entity.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.description:
entity_kind and entity_id name what was written. EQ-filterable, because
 "every artifact for this ticket" is the question provenance has to answer.

enum_values.name: SCOTTY_ENTITY_KIND_TICKET_CHAIN
enum_values.description:
A TICKET_CHAIN artifact is left ONCE per chain, on the hop that reaches
 Config.max_chain_hops — the moment Scotty stops mediating. entity_id is the
 chain_id. It records that AI mediation hit its limit, which is a thing that
 was DONE and therefore belongs in the auditor's store; no ticket is decided
 by it.

fields.name: occurred_at_ms
fields.description:
occurred_at_ms is the RANGE criterion — "what happened between D1 and D2"
 is the auditor's own question.

fields.name: acted_by
fields.description:
acted_by is the principal on whose behalf the write happened. NOT redacted:
 §4 says a finding is a citation naming "action A by principal X at T", and
 a citation whose principal egress clears is not a citation.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s
 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER
 — eventbus stamps scotty's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. acted_by is the
 authenticated human the write happened for, taken from the verified token
 (service.rs `principal()`) or from the written row's own (spec.principal)
 field, never from anything the caller writes. That is the value the
 generated wrapper's row filter must compare against.
 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query, and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that wrote
 this row" and "which row did that request write" are one predicate asked of
 two record types. Without it provenance stops at the accounting plane's
 edge, which is precisely where §4's auditor starts.

 Empty is legitimate, not an error: an unauthenticated path has no Caller to
 read one from, so a required-and-absent field would fail the publish rather
 than record the gap.

fields.name: spiffe_actor
fields.description:
spiffe_actor is the DELEGATE that made the call, stamped by EventBus from
 the token's `act` claim at publish time — the agent acting for the person
 in acted_by, unset in the ordinary non-delegated case. Provenance only: it
 is never the principal, and sys/spec.proto forbids wiring it into one.

 The service does not set it and must not: like spiffe_id above, a value
 written here would be a claim about identity that nothing verified.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose write this artifact records. It is the tenant half of the identity
 acted_by carries the subject half of — that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant", by EXACT
 string equality against the caller's claim (never the level-or-below
 containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over EVERY record in
 the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of them for this
 type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than the caller's
 halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like acted_by.

 AN EQ (spec.query_field), and it did not used to be. The reasoning that kept
 it off was that a boundary is not a caller-supplied predicate — which is
 right about the CALLER and wrong about the SERVER. The client-facing read
 plane pins this field to the caller's verified namespace claim BEFORE the
 store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into; the record
 store evaluates only the criteria a record annotates, so without this line
 the pin is generated and silently ignored, leaving the aborting egress
 filter as the only tenant boundary. tacplus refuses (spec.record).c2s_read
 on a record whose namespace field is not EQ-queryable, for exactly that
 reason.

 It stays uncallable by clients, which is the part the old comment cared
 about: the emitted GetScottyActivityRequest and ListScottyActivityRequest
 carry no namespace field, and ScottyActivityReadFilter — the only filter a
 c2s caller supplies — is generated without one.

types.name: ScottyConfigState
types.description:
ScottyConfigState is the state boundary for scotty service configuration.
 Auto-injected by tacplus from (spec.grpc_config) annotation.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_open_tickets
fields.description:
max_open_tickets bounds how many tickets may be open at once, and exists
 for the same reason tasks.Config.max_open_tasks does: to give the service a
 rule that comes from CONFIG rather than from code, so changing it in kernel
 changes behaviour with no redeploy.

 NOT a written policy. §2 is explicit that "an entitlement makes an action
 impossible, a written policy makes it inadvisable" — a config bound that
 hard-fails a create is neither, it is a resource limit on the service. No
 business rule may be expressed here.

fields.name: max_chain_hops
fields.description:
max_chain_hops is the CIRCUIT BREAKER on AI-mediated negotiation, and it is
 a HOP COUNT, not a duration. A chain's hop count is the number of turns
 taken in it — every Ticket, TicketAdvice and TicketComment sharing a
 chain_id — and when it reaches this bound Scotty stops adding its own
 judgement to that chain. Jody, 2026-08-30: "it escalates to the human at
 the same level. It just keeps LLMs from getting stuck in a loop."

 Config for the same reason max_open_tickets is: it is a resource-shaped
 bound on the service, changeable in kernel with no redeploy, and it is NOT
 a written policy — nothing here decides anything about a request.

 A wall-clock TTL was proposed for this and explicitly discarded; see
 loopers/schematic/decisions/ticket-ttl-hop-count-circuit-breaker-2026-08-30.md.

fields.name: llm_credential
fields.description:
llm_credential is the Anthropic API key, fanned out by operator into this
 service's generated bootstrap config under the YAML key "llm_credential"
 (see platform/proto/services/operator.proto's Config.llm_credential and
 .llm_credential_services, and operator.yaml's own llm_credential_services
 list, which must include "scotty" for the fan-out to reach here). Field
 name and type must match what operator's bootstrap.go writes, or the
 service fails to unmarshal its own generated config.

types.name: ScottyState
types.description: ScottyState is this service's state root, stored in kernel's cluster.

fields.name: humans
fields.description:
Every boundary here is a COLLECTION. There is no singleton: nothing in the
 settled design is per-tenant-and-exactly-one.

 Bounds are real limits on the store, not decoration — tacplus rejects an
 unbounded repeated field at generation time. They are sized off the design
 record's own volume finding (§1: "at Jimerson scale (~100 people) the
 entire product dataset is single-digit GB after a decade"), with headroom.

message.name: Human
message.description:
Human is the durable identity record.

 The load-bearing principle, from architecture-sketch.md §4 and reaffirmed by
 the design record: "the Human record is the durable source of truth;
 OAuth/SAML claims are ephemeral proof of 'this session is really this
 person', never themselves the store of who someone is or what they're
 allowed to do."

 DELIBERATELY ABSENT — every one of these appears in the architecture sketch's
 draft and is contradicted or unsettled by the later design record:
   - org_unit_id / reports_through: §2 "Hierarchy" says these as single
     strings "do not express this", because a chain can differ per job.
   - rule_auth_level: "rule" was retired in favour of "written policy", and
     the sketch derived this field FROM org_unit_id, which is the field above.
   - personal_scotty_id: agent-instance binding is not settled as a type.
 See the schematic looper's decisions/human-hierarchy-fields-omitted-not-invented.md
 (pre-split snoopy history, not in this repo).

 Human carries NO (spec.store_principal). On tasks.Task that option filters
 every read down to the creating caller — correct for a personal task list and
 wrong here, because a Human record exists precisely to be read by people
 other than whoever typed it in. Read authorization for Human is entitlement
 work and is not done; see the schematic looper's
 decisions/scotty-read-authorization-not-wired.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

fields.name: human_id
fields.description:
human_id is the collection key: indexed, required, non-empty — the
 state-collection convention.

fields.name: email
fields.description:
email and phone are AUTHORED facts in the §1 sense — "a phone number, a
 written policy, a stated deadline — are not distilled from anything" — so a
 write to either has to leave an artifact, which requires_artifact_on_write
 above enforces.

 Not (spec.assert_email): an empty string is a legitimate value here (an
 unskilled labourer who rolls up through someone else may have no address on
 file at all), and assert_email would reject it.

fields.name: skill
fields.description:
skill is the SETTLED axis. feature-ideas.md: "CONFIRMED by Dennis
 (2026-08-11): agreed skilled labor interfaces with the system directly,
 unskilled labor rolls up through someone else." It replaces the
 Director/Foreman/Worker hierarchy the earlier drafts used.

enum_values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_SKILLED
enum_values.description: SKILLED: interfaces with the system directly.

enum_values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_UNSKILLED
enum_values.description: UNSKILLED: rolls up through whoever they are working under.

fields.name: credentials
fields.description:
credentials is plural and typed because a single `license` field was
 explicitly rejected: "Credentialing needs to support multiple types (state
 license number, industry cert, company-asserted judgment), not one field."

message.name: Credential
message.description: Credential is one credential a Human holds.

fields.name: credential_type
fields.description:
credential_type carries the RELIABILITY CLASS of the claim, which
 feature-ideas.md calls out as the reason one field would not do: a state
 licence number and a company's own judgement are "different reliability
 classes of fact and worth treating that way".

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_STATE_LICENSE
enum_values.description:
A state occupational licence (electrical, plumbing) — tied to permitting
 and code inspection.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_INDUSTRY_CERT
enum_values.description:
An industry certification (AWS, NCCER) — how welding and heavy equipment
 operation are actually governed.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_COMPANY_ASSERTED
enum_values.description:
The company's own judgement about autonomy/experience, with no papers
 behind it.

fields.name: trade
fields.description:
trade is the trade the credential is in (welder, electrician, operator).
 Prose for now, deliberately: §5 "prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known", and the trade taxonomy is not settled. It must never be parsed —
 "if anything has to parse it to act on it, it should have been a field".

fields.name: issuing_body
fields.description: issuing_body is empty for COMPANY_ASSERTED, which has no issuer.

fields.name: credential_number
fields.description:
credential_number is the licence/certificate number. Empty for
 COMPANY_ASSERTED for the same reason.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description:
expires_at_ms is 0 for a credential that does not expire. Credential
 expiry tracking is listed in §9 as its own typed capability ("a ticket that
 lapses") and is NOT built here — this field is the fact, not the mechanism.

fields.name: verified_by_human_id
fields.description:
verified_by_human_id is who stood behind the claim. For COMPANY_ASSERTED it
 is the whole of the credential's authority, which is why it is a Human id
 rather than a free-text name.

fields.name: identity_links
fields.description:
identity_links are the external subjects that map ONTO this record. The
 direction is the whole point: links point at the Human, never the reverse.

message.name: IdentityLink
message.description: IdentityLink binds one external auth identity to this Human.

fields.name: subject
fields.description:
subject is the provider's own subject claim. It is opaque and must never be
 parsed for meaning.

fields.name: business_hours
fields.description:
business_hours is INFERRED KNOWLEDGE, not configuration, and it is stamped
 by the server — CreateHumanRequest has no field for it and no RPC updates
 it. Jody, 2026-08-30: "business hours are really something we can figure
 out on our own... not a setting."

 It sits on Human rather than on an org type because there is no org type:
 §2 "Hierarchy" leaves org structure unsettled and this file does not invent
 it. Per-person is also the finer of the two grains the ruling allowed, so a
 later per-org layer is a source of the PRIOR, not a move of this field.

message.name: BusinessHours
message.description:
BusinessHours is when this person is taken to be working. It is KNOWLEDGE in
 §1's sense — "what was learned" — not a setting, and nothing in the API lets
 a caller author it.

 TWO LAYERS, and `source` says which one produced the values in this message:

   PRIOR    — an industry+geography default, which is what a brand-new record
              with zero history has. It is a guess, and it is marked as one.
   OBSERVED — refined from the person's own recorded activity once there is
              enough of it to say anything.

 Only the PRIOR layer is WRITTEN today. The observed layer is shape here and
 nothing else, deliberately: the naive refinement (widen the window to cover
 every hour a read was seen at) would defeat the thing the deferral exists to
 protect — one 11pm read would make 11pm business hours. That is a question
 about what evidence of "working" means, not an implementation detail, and it
 is written up rather than guessed. See
 loopers/schematic/decisions/business-hours-inferred-not-configured.md.

 SINGLE CONCEPT. This is the same "business hours" feature-ideas.md's loop
 cadence needs ("looped more frequently Mon-Fri during business hours"). Do
 not add a second notion of it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_PRIOR
enum_values.description: PRIOR: an industry+geography default. No activity data went into it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_OBSERVED
enum_values.description: OBSERVED: refined from this person's own recorded activity.

fields.name: start_of_day_minutes
fields.description:
Minutes past LOCAL midnight, start < end. Nothing validates these on the
 way in because nothing writes them but the service itself; a stored row
 that does not describe a usable window is ignored on the read path in
 favour of the prior, rather than being repaired in place.

fields.name: working_days
fields.description:
The days that are working days. Repeated rather than a mask so the value
 reads as itself in a dump. An empty set is not a usable window, and is
 treated the same way an inverted start/end is — see above.

fields.name: utc_offset_minutes
fields.description:
utc_offset_minutes is the GEOGRAPHY half of the prior, in the crudest form
 that is still correct for the thing it is used for: a fixed offset, no
 DST and no tz database. A Texas crew reading a thread at 23:03 local is
 23:03 whether or not the offset moved an hour in March, and the label the
 deferral produces is a date-and-time, not an instant anyone schedules
 against. A real tz identifier is future work, noted in the decision doc.

fields.name: observed_event_count
fields.description:
observed_event_count is how much activity the OBSERVED layer was refined
 from, and is 0 while source is PRIOR. It is on the message so that "how
 confident is this" is answerable from the row rather than from a guess
 about how old it is.

fields.name: policy_versions
fields.description:
One row per policy VERSION, never one row per policy. §2: "policy is
 quotable or it isn't policy... Versioning and effective dating come with
 it, and 'was Dennis in violation' is a question about what the policy said
 AT THE TIME." A mutable policy row cannot answer that question, so a
 version is a new row and no RPC updates an existing one.

message.name: PolicyVersion
message.description:
PolicyVersion is ONE version of one written policy, and it is immutable.

 §2, and the word doing the work is "written": "A written policy has a
 document, an author and a date, so policy is quotable or it isn't policy —
 which converts 'Scotty invented a company policy' from a prompt problem into
 a structural one."

 So all four properties are fields, not conventions: body (the document),
 authored_by_human_id (the author), authored_at_ms (the date) and
 effective_from_ms + version (the "at the time" axis). There is no
 UpdatePolicyVersion RPC anywhere in this file. Amending a policy means
 creating version N+1; that is what makes "what did the policy say on the day
 Dennis acted" answerable at all.

 DELIBERATELY ABSENT: any scope/binding field ("who does this bind"). §2 is
 explicit that the answer is a query over (person, context), not a field, and
 that the hierarchy which would feed it is unsettled. Inventing a scope field
 here would silently settle it. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/written-policy-scope-omitted.md (pre-split snoopy history, not in
 this repo).

fields.name: policy_version_id
fields.description: policy_version_id is the collection key — one row per (policy_id, version).

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description:
policy_id is stable ACROSS versions. It is what "policy P version 3
 effective D" (§4's definition of a finding as a citation) names.

fields.name: version
fields.description:
version starts at 1 and increments. Server-assigned, so two authors cannot
 both write version 4.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
body is the document itself — the thing that makes the policy quotable. It
 is prose by nature and must never be parsed to act on.

fields.name: authored_by_human_id
fields.description:
authored_by_human_id is the ATTRIBUTION. §2's known gap turns on this
 field: "Joe overrides a policy Alicia wrote; Dennis is notified, Alicia
 isn't... authorship and override-visibility come apart, and an author
 should know that going in." Recording the author is what makes that gap
 stateable rather than invisible.

 May be empty for POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY, which "isn't authored by anyone
 in the org, so it isn't in the hierarchy at all". Who a statutory policy is
 attributed to is an open product question — see the schematic looper's
 decisions/statutory-policy-authorship-open.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

fields.name: effective_from_ms
fields.description:
effective_from_ms is when this version began to bind. There is no
 effective_to: a version is superseded by the next version's
 effective_from_ms, which cannot drift out of agreement with itself the way
 a separately-written end date can.

fields.name: weight
fields.description:
weight is AUTHORED, never inferred — §2, stated as a rule. It is an enum so
 an undefined weight cannot be stored at all.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_SOFT
enum_values.description: Soft — push back once, capture the reason, comply, notify.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_HEAVY
enum_values.description:
Heavy — override requires SOMEONE ELSE's entitlement; the actor cannot
 self-clear.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY
enum_values.description:
Statutory — not overridable in-system by anyone. Ships with the product as
 trade knowledge: "Dennis shouldn't have to know to write the 811 policy."

fields.name: tickets
fields.description:
The ticket's IMMUTABLE CORE. §3: "request, routed, advised, decided,
 commented, immutable, appendable". Nothing that changes over a ticket's
 life lives on this row — see Ticket below for why there is no status field.

message.name: Ticket
message.description:
Ticket is the IMMUTABLE CORE of a request. §3: "The ticket is a general
 primitive, not a time-off feature — request, routed, advised, decided,
 commented, immutable, appendable, accounted. It covers overrides, permits and
 approvals generally, and it exercises the entire stack."

 NO STATUS FIELD, and that is not an omission. "Immutable" and "a lifecycle
 enum this row keeps up to date" are contradictory, and the lifecycle is
 already fully derivable: a ticket is decided iff a TicketDecision exists for
 it, advised iff a TicketAdvice does. Storing it twice creates a state that
 can disagree with the records it summarises. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/ticket-status-derived-not-stored.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

 NO KIND/CATEGORY FIELD either. §5: "Prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known; a field never degrades to prose because it got inconvenient."
 Time-off, override and permit tickets have not yet shown a common structure,
 so classifying them now would be inventing the taxonomy. request_text carries
 it as attributed prose until the pattern is known. See the schematic
 looper's decisions/ticket-kind-field-deliberately-absent.md (pre-split
 snoopy history, not in this repo).

 NO (spec.store_principal), unlike tasks.Task. That option filters reads to
 the row's creating caller, which would make a routed ticket unreadable BY THE
 PERSON IT IS ROUTED TO — the one read the primitive exists to serve.

fields.name: requested_by
fields.description:
requested_by is the authenticated PRINCIPAL that opened the ticket, stamped
 from the token by the generated wrapper (see CreateTicketRequest). It is
 the token subject, not a Human id, because it has to be the thing the
 platform can actually vouch for.

fields.name: subject_human_id
fields.description:
subject_human_id is the Human the request is ABOUT. Usually the requester
 ("can I take off early Friday"), but not necessarily — a foreman opens a
 ticket about a crew member who has no direct access at all, which is
 exactly the unskilled-rolls-up-through-someone case.

 Its relationship to requested_by is the open half: the design settles that
 the Human record is the source of truth and the token is ephemeral proof,
 but not how a principal is resolved to a Human id at the seam. See
 decisions/principal-to-human-id-resolution-open.md.

fields.name: routed_to_human_id
fields.description:
routed_to_human_id is whose decision is being sought — the "routes to
 Dennis_Scotty" half of §3. One recipient, not a list: §2's propagation rule
 is "escalation is exceptional, and ONE LEVEL ONLY. You do not ask your
 boss's boss", and a repeated field would quietly permit the thing that rule
 forbids.

fields.name: request_text
fields.description:
request_text is the ask, in the requester's own words. It is UNTRUSTED
 INPUT by construction — §5: "Ticket routing puts one person's text into
 another person's agent's context by design; that is a prompt-injection
 channel created by the feature." The two defences are structural and both
 apply here: authority never derives from this string (every authorisation
 in this file is an entitlement or a typed field), and it is attributed at
 the context seam — "Joe wrote:", never a directive.

fields.name: chain_id
fields.description:
chain_id groups every ticket of ONE negotiation. Jody, 2026-08-30:
 "the requestor should be able to ask for reconsideration by amending
 request... you want the entire chain."

 A resubmission after TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED is a NEW
 ticket row, never a mutation of the old one — this row is immutable and the
 rest of the design is append-only for the reasons
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md gives. chain_id is what
 makes the several rows one conversation.

 SERVER-ASSIGNED, and the caller cannot supply it: CreateTicketRequest
 carries amends_ticket_id only, and the server copies the predecessor's
 chain_id. Only the FIRST ticket of a chain has chain_id == ticket_id.

 Not (spec.indexed): that option marks the COLLECTION KEY, which is
 ticket_id. "The entire chain" is ListTickets filtered by this field, the
 same shape routed_to_human_id already has, and it is a service-side filter
 over the collection read — see
 decisions/ticket-decision-chain-2026-08-30.md for the cost.

fields.name: amends_ticket_id
fields.description:
amends_ticket_id names the IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR, and is empty for the
 first ticket in a chain. It is kept alongside chain_id rather than instead
 of it because the two answer different questions: this one is "what did
 this ticket revise", chain_id is "what conversation is this", and reading
 the whole chain off chain_id is one filtered read instead of a walk.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, and the read half of the isolation
 pair this retrofit adds. Its twin is (spec.namespace) on the Create request
 above: that one binds the field to the caller's namespace claim on the way
 IN (stamp when empty, accept when equal, INVALID_ARGUMENT when different);
 this one is what the generated wrapper filters egress rows against on the
 way OUT, by EXACT string equality — never the level-or-below containment
 the administrative namespace rule uses, because "users and data always has
 to land in a leaf".

 A row that has to be dropped by that filter ABORTS THE PROCESS rather than
 failing the one call. Reaching it means kernel handed this service another
 tenant's row, which is a leak the filter exists to make impossible, and the
 decision record settles that a crash is the cheaper failure against it.

 Bounded like ScottyActivity.namespace, and deliberately NOT a query field:
 the field is the egress boundary, and a boundary a caller can name as a
 predicate is not one.

fields.name: ticket_advice
fields.description:
The three APPEND-ONLY sides of a ticket, held as three separate
 collections rather than one polymorphic entry type. They are separate
 because their VISIBILITY differs and that difference is the design: §3,
 "Joe sees the decision and Dennis's comment. Not the advice." Distinct
 collections reached by distinct RPCs give that rule somewhere to attach.
 A oneof inside one collection would put the restricted and unrestricted
 rows behind one read, which is the shape that cannot be entitled apart.

message.name: TicketAdvice
message.description:
TicketAdvice is Scotty's advice, SEALED.

 §3: "The advice is sealed when given, not composed at decision time.
 Otherwise a Scotty built to serve Dennis softens a warning it knows he's
 about to override — nobody would have to instruct it to." And: "Immutable to
 Dennis_Scotty too, not only to Dennis."

 Sealing here is STRUCTURAL, not a flag. There is no UpdateTicketAdvice RPC in
 the Scotty service, so no caller — human or agent — has a mutation path to
 reach. A `sealed: bool` would be decoration; an absent RPC is not.

 Advice may be given more than once on a ticket ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Each
 giving is a new sealed row, and the LAST one is the final advice. The design
 record says the ticket carries "the final advice PLUS the asserted facts that
 moved it, not the deliberation" — the append chain is that, with the
 intermediate rows retained rather than discarded. See
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md.

fields.name: advice_text
fields.description:
advice_text is what Scotty advised. Prose, and untrusted at the context
 seam exactly as request_text is — §5 puts "policy text authored by Alicia,
 an override reason from Joe, and a summary distilled by Scotty" in the same
 shape with very different standing, and the standing lives in the
 attribution, not the string.

fields.name: asserted_facts
fields.description:
asserted_facts are the CLAIMS that moved the advice. §3: "Dennis can move
 his Scotty with claims, which land on the record and can be wrong, never
 with vibes." Their landing on the record is the entire mechanism — a claim
 that is not recorded cannot later be found to have been false.

message.name: AssertedFact
message.description: AssertedFact is one claim offered to move advice.

fields.name: claim_text
fields.description:
claim_text is the claim as stated ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Prose, and it
 can be wrong — that is the point of recording it.

fields.name: asserted_by_human_id
fields.description: asserted_by_human_id is who is on the hook for it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketAdviceRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

message.name: TicketDecision
message.description:
TicketDecision is the authorise/decline. §3: "when Dennis authorizes or
 declines the request the ticket shows what Scottys advice is and its
 immutable to Dennis."

 Append-only for the same structural reason advice is: no Update RPC. A
 reversal is a new decision row, which keeps "what was decided, and when" from
 being overwritten by "what is decided now".

fields.name: outcome
fields.description:
outcome is authorise, decline or amend-requested. All three are TERMINAL
 for the ticket they are recorded against — an amend request does not
 reopen this ticket, it invites a NEW one carrying the same chain_id. The
 absence of a decision row still means the ask is unresolved, which §3 calls
 "the highest-value finding".

enum_values.name: TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED
enum_values.description:
AMEND_REQUESTED: this ask, as written, is not being granted, and the
 decider is inviting a revised one. The requester answers it by opening a
 new ticket with amends_ticket_id set to this one, which carries the chain
 forward. Tag 3 is NEW — 1 and 2 keep their wire values.

fields.name: decided_by
fields.description:
decided_by is the authenticated principal that decided, stamped from the
 token by the generated wrapper. It is ALWAYS the human — Scotty never
 decides as itself.

fields.name: decided_by_actor
fields.description:
decided_by_actor is the token's `act` claim: the delegate that actually
 made the call, when the human's Scotty made it under a standing policy
 rather than the human making it directly. EMPTY is the ordinary case and
 means the human decided in person; it is not an error or an unknown.

 The distinction is only worth recording if the REQUESTER can see it, which
 is why it is on this row and therefore on GetTicketResponse.decisions,
 rather than only on the artifact envelope. "Dennis authorized this" and
 "Dennis's Scotty authorized this under a policy Dennis wrote" are different
 answers to the question the requester is actually asking.

 NOT (spec.principal) and NOT (spec.store_principal) — the principal is
 decided_by above and stays that way. sys/spec.proto says the same of its
 event-envelope counterpart (spec.identity_spiffe_actor): actor is
 provenance, never the owning principal. There is no store-side annotation
 for it on a state row, so the service stamps it from the generated token
 accessor; see the decision doc for that generator gap.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketDecisionRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

message.name: TicketComment
message.description:
TicketComment is a decider's own comment, appended. §3: "Dennis can add his
 own comments... Dennis's comment APPENDS as a separate record, same primitive
 as a field-log correction."

 It is visible to the requester where advice is not — "Joe sees the decision
 and Dennis's comment. Not the advice."

fields.name: authored_by
fields.description: authored_by is the authenticated principal, stamped from the token.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketCommentRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

 from the token by the generated wrapper (see CreateTicketRequest). It is

subject_human_id is the Human the request is ABOUT. Usually the requester
 ("can I take off early Friday"), but not necessarily — a foreman opens a
 ticket about a crew member who has no direct access at all, which is
 exactly the unskilled-rolls-up-through-someone case.

 Its relationship to requested_by is the open half: the design settles that
 the Human record is the source of truth and the token is ephemeral proof,
 but not how a principal is resolved to a Human id at the seam. See
 decisions/principal-to-human-id-resolution-open.md.

fields.name: routed_to_human_id
fields.description:
routed_to_human_id is whose decision is being sought — the "routes to
 Dennis_Scotty" half of §3. One recipient, not a list: §2's propagation rule
 is "escalation is exceptional, and ONE LEVEL ONLY. You do not ask your
 boss's boss", and a repeated field would quietly permit the thing that rule
 forbids.

fields.name: request_text
fields.description:
request_text is the ask, in the requester's own words. It is UNTRUSTED
 INPUT by construction — §5: "Ticket routing puts one person's text into
 another person's agent's context by design; that is a prompt-injection
 channel created by the feature." The two defences are structural and both
 apply here: authority never derives from this string (every authorisation
 in this file is an entitlement or a typed field), and it is attributed at
 the context seam — "Joe wrote:", never a directive.

fields.name: chain_id
fields.description:
chain_id groups every ticket of ONE negotiation. Jody, 2026-08-30:
 "the requestor should be able to ask for reconsideration by amending
 request... you want the entire chain."

 A resubmission after TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED is a NEW
 ticket row, never a mutation of the old one — this row is immutable and the
 rest of the design is append-only for the reasons
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md gives. chain_id is what
 makes the several rows one conversation.

 SERVER-ASSIGNED, and the caller cannot supply it: CreateTicketRequest
 carries amends_ticket_id only, and the server copies the predecessor's
 chain_id. Only the FIRST ticket of a chain has chain_id == ticket_id.

 Not (spec.indexed): that option marks the COLLECTION KEY, which is
 ticket_id. "The entire chain" is ListTickets filtered by this field, the
 same shape routed_to_human_id already has, and it is a service-side filter
 over the collection read — see
 decisions/ticket-decision-chain-2026-08-30.md for the cost.

fields.name: amends_ticket_id
fields.description:
amends_ticket_id names the IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR, and is empty for the
 first ticket in a chain. It is kept alongside chain_id rather than instead
 of it because the two answer different questions: this one is "what did
 this ticket revise", chain_id is "what conversation is this", and reading
 the whole chain off chain_id is one filtered read instead of a walk.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, and the read half of the isolation
 pair this retrofit adds. Its twin is (spec.namespace) on the Create request
 above: that one binds the field to the caller's namespace claim on the way
 IN (stamp when empty, accept when equal, INVALID_ARGUMENT when different);
 this one is what the generated wrapper filters egress rows against on the
 way OUT, by EXACT string equality — never the level-or-below containment
 the administrative namespace rule uses, because "users and data always has
 to land in a leaf".

 A row that has to be dropped by that filter ABORTS THE PROCESS rather than
 failing the one call. Reaching it means kernel handed this service another
 tenant's row, which is a leak the filter exists to make impossible, and the
 decision record settles that a crash is the cheaper failure against it.

 Bounded like ScottyActivity.namespace, and deliberately NOT a query field:
 the field is the egress boundary, and a boundary a caller can name as a
 predicate is not one.

types.name: TicketAdvice
types.description:
TicketAdvice is Scotty's advice, SEALED.

 §3: "The advice is sealed when given, not composed at decision time.
 Otherwise a Scotty built to serve Dennis softens a warning it knows he's
 about to override — nobody would have to instruct it to." And: "Immutable to
 Dennis_Scotty too, not only to Dennis."

 Sealing here is STRUCTURAL, not a flag. There is no UpdateTicketAdvice RPC in
 the Scotty service, so no caller — human or agent — has a mutation path to
 reach. A `sealed: bool` would be decoration; an absent RPC is not.

 Advice may be given more than once on a ticket ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Each
 giving is a new sealed row, and the LAST one is the final advice. The design
 record says the ticket carries "the final advice PLUS the asserted facts that
 moved it, not the deliberation" — the append chain is that, with the
 intermediate rows retained rather than discarded. See
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md.

fields.name: advice_text
fields.description:
advice_text is what Scotty advised. Prose, and untrusted at the context
 seam exactly as request_text is — §5 puts "policy text authored by Alicia,
 an override reason from Joe, and a summary distilled by Scotty" in the same
 shape with very different standing, and the standing lives in the
 attribution, not the string.

fields.name: asserted_facts
fields.description:
asserted_facts are the CLAIMS that moved the advice. §3: "Dennis can move
 his Scotty with claims, which land on the record and can be wrong, never
 with vibes." Their landing on the record is the entire mechanism — a claim
 that is not recorded cannot later be found to have been false.

message.name: AssertedFact
message.description: AssertedFact is one claim offered to move advice.

fields.name: claim_text
fields.description:
claim_text is the claim as stated ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Prose, and it
 can be wrong — that is the point of recording it.

fields.name: asserted_by_human_id
fields.description: asserted_by_human_id is who is on the hook for it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketAdviceRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

types.name: TicketDecision
types.description:
TicketDecision is the authorise/decline. §3: "when Dennis authorizes or
 declines the request the ticket shows what Scottys advice is and its
 immutable to Dennis."

 Append-only for the same structural reason advice is: no Update RPC. A
 reversal is a new decision row, which keeps "what was decided, and when" from
 being overwritten by "what is decided now".

fields.name: outcome
fields.description:
outcome is authorise, decline or amend-requested. All three are TERMINAL
 for the ticket they are recorded against — an amend request does not
 reopen this ticket, it invites a NEW one carrying the same chain_id. The
 absence of a decision row still means the ask is unresolved, which §3 calls
 "the highest-value finding".

enum_values.name: TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED
enum_values.description:
AMEND_REQUESTED: this ask, as written, is not being granted, and the
 decider is inviting a revised one. The requester answers it by opening a
 new ticket with amends_ticket_id set to this one, which carries the chain
 forward. Tag 3 is NEW — 1 and 2 keep their wire values.

fields.name: decided_by
fields.description:
decided_by is the authenticated principal that decided, stamped from the
 token by the generated wrapper. It is ALWAYS the human — Scotty never
 decides as itself.

fields.name: decided_by_actor
fields.description:
decided_by_actor is the token's `act` claim: the delegate that actually
 made the call, when the human's Scotty made it under a standing policy
 rather than the human making it directly. EMPTY is the ordinary case and
 means the human decided in person; it is not an error or an unknown.

 The distinction is only worth recording if the REQUESTER can see it, which
 is why it is on this row and therefore on GetTicketResponse.decisions,
 rather than only on the artifact envelope. "Dennis authorized this" and
 "Dennis's Scotty authorized this under a policy Dennis wrote" are different
 answers to the question the requester is actually asking.

 NOT (spec.principal) and NOT (spec.store_principal) — the principal is
 decided_by above and stays that way. sys/spec.proto says the same of its
 event-envelope counterpart (spec.identity_spiffe_actor): actor is
 provenance, never the owning principal. There is no store-side annotation
 for it on a state row, so the service stamps it from the generated token
 accessor; see the decision doc for that generator gap.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketDecisionRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. See Ticket.namespace.

 decided_by above and stays that way. sys/spec.proto says the same of its

 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketDecisionRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that

message.name: Ticket
message.description:
Ticket is the IMMUTABLE CORE of a request. §3: "The ticket is a general
 primitive, not a time-off feature — request, routed, advised, decided,
 commented, immutable, appendable, accounted. It covers overrides, permits and
 approvals generally, and it exercises the entire stack."

 NO STATUS FIELD, and that is not an omission. "Immutable" and "a lifecycle
 enum this row keeps up to date" are contradictory, and the lifecycle is
 already fully derivable: a ticket is decided iff a TicketDecision exists for
 it, advised iff a TicketAdvice does. Storing it twice creates a state that
 can disagree with the records it summarises. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/ticket-status-derived-not-stored.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

 NO KIND/CATEGORY FIELD either. §5: "Prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known; a field never degrades to prose because it got inconvenient."
 Time-off, override and permit tickets have not yet shown a common structure,
 so classifying them now would be inventing the taxonomy. request_text carries
 it as attributed prose until the pattern is known. See the schematic
 looper's decisions/ticket-kind-field-deliberately-absent.md (pre-split
 snoopy history, not in this repo).

 NO (spec.store_principal), unlike tasks.Task. That option filters reads to
 the row's creating caller, which would make a routed ticket unreadable BY THE
 PERSON IT IS ROUTED TO — the one read the primitive exists to serve.

fields.name: requested_by
fields.description:
requested_by is the authenticated PRINCIPAL that opened the ticket, stamped
 from the token by the generated wrapper (see CreateTicketRequest). It is
 the token subject, not a Human id, because it has to be the thing the
 platform can actually vouch for.

fields.name: subject_human_id
fields.description:
subject_human_id is the Human the request is ABOUT. Usually the requester
 ("can I take off early Friday"), but not necessarily — a foreman opens a
 ticket about a crew member who has no direct access at all, which is
 exactly the unskilled-rolls-up-through-someone case.

 Its relationship to requested_by is the open half: the design settles that
 the Human record is the source of truth and the token is ephemeral proof,
 but not how a principal is resolved to a Human id at the seam. See
 decisions/principal-to-human-id-resolution-open.md.

fields.name: routed_to_human_id
fields.description:
routed_to_human_id is whose decision is being sought — the "routes to
 Dennis_Scotty" half of §3. One recipient, not a list: §2's propagation rule
 is "escalation is exceptional, and ONE LEVEL ONLY. You do not ask your
 boss's boss", and a repeated field would quietly permit the thing that rule
 forbids.

fields.name: request_text
fields.description:
request_text is the ask, in the requester's own words. It is UNTRUSTED
 INPUT by construction — §5: "Ticket routing puts one person's text into
 another person's agent's context by design; that is a prompt-injection
 channel created by the feature." The two defences are structural and both
 apply here: authority never derives from this string (every authorisation
 in this file is an entitlement or a typed field), and it is attributed at
 the context seam — "Joe wrote:", never a directive.

fields.name: chain_id
fields.description:
chain_id groups every ticket of ONE negotiation. Jody, 2026-08-30:
 "the requestor should be able to ask for reconsideration by amending
 request... you want the entire chain."

 A resubmission after TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED is a NEW
 ticket row, never a mutation of the old one — this row is immutable and the
 rest of the design is append-only for the reasons
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md gives. chain_id is what
 makes the several rows one conversation.

 SERVER-ASSIGNED, and the caller cannot supply it: CreateTicketRequest
 carries amends_ticket_id only, and the server copies the predecessor's
 chain_id. Only the FIRST ticket of a chain has chain_id == ticket_id.

 Not (spec.indexed): that option marks the COLLECTION KEY, which is
 ticket_id. "The entire chain" is ListTickets filtered by this field, the
 same shape routed_to_human_id already has, and it is a service-side filter
 over the collection read — see
 decisions/ticket-decision-chain-2026-08-30.md for the cost.

fields.name: amends_ticket_id
fields.description:
amends_ticket_id names the IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR, and is empty for the
 first ticket in a chain. It is kept alongside chain_id rather than instead
 of it because the two answer different questions: this one is "what did
 this ticket revise", chain_id is "what conversation is this", and reading
 the whole chain off chain_id is one filtered read instead of a walk.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, and the read half of the isolation
 pair this retrofit adds. Its twin is (spec.namespace) on the Create request
 above: that one binds the field to the caller's namespace claim on the way
 IN (stamp when empty, accept when equal, INVALID_ARGUMENT when different);
 this one is what the generated wrapper filters egress rows against on the
 way OUT, by EXACT string equality — never the level-or-below containment
 the administrative namespace rule uses, because "users and data always has
 to land in a leaf".

 A row that has to be dropped by that filter ABORTS THE PROCESS rather than
 failing the one call. Reaching it means kernel handed this service another
 tenant's row, which is a leak the filter exists to make impossible, and the
 decision record settles that a crash is the cheaper failure against it.

 Bounded like ScottyActivity.namespace, and deliberately NOT a query field:
 the field is the egress boundary, and a boundary a caller can name as a
 predicate is not one.

GetTicket is the REQUESTER-SAFE read: core, decisions and comments. It does
 NOT return advice, and that is §3's rule made structural — "Joe sees the
 decision and Dennis's comment. Not the advice. Otherwise Joe starts
 managing his relationship with his boss's assistant."

 Entitled as well as structural: only a PARTICIPANT of the ticket — the
 requester who opened it or the decider it is routed to — may call it at
 all. Advice lives behind a different RPC AND that RPC refuses Joe.

 It used to be the one read in this service that WROTE, because it recorded
 a HUMAN_VIEWED receipt. That receipt is messaging's now, so this is an
 ordinary read again.

 tickets they opened, the decisions and comments recorded against those
 tickets, and the immutable ARTIFACT rows those writes left behind. It is an

BrokerScottyMcpSession carries one Model Context Protocol session for Scotty over a
 single bidirectional stream: one complete JSON-RPC frame per stream message,
 request frames in and response frames out, for the life of the session.

enums.name: SkillClassification
enums.description: SkillClassification is the confirmed skilled/unskilled axis.

values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_UNSPECIFIED
values.description:
Unspecified is the proto3 zero value and is never stored; the service
 rejects it, so a caller that omits skill gets an error rather than a Human
 whose access model is undefined.

values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_SKILLED
values.description: SKILLED: interfaces with the system directly.

values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_UNSKILLED
values.description: UNSKILLED: rolls up through whoever they are working under.

enums.name: BusinessHoursSource
enums.description:
BusinessHoursSource names which of the two layers produced a BusinessHours.
 It is the field that keeps a guess from being read as a finding.

values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_PRIOR
values.description: PRIOR: an industry+geography default. No activity data went into it.

values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_OBSERVED
values.description: OBSERVED: refined from this person's own recorded activity.

enums.name: Weekday
enums.description:
Weekday is the ISO numbering, Monday = 1. Named here rather than borrowed
 because nothing in the platform proto set carries one.

enums.name: CredentialType
enums.description: CredentialType is the reliability class, per feature-ideas.md's refinement.

values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_STATE_LICENSE
values.description:
A state occupational licence (electrical, plumbing) — tied to permitting
 and code inspection.

values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_INDUSTRY_CERT
values.description:
An industry certification (AWS, NCCER) — how welding and heavy equipment
 operation are actually governed.

values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_COMPANY_ASSERTED
values.description:
The company's own judgement about autonomy/experience, with no papers
 behind it.

enums.name: IdentityProvider
enums.description:
IdentityProvider names the external IdP. Only the two the architecture sketch
 actually settles are listed; a third is a real decision (which broker, which
 consent flow) and not a proto edit made in passing.

enums.name: PolicyWeight
enums.description:
PolicyWeight is §2's settled three-way weight.

 Note what weight is NOT: it never carries security. "A policy can never carry
 security weight. If something genuinely must not happen, it is an
 entitlement." Even STATUTORY here is a statement about overridability of the
 POLICY, not a server-side refusal of an action.

values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_SOFT
values.description: Soft — push back once, capture the reason, comply, notify.

values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_HEAVY
values.description:
Heavy — override requires SOMEONE ELSE's entitlement; the actor cannot
 self-clear.

values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY
values.description:
Statutory — not overridable in-system by anyone. Ships with the product as
 trade knowledge: "Dennis shouldn't have to know to write the 811 policy."

enums.name: TicketDecisionOutcome
enums.description:
TicketDecisionOutcome is the decider's conclusion. Jody, 2026-08-30:
 "request approval is more than authorized/denied. There needs to be enums
 such as 'considering', 'amend', etc..."

 Three values, and all three are TERMINAL for the ticket they are recorded
 against — so the schematic looper's decisions/ticket-status-derived-not-stored.md's rule is
 untouched: a ticket is decided iff ANY decision row exists for it. This adds
 a third possible conclusion, not a lifecycle state.

 CONSIDERING is DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and that is settled rather than open:
 Jody confirmed on 2026-08-30 that it is not an enum value. "Considering" is
 the interval in which no decision row exists, which the design already
 represents by absence.

values.name: TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED
values.description:
AMEND_REQUESTED: this ask, as written, is not being granted, and the
 decider is inviting a revised one. The requester answers it by opening a
 new ticket with amends_ticket_id set to this one, which carries the chain
 forward. Tag 3 is NEW — 1 and 2 keep their wire values.

enums.name: ScottyEntityKind
enums.description: ScottyEntityKind names which knowledge type an artifact is about.

values.name: SCOTTY_ENTITY_KIND_TICKET_CHAIN
values.description:
A TICKET_CHAIN artifact is left ONCE per chain, on the hop that reaches
 Config.max_chain_hops — the moment Scotty stops mediating. entity_id is the
 chain_id. It records that AI mediation hit its limit, which is a thing that
 was DONE and therefore belongs in the auditor's store; no ticket is decided
 by it.

enums.name: ComparisonOp
enums.description: Collection query types (auto-injected)

services.name: Scotty
services.description:
Scotty is user-facing: it accepts user tokens minted from a browser login.

 EVERY write verb here is Create. That is not a naming accident — it is the
 immutability model expressed in the RPC set. There is no Update or Delete
 anywhere in this service, so "immutable core, appendable records, sealed
 advice" has no mutation path to have to guard.

 The RPC verb registry is CLOSED (tacplus/pkg/internal/common/verbs/
 registry.json), which is why the design record's vocabulary — open, advise,

types.name: AgentCursor
types.description:
AgentCursor is one row per user: everything a cycle needs to know about what
 the previous cycle did. It lives in KERNEL STATE, and that placement is a
 deliberate departure from the design record's "all of Scotty's state is a
 Stratum record" — written up in workers/big8-p1-scotty-agent-questions.md §1
 rather than made silently. The three reasons, briefly:

   - The design record's own requirement is that a write "must be visible to
     the very next cycle even if it runs moments later on a different
     instance". A record reaches Stratum through an EventBus publish and an
     asynchronous ingest; kernel state is CRUD and is visible on the next
     read. The lock provides atomicity; it cannot provide visibility through
     an async pipe.
   - There is no s2s read path back out of the record plane for an ordinary
     service today: the plane's s2s half is authorized to the record store
     itself and to nobody else (the superseded shared `query` trait; it named
     the since-deleted `argus` until 2026-09-01, and phase 2 item 10 cannot
     delete the trait until the per-service own-record client exists).
   - An s2s publish is stamped with the PUBLISHING SERVICE's namespace, not
     the user's (workers/big8-p1-messaging-questions.md §1), so a per-user row
     written that way is a row no user can read.

 What DOES stay a record is the cycle history — AgentCycle below — which is
 append-shaped, does not need read-back by this service, and is what the
 design record's user-facing "Bird's Eye View" reads through the generated
 c2s record query plane.

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is the principal this cursor belongs to and the collection key.

 For a message-triggered cycle it is messaging.Message.recipient — the
 ADDRESSEE, not the sender: the loop that wakes is the recipient's agent.

fields.name: cycles_completed
fields.description:
cycles_completed counts the loop cycles that have finished for this user.
 Monotonic, and the source of AgentCycle.cycle below.

fields.name: last_fencing_token
fields.description:
last_fencing_token is THE FENCE, and it is what makes the lock a fencing
 lock rather than a mutex.

 A fencing token is kernel's Raft log index of the granting Acquire:
 strictly increasing over every grant of every key, never reused. A resource
 owner stores the highest token it has seen and REJECTS a write carrying a
 lower one — that, not the lock, is what makes a paused or partitioned stale
 holder safe. This field is that stored highest-seen value, and this service
 is the resource owner doing the comparing (see service.rs `write_cursor`).

 Without it, a holder that stalled long enough for its lease to lapse could
 wake up and overwrite the cursor a newer holder had already advanced. The
 lock alone narrows that window; it does not close it.

fields.name: last_cycle_at_ms
fields.description: last_cycle_at_ms is when the last completed cycle finished.

fields.name: last_instance_id
fields.description:
last_instance_id is the instance that ran it. Recorded because consecutive
 cycles for one user legitimately run on different instances and "which pod
 was that" is otherwise unanswerable after the fact — NOT because anything
 routes on it. Nothing reads this field to make a decision.

fields.name: last_wake
fields.description: last_wake is the last event that woke a cycle for this user.

message.name: WakeEvent
message.description:
WakeEvent is ONE thing that woke the loop. A cycle carries every event it
 aggregated, not just the first, so "why did you wake" has a complete answer
 even when several arrived at once.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason is the trigger kind.

enum_values.name: WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A messaging.Message arrived on this user's EventBus queue and this
 instance's consumer group took it.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the specific event. For WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE it is the
 messaging.Message's delivery_id — the record key of the one delivery this
 wake is for, not the message_id it shares with its siblings, because the
 delivery is what this consumer group consumed.

fields.name: observed_at_ms
fields.description: observed_at_ms is when this instance took the event off the queue.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by exact string equality against the
 reader's namespace claim.

 (spec.store_namespace) here generates the READ-side egress filter on every
 surface that returns this row — including the MCP dispatch, which resolves
 the caller's claim itself, holds each returned row to it, and ABORTS THE
 PROCESS on a row it would otherwise have to drop. That abort is the
 designed behaviour for a genuine tenant violation, not a bug.

 WHERE THE VALUE COMES FROM, stated because it is the weak link and hiding
 it would be worse. An event-driven cycle has NO CALLER: nothing
 authenticated this work, so there is no verified claim to stamp from. The
 only tenant signal available is the consumed messaging.Message's own
 `namespace`, and this service copies that. That value is itself stamped by
 eventbus from MESSAGING'S service token rather than from the sender's
 (workers/big8-p1-messaging-questions.md §1, a fleet-wide open gap), so it
 is the right FIELD carrying a value whose provenance is not yet what the
 design intends. Copying it is still correct: it is the only tenant fact the
 event carries, and the moment tacplus grows a delegated s2s publish the
 value becomes the sender's with no change here.

 Not a query field: the field exists to BE the egress boundary, and a
 boundary a caller can predicate on is not one.

types.name: AgentCycle
types.description:
AgentCycle is one completed loop cycle: what woke it, when, on which
 instance, under which fencing token.

 It is the durable history the design record calls the "Bird's Eye View" —
 "an ordinary generated read surface on that record — no new mechanism". This
 file therefore declares no read RPC for it: the c2s record query plane
 generated from (spec.store_principal) and the query fields below IS that
 surface, and hand-writing a second one would be the drift the typed-contract
 argument exists to prevent.

 Append-shaped by construction: the key carries the cycle number, so a cycle
 is a new row and no cycle ever rewrites another.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 AgentCycleBus with topic ref scottyagent.AgentCycleBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: cycle_id
fields.description: cycle_id is the record key: "<user>/<cycle>".

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is whose agent ran, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL.

 (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's reads of this record to
 their own rows on the c2s query plane, and it is the reason the Bird's Eye
 View needs no filtering code: "my cycles" is the only query the plane will
 answer. `spiffe_id` below is the record's declared owner but holds THIS
 SERVICE's identity (eventbus stamps the publisher), so filtering on that
 would show every user nothing.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the filter into the plane's size-only
 RPCs, which return a number over the handle's predicate and no rows for an
 egress filter to narrow.

fields.name: cycle
fields.description: cycle is this user's monotonic cycle number, the second half of cycle_id.

fields.name: fencing_token
fields.description:
fencing_token is the kernel.FencedLock token this cycle ran under. Carried
 onto the row so the history itself shows the fence: cycles for one user
 must appear in strictly increasing token order, and a row that does not is
 visible evidence of a stale holder that got through.

fields.name: woke_for
fields.description:
woke_for is EVERY event this cycle aggregated, in the order they were
 observed — not just the one that started it. That is the aggregation the
 design record asks for, made legible: "multiple events can land within one
 loop cycle; they are aggregated and processed together".

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_events_per_cycle's ceiling.

message.name: WakeEvent
message.description:
WakeEvent is ONE thing that woke the loop. A cycle carries every event it
 aggregated, not just the first, so "why did you wake" has a complete answer
 even when several arrived at once.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason is the trigger kind.

enum_values.name: WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A messaging.Message arrived on this user's EventBus queue and this
 instance's consumer group took it.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the specific event. For WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE it is the
 messaging.Message's delivery_id — the record key of the one delivery this
 wake is for, not the message_id it shares with its siblings, because the
 delivery is what this consumer group consumed.

fields.name: observed_at_ms
fields.description: observed_at_ms is when this instance took the event off the queue.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the business clock — when the cycle began, which is after
 the lock was granted. It is what retention measures age from, and the RANGE
 criterion because "what did my agent do last week" is the question the
 Bird's Eye View asks.

fields.name: finished_at_ms
fields.description: finished_at_ms is when it ended, before the release.

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id is the instance that ran the cycle. Provenance, not routing —
 see AgentCursor.last_instance_id.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The NAME IS LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off. It holds THIS SERVICE's identity,
 because the publish is s2s; `user` above is where the person is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT. MANDATORY on a (spec.record):
 tacplus's ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations fails generation for any
 record declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record nobody
 remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 Left EMPTY by this service on publish, on purpose. eventbus's
 PublishHandler stamps it from the publishing token's namespace claim and
 REFUSES the publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none —
 stamp-or-refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty, because a row published
 with an empty namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read. A
 value written here would be this service asserting a tenant nothing
 verified. (That the stamp is the SERVICE's namespace rather than the user's
 is the gap AgentCursor.namespace describes.)

Config
types.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: lock_acquire_attempts
fields.description:
lock_acquire_attempts bounds how many times a cycle retries a contended
 per-user lock before giving the record back to the queue.

 kernel.FencedLock.Acquire is NON-BLOCKING — a key held by a different
 holder returns granted=false rather than parking the call — so a contended
 acquire is a poll, and something has to bound the polling. Giving up is not
 a failure: the record has not been ACKed, so it is redelivered, and by then
 the instance that held the lock has finished the cycle that would have
 absorbed it anyway.

 Config rather than a constant for the same reason messaging's
 max_recipients is: contention is a property of the deployment, and changing
 it must not need a redeploy.

fields.name: lock_acquire_backoff_ms
fields.description: lock_acquire_backoff_ms is the wait between those attempts.

fields.name: max_events_per_cycle
fields.description:
max_events_per_cycle bounds the AGGREGATION. Multiple events landing for
 one user while a cycle is running are drained into that cycle rather than
 starting a cycle each — "they are aggregated and processed together rather
 than firing one loop per event", per the design record. This is the ceiling
 on one cycle's drain, so a burst cannot buy unbounded work with one lock
 hold; the remainder is picked up by the next cycle.

 It must not exceed AgentCycle.woke_for's assert_max_size (256), which is
 the hard edge on how many wake events one cycle row can record.

types.name: EventBusRecordMeta
ListMyAgentStateRequest
types.description:
ListMyAgentStateRequest carries NO caller identity a caller may set.

 `user` is the server-computed field §6's "any predicate that would scope
 results to a caller is computed server-side from the verified Caller and is
 NEVER an LLM-writable tool argument" names. It is the ordinary
 (spec.principal) marker, reused as-is: the generated MCP dispatch honours it
 the same way the gRPC wrapper does, and additionally OMITS it from the
 published tool schema and REFUSES a tool call that names it. "Scoped to me"
 is therefore not a filter the model is trusted to pass — it is a value the
 model cannot express.

 NO (spec.namespace) FIELD, for the same two reasons the ticketing MCP audit
 read carries none. The request-side marker's job is to bind a value the
 handler then STAMPS ONTO A ROW, and this rpc writes nothing; the tenant
 boundary it needs is on the READ side and is already generated from
 (spec.store_namespace) on AgentCursor, which the dispatch holds to the
 caller's claim by exact equality. And tacplus's own generated
 `<tool>_reaches_its_typed_handler` test builds a caller with a subject and no
 namespace claim, so an MCP request declaring (spec.namespace) fails its own
 generated test today — a reported tacplus gap
 (workers/big8-p1-ticketing-retrofit-questions.md §2), not the reason the
 field is absent, but it does mean nothing is lost by its absence.

types.name: ListMyAgentStateResponse
types.description:
ListMyAgentStateResponse carries the caller's own cursor row: exactly one when
 their agent has ever woken, none when it has not. An empty list is the
 complete answer to "has my agent ever run" and needs no companion bool.

 A LIST OF AT MOST ONE, and that is not stylistic. tacplus generates the
 (spec.store_namespace) egress backstop — resolve the caller's claim, hold
 every returned row to it by exact equality, std::process::abort on a row it
 would have to drop — only for REPEATED message fields whose item type carries
 the annotation (`namespaceListFields`, rust/types/namespace_gen.go:64: it
 skips any field that is not `IsRepeated`). A singular `AgentCursor cursor`
 field would have carried the annotation and generated NO backstop at all,
 silently. So the response shape is the one the control actually covers.

 The singular-field hole is a real generator gap, reported rather than only
 worked around here — see workers/big8-p1-scotty-agent-questions.md §3.

ScottyagentConfigState is the state boundary for scottyagent service configuration.
 Auto-injected by tacplus from (spec.grpc_config) annotation.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: lock_acquire_attempts
fields.description:
lock_acquire_attempts bounds how many times a cycle retries a contended
 per-user lock before giving the record back to the queue.

 kernel.FencedLock.Acquire is NON-BLOCKING — a key held by a different
 holder returns granted=false rather than parking the call — so a contended
 acquire is a poll, and something has to bound the polling. Giving up is not
 a failure: the record has not been ACKed, so it is redelivered, and by then
 the instance that held the lock has finished the cycle that would have
 absorbed it anyway.

 Config rather than a constant for the same reason messaging's
 max_recipients is: contention is a property of the deployment, and changing
 it must not need a redeploy.

fields.name: lock_acquire_backoff_ms
fields.description: lock_acquire_backoff_ms is the wait between those attempts.

fields.name: max_events_per_cycle
fields.description:
max_events_per_cycle bounds the AGGREGATION. Multiple events landing for
 one user while a cycle is running are drained into that cycle rather than
 starting a cycle each — "they are aggregated and processed together rather
 than firing one loop per event", per the design record. This is the ceiling
 on one cycle's drain, so a burst cannot buy unbounded work with one lock
 hold; the remainder is picked up by the next cycle.

 It must not exceed AgentCycle.woke_for's assert_max_size (256), which is
 the hard edge on how many wake events one cycle row can record.

 there is no dispatch-exclusivity lock and no ownership to record.

fields.description:
source_id identifies the specific event. For WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE it is the

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by exact string equality against the
 reader's namespace claim.

 (spec.store_namespace) here generates the READ-side egress filter on every
 surface that returns this row — including the MCP dispatch, which resolves
 the caller's claim itself, holds each returned row to it, and ABORTS THE
 PROCESS on a row it would otherwise have to drop. That abort is the
 designed behaviour for a genuine tenant violation, not a bug.

 WHERE THE VALUE COMES FROM, stated because it is the weak link and hiding
 it would be worse. An event-driven cycle has NO CALLER: nothing
 authenticated this work, so there is no verified claim to stamp from. The
 only tenant signal available is the consumed messaging.Message's own
 `namespace`, and this service copies that. That value is itself stamped by
 eventbus from MESSAGING'S service token rather than from the sender's
 (workers/big8-p1-messaging-questions.md §1, a fleet-wide open gap), so it
 is the right FIELD carrying a value whose provenance is not yet what the
 design intends. Copying it is still correct: it is the only tenant fact the
 event carries, and the moment tacplus grows a delegated s2s publish the
 value becomes the sender's with no change here.

 Not a query field: the field exists to BE the egress boundary, and a
 boundary a caller can predicate on is not one.

WakeReason names the trigger that produced one wake event. The agent is
 always told WHY it woke — that is the design record's phrasing, and it is why
 this is a typed field on the cycle rather than something inferred from which
 collection had a row.

 is not designed. A WAKE_REASON_SCHEDULED value is added by whoever builds it;

message.name: StateUpdated

 Emitted when entities are created, updated, or deleted via state services.
 Provides a coarse audit trail — "what changed" without the full payload.

message.name: Diagnostic
message.description:
Diagnostic is the freeform escape hatch for cases where no typed event
 exists yet. [ERROR]

 Use this sparingly. When a Diagnostic pattern emerges (same context, same
 kind of message), promote it to a typed event. Diagnostics are a migration
 path, not a permanent solution.

types.name: S2SCredPair
types.description:
S2SCredPair authenticates a service bootstrapping its identity (S2S). It
 confers the set of services the bootstrapped token may act as / call,
 formalizing service bootstrap delegate cred_pairs.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: DiskPersistenceConfig

DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that

fields.name: group

compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
