PackageNode is a node in the hierarchical registry tree.
 The root node represents the tacplus build; children are proto packages
 (sys/, services/, common/, utils/). Each node carries its own types,
 RPCs, and boundaries and recursively contains sub-packages.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the short package name (e.g. "identity", "spec", "sys").

fields.name: full_path
fields.description: full_path is the slash-separated path from the root (e.g. "services/identity").

fields.name: children
fields.description: children are sub-packages contained in this node.

fields.name: types
fields.description: types are the message type descriptors defined in this package.

message.name: TypeInfo
message.description: TypeInfo describes a protobuf message type in the generated registry.

message.name: FieldInfo
message.description: FieldInfo describes a field in type metadata.

message.name: EnumValueInfo
message.description: EnumValueInfo describes a single enum value in type metadata.

fields.name: projection_source
fields.description:
projection source path from (spec.projection_source), e.g. "agent_id" or "tool_use.tool_name".
 Maps a projection field to a field path on the source event message.

fields.name: timeseries_order_key
fields.description:
Position in the store-neutral sort-key role from (spec.timeseries_column).order_key
 (1-indexed, 0 = not a sort key).

fields.name: timeseries_partition_key
fields.description:
True when this column is part of the store-neutral partition role from
 (spec.timeseries_column).partition_key.

fields.name: oneof
fields.description: True when this field is a member of a protobuf oneof group.

fields.name: oneof_name
fields.description: Name of the protobuf oneof group when oneof is true.

fields.name: store_key
fields.description: True when this field is the key field for a service_store message.

fields.name: quorum_write
fields.description: True when writes involving this field require quorum acknowledgement.

fields.name: constraint_infos
fields.description: Machine-readable constraints derived from proto annotations and defaults.

message.name: FieldConstraintInfo
message.description: FieldConstraintInfo describes one machine-readable validation constraint.

fields.name: rule
fields.description: rule is the source annotation or derived rule name, e.g. assert_max_size.

fields.name: target
fields.description: target identifies what the rule constrains: field, element, key, or value.

fields.name: value_kind
fields.description: value_kind is bool, int, float, string, enum, int_list, or float_list.

fields.name: operator
fields.description:
operator carries comparisons such as gt, ge, lt, le, eq, ne, in, not_in,
 or multiple_of for compound numeric annotations.

fields.name: defaulted
fields.description: defaulted is true for compiler-provided default bounds.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: unit is bytes, elements, entries, or another rule-specific unit.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is annotation or default_bound.

fields.name: timeseries_cardinality_hint
fields.description:
Store-neutral distinct-value hint from (spec.timeseries_column).cardinality_hint.
 (Field 25, the spec's suggested number, is already taken by `oneof`.)

fields.name: data_entitlement_mode
fields.description:
data-entitlement mode for this field, from (spec.redact) or inherited from the
 message-level (spec.data_entitlement) default: DROP / PSEUDONYMIZE /
 MAY_REDACT / MAY_ANONYMIZE. UNSPECIFIED = not annotated (never transformed).
 This field's wire number is the field id reported in the sanitize
 redacted-id set and checked by the data-entitlement drift guard.

fields.name: filter_mode
fields.description:
filter_mode is the field's RecordMap filterability, from (spec.query_field).op:
 EQ  -> the generated <T>Filter carries `optional <type> <name>`;
 RANGE -> it carries `optional <type> <name>_from` + `optional <type> <name>_to`.
 UNSPECIFIED = the field carries no (spec.query_field) and is NOT filterable — a
 record type whose fields are all UNSPECIFIED gets no <T>Filter message at all.

fields.name: timeseries_table_name
fields.description: Timeseries table name from (spec.timeseries_type).name or snake_case of message name.

fields.name: timeseries_table_source
fields.description: Source event FQN from (spec.timeseries_type).source.

fields.name: record_key
fields.description: record_key from (spec.record).key. Event unique identifier field.

fields.name: record_owner
fields.description: record_owner from (spec.record).owner. Event owner/identity field.

fields.name: transformations
fields.description: transformations from (spec.transformation). Derived row types to generate.

message.name: TransformationInfo
message.description:
TransformationInfo describes a derived row type produced by a pure typed
 conversion of a source message. Store-neutral: dedup and cardinality_hint are
 semantic intent, not backend DDL. It carries NO retention — retention is
 delivery-side state and lives on TypeInfo.record_retention.

message.name: TransformationFieldInfo
message.description: TransformationFieldInfo describes a single field in a transformation.

message.name: DedupPolicyInfo
message.description:
DedupPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.DedupPolicy — the store-neutral
 row identity + duplicate-resolution policy. A downstream materializer maps this
 onto an engine's merge/dedup mechanism.

fields.name: service_store
fields.description: True when this message is annotated as a durable service_store value.

fields.name: service_store_name
fields.description: Durable service_store name. Defaults to the protobuf message name.

fields.name: service_store_label
fields.description: Hosting service labels from (spec.service_store).label.

fields.name: timeseries_dedup
fields.description:
now lives on record_retention (from (spec.record).retention),
 never on a transformation or its compile target. 2026-08-25.
 Store-neutral dedup policy for a standalone (spec.timeseries_type) table, from
 its .dedup. Unset = append-only (no dedup) — the standalone-table default.

fields.name: data_entitlement_default
fields.description:
Message-level data-entitlement default from (spec.data_entitlement): the
 default transform applied to this message's eligible fields, overridden per
 field by (spec.redact). UNSPECIFIED = no message-level default.

fields.name: record_retention
fields.description:
record_retention from (spec.record).retention: the store-neutral row
 retention policy for this record's stored rows. Unset = indefinite.
 Retention is DELIVERY-side state — a transformation is a pure conversion and
 carries none.

message.name: RetentionPolicyInfo
message.description:
RetentionPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.RetentionPolicy — the
 store-neutral row retention policy. A downstream materializer renders this
 into an engine-specific TTL/eviction rule.

fields.name: rpcs
fields.description: rpcs are the RPC descriptors defined in this package.

message.name: RpcInfo
message.description: RpcInfo describes a protobuf RPC in the generated registry.

fields.name: service
fields.description:
Owning service as the project-specific ServiceName enum — a placeholder
 populated downstream (SERVICE_NAME_UNSPECIFIED in the base registry); use
 service_name (field 2) for the name tacplus emits.

fields.name: grpc_path
fields.description: Full gRPC method path, e.g. "/policy.PolicyService/GetApiCatalog".

fields.name: http_path
fields.description:
HTTP REST convention path, e.g. "/api/v1/identity/IdentityService/ListProviders".
 Always present for gateway-exposed RPCs: {REST_ROOT_PATH}/{package}/{Service}/{MethodName}.
 The service segment mirrors the gRPC + entitlement-grant identity so routes
 stay collision-free when a package hosts multiple services sharing a method.

fields.name: http_methods
fields.description:
HTTP methods for REST access. POST is always present for convention routes.
 Additional methods come from spec.rest_method (e.g. ["POST", "GET"]).

fields.name: http_alias_path
fields.description:
HTTP alias path from spec.rest_path, relative to REST_ROOT_PATH.
 When present, creates an additional route (e.g. "/api/v1/.well-known/openid-configuration").
 Same http_methods apply to the alias.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description: Auth policy — inherited from service-level annotation.

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description:
auth_model: "s2s" (service-to-service), "c2s" (client-to-service),
 or "c2d" (client-to-daemon local IPC).

fields.name: collection_mode
fields.description:
method_collection (collection-returning read) — see docs/API.md.
 collection_mode is "SNAPSHOT" | "WATCH" | "PAGE"; empty when the RPC is not
 a collection read. The remaining fields are the declared bounds.

fields.name: collection_default_page_size
fields.description:
PAGE keyset default page size when the request omits a limit (0 on
 SNAPSHOT/WATCH). The wrapper bounds an explicit limit to collection_max_items.

fields.name: rpc_verb
fields.description:
Governed RPC classification derived from the method name and streaming /
 collection shape. Empty when the method does not yet classify cleanly.

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
Namespace authorization metadata. These fields expose the same level-or-below
 decision inputs that generated authorizers enforce at runtime.

fields.name: verb_status
fields.description: verb_status is "classified", "unclassified", or "exempt".

fields.name: folded_to_verb
fields.description: folded_to_verb is the canonical verb for a rejected leading synonym, when known.

fields.name: surfaces
fields.description:
surfaces lists every generated transport/auth surface for this RPC. This
 includes derived W2S gRPC-over-REST exposure when a C2S RPC has REST route
 metadata.

message.name: RpcSurfaceInfo
message.description: RpcSurfaceInfo describes one transport/auth surface for an RPC.

fields.name: surface_kind
fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", "c2d", or "w2s".

fields.name: transport
fields.description: transport is "grpc", "grpc_over_rest", or "unix".

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description: auth_model is the auth model enforced on this surface.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when the rpc declares principal RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP: it is an MCP
 tool, not a gRPC call. The tool's description is the `description` field
 (field 8) — the rpc's own doc comment — so there is no second description
 here to drift from it.

fields.name: mcp_tool_name
fields.description:
mcp_tool_name is the tool name this rpc is published under: the RPC name in
 snake_case, or the spec.rpc mcp_tool_name override when one is declared.
 Empty unless mcp is true.

fields.name: mcp_session_carrier
fields.description:
mcp_session_carrier is true for the one rpc per MCP-hosting service that
 tacplus generates rather than the author declaring: the bidirectional
 session over which MCP JSON-RPC frames reach that service's tools. Its
 exposure is the owning ServiceInfo.mcp_exposure. Mutually exclusive with
 `mcp` — the carrier is the transport, not a tool.

fields.name: boundaries
fields.description: boundaries are the state boundaries owned by this package's service.

message.name: BoundaryInfo
message.description:
BoundaryInfo describes a state boundary in a tacplus build.
 This is language-neutral metadata exposed by generated registry code.

fields.name: service
fields.description:
Owning service, as the project-specific ServiceName enum. Like
 RpcInfo.service, this is a placeholder POPULATED DOWNSTREAM once the full
 ServiceName enum is generated into generated/services.proto — it is
 SERVICE_NAME_UNSPECIFIED in the base registry tacplus emits (the base enum has
 only UNSPECIFIED/ANY). For the owning-service identifier tacplus actually
 emits, use `label` (field 15), the service_state routing labels.

fields.name: state_root
fields.description: State root message name, e.g. "ClusterState".

fields.name: boundary
fields.description: Boundary field name, e.g. "ClusterInfo".

fields.name: persistence
fields.description: True when the boundary is persisted.

fields.name: collection
fields.description: True when the boundary is a collection (repeated field).

fields.name: type_fqn
fields.description: Fully qualified type name of the boundary message.

fields.name: boundary_callers
fields.description: Cross-namespace callers allowed on this boundary field.

fields.name: rpcs
fields.description: RPCs that operate on this boundary (derived from naming convention).

fields.name: is_config
fields.description: True when this boundary is a configuration boundary (ConfigState pattern).

fields.name: label
fields.description:
Routing labels from the service_state annotation (e.g., ["state-store"],
 ["kernel", "edge"]).

fields.name: graph_type
fields.description:
Graph type of this boundary: "singleton", "collection", "topic",
 "queue", "priority_queue", "command", "view", "state_import", "private".

fields.name: auto_tls_key_type
fields.description:
auto_tls_key_type is the key algorithm when auto_tls is enabled ("ed25519" or "ecdsa").
 Empty means auto_tls is disabled.

fields.name: collected_health
fields.description: True when this boundary is marked for Sentinel health collection.

fields.name: docs
fields.description:
docs is a map of documentation file name → content.
 Populated on the root node only; contains embedded project documentation.

fields.name: schema
fields.description:
schema describes the structure of this document for self-reference.
 Populated on the root node only; points readers to the type definitions
 under sys/tacplus that define PackageNode, TypeInfo, FieldInfo, RpcInfo,
 BoundaryInfo, and EnumValueInfo.

fields.name: enums
fields.description: enums are the top-level enum definitions in this package.

message.name: EnumInfo
message.description: EnumInfo describes a top-level protobuf enum definition.

fields.name: services
fields.description: services are first-class service descriptors (populated on leaf nodes with RPCs).

message.name: ServiceInfo
message.description: ServiceInfo describes a gRPC service as a first-class object.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Service name, e.g. "PolicyService".

fields.name: description
fields.description: Human-readable description from proto comments.

fields.name: package
fields.description: Proto package this service belongs to.

fields.name: grpc_service
fields.description: Full gRPC service path, e.g. "policy.PolicyService".

fields.name: rpcs
fields.description: RPCs defined on this service.

fields.name: boundaries
fields.description: Boundary names owned by this service's state root.

fields.name: event_label
fields.description: event_label is the routing label for gateway-exposed event services.

fields.name: smb
fields.description:
smb marks a Service Mesh Blackbox service: its own instances talk over a
 black-box peer protocol within a single cluster (SPIFFE
 plan D7). Consumers read this from the registry, not proto text, to drive
 the per-SMB CA + member-cert wiring.

fields.name: smb_authority
fields.description:
smb_authority marks the consumer service designated to issue per-SMB CAs +
 member certs for smb services (SPIFFE plan D7). Read from the registry so an
 SMB service / its tooling can resolve which service to obtain its CA + cert
 from. tacplus does not implement the authority.

fields.name: smb_root
fields.description:
smb_root is present when smb is true and records the trust profile selected
 by spec.smb. SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED is the default; SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER requests a
 per-SMB intermediate rooted in the cluster CA.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

fields.name: host_label
fields.description: host_label is the service_s2s label for hosted vservice RPC surfaces.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when at least one of this service's rpcs declares principal
 RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP. That fact alone is what decides whether the service gets
 the generated session-carrying MCP transport; it is never declared.

fields.name: mcp_exposure
fields.description:
mcp_exposure is the derived exposure of that generated carrier: the
 most-permissive (union) exposure of this service's MCP rpcs, so one EXTERNAL
 tool makes the carrier reachable from outside to serve it. Meaningless
 unless mcp is true.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL: reachable only from inside the cluster boundary.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL: reachable from outside the cluster boundary.

fields.name: build
fields.description: build contains version and build metadata. Populated on the root node only.

message.name: BuildInfo
message.description: BuildInfo contains version and build metadata for the registry.

fields.name: tacplus_version
fields.description: tacplus version that generated this registry.

fields.name: build_timestamp
fields.description: Timestamp when the registry was generated (RFC 3339).

fields.name: source_git_sha
fields.description: Git SHA of the source proto directory, if available.

fields.name: subscriptions
fields.description:
subscriptions are event-bus topic subscriptions declared on state roots
 in this package (from spec.subscribe annotations).

message.name: SubscriptionInfo
message.description:
SubscriptionInfo describes an event-bus topic subscription declared
 via (spec.subscribe) on a service_state message.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is the original annotation value, e.g. "aegis.AegisState.event_stream".

fields.name: source_package
fields.description: source_package is the proto package of the source state root, e.g. "aegis".

fields.name: source_state_root
fields.description: source_state_root is the state root message name, e.g. "AegisState".

fields.name: source_field
fields.description: source_field is the topic field name, e.g. "event_stream".

fields.name: source_type_fqn
fields.description:
source_type_fqn is the fully-qualified proto type of the topic message,
 e.g. "aegis.TopologyEvent".

fields.name: constants
fields.description:
constants are file-level named constants (string, int, float, bool)
 defined via spec.string_const, spec.int_const, etc.
 Key is the constant name, value is the constant value as a string.

fields.name: entitlement_grants

message.name: EntitlementGrantInfo
message.description:
EntitlementGrantInfo describes one generated entitlement grant token.
 Exact grants name a package + service + RPC. Wildcard grants name a package
 plus a capability scope and expand to the exact grant tokens they cover.

fields.name: token
fields.description:
token is the stable flattened grant token, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC,
 PACKAGE_ANY, or PACKAGE_READ_ANY.

fields.name: package
fields.description: package is the proto package/capability namespace this grant belongs to.

fields.name: service_name
fields.description: service_name is set for exact grants.

fields.name: rpc
fields.description: rpc is set for exact grants.

fields.name: capability_scope
fields.description:
capability_scope is set for wildcard grants: ANY, READ, WRITE, WATCH,
 PAGE, AGENT, or another generated capability scope.

fields.name: expands_to
fields.description:
expands_to lists exact grant tokens implied by a wildcard grant.
 Exact grants leave this empty.

fields.name: routing_alias_packages
fields.description:
routing_alias_packages lists physical routing-alias packages this exact
 grant's (service, rpc) is also reachable under, e.g. an EventBus-hosted
 C2S publish RPC declared in package "tasks" is physically dialed via
 package "eventbus". A token audience-scoped to one of these packages
 should still keep this grant: the alias names the physical dial target,
 not the entitlement contract, which stays this grant's own package.
 Wildcard grants leave this empty.

fields.name: proto_packages
fields.description:
proto_packages are the declared protobuf package names represented by this
 leaf node. Present on leaf nodes so consumers do not infer package identity
 from registry directory names.

fields.name: vservices
fields.description:

message.description: VServiceInfo describes a file-level virtual service identity.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Virtual service identity name from spec.vservice.name.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable field id from spec.vservice.id.

fields.name: package
fields.description: Proto package that declares this vservice.

fields.name: client_dependencies
fields.description:

message.name: ClientDependencyInfo
message.description: ClientDependencyInfo describes a file-level declared gRPC client dependency.

fields.name: source_package
fields.description: source_package is the proto package that declares the dependency.

fields.name: surface_kind
fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", or "w2s".

fields.name: service
fields.description: service is the declared target service ref, usually "package.ServiceName".

fields.name: target_package
fields.description: target_package is parsed from service when service is package-qualified.

fields.name: target_service
fields.description: target_service is parsed from service when service is package-qualified.

fields.name: wildcard
fields.description: wildcard is true for spec.all_grpc_s2s_clients.

fields.name: event_publishes
fields.description: event_publishes are validated event_publish bindings declared in this leaf.

message.name: EventPublishInfo
message.description: EventPublishInfo describes an event_publish binding declared by an actor.

fields.name: event_watches
fields.description: event_watches are validated event_watch bindings declared in this leaf.

message.name: EventWatchInfo
message.description: EventWatchInfo describes an event_watch binding declared by an actor.

auth_model: "s2s" (service-to-service), "c2s" (client-to-service),
 or "c2d" (client-to-daemon local IPC).

fields.name: collection_mode
fields.description:
method_collection (collection-returning read) — see docs/API.md.
 collection_mode is "SNAPSHOT" | "WATCH" | "PAGE"; empty when the RPC is not
 a collection read. The remaining fields are the declared bounds.

fields.name: collection_default_page_size
fields.description:
PAGE keyset default page size when the request omits a limit (0 on
 SNAPSHOT/WATCH). The wrapper bounds an explicit limit to collection_max_items.

fields.name: rpc_verb
fields.description:
Governed RPC classification derived from the method name and streaming /
 collection shape. Empty when the method does not yet classify cleanly.

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
Namespace authorization metadata. These fields expose the same level-or-below
 decision inputs that generated authorizers enforce at runtime.

fields.name: verb_status
fields.description: verb_status is "classified", "unclassified", or "exempt".

fields.name: folded_to_verb
fields.description: folded_to_verb is the canonical verb for a rejected leading synonym, when known.

fields.name: surfaces
fields.description:
surfaces lists every generated transport/auth surface for this RPC. This
 includes derived W2S gRPC-over-REST exposure when a C2S RPC has REST route
 metadata.

message.name: RpcSurfaceInfo
message.description: RpcSurfaceInfo describes one transport/auth surface for an RPC.

fields.name: surface_kind
fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", "c2d", or "w2s".

fields.name: transport
fields.description: transport is "grpc", "grpc_over_rest", or "unix".

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description: auth_model is the auth model enforced on this surface.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when the rpc declares principal RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP: it is an MCP
 tool, not a gRPC call. The tool's description is the `description` field
 (field 8) — the rpc's own doc comment — so there is no second description
 here to drift from it.

fields.name: mcp_tool_name
fields.description:
mcp_tool_name is the tool name this rpc is published under: the RPC name in
 snake_case, or the spec.rpc mcp_tool_name override when one is declared.
 Empty unless mcp is true.

fields.name: mcp_session_carrier
fields.description:
mcp_session_carrier is true for the one rpc per MCP-hosting service that
 tacplus generates rather than the author declaring: the bidirectional
 session over which MCP JSON-RPC frames reach that service's tools. Its
 exposure is the owning ServiceInfo.mcp_exposure. Mutually exclusive with
 `mcp` — the carrier is the transport, not a tool.

fields.name: boundaries
fields.description: Boundary names owned by this service's state root.

fields.name: event_label
fields.description: event_label is the routing label for gateway-exposed event services.

fields.name: smb
fields.description:
smb marks a Service Mesh Blackbox service: its own instances talk over a
 black-box peer protocol within a single cluster (SPIFFE
 plan D7). Consumers read this from the registry, not proto text, to drive
 the per-SMB CA + member-cert wiring.

fields.name: smb_authority
fields.description:
smb_authority marks the consumer service designated to issue per-SMB CAs +
 member certs for smb services (SPIFFE plan D7). Read from the registry so an
 SMB service / its tooling can resolve which service to obtain its CA + cert
 from. tacplus does not implement the authority.

fields.name: smb_root
fields.description:
smb_root is present when smb is true and records the trust profile selected
 by spec.smb. SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED is the default; SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER requests a
 per-SMB intermediate rooted in the cluster CA.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

fields.name: host_label
fields.description: host_label is the service_s2s label for hosted vservice RPC surfaces.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when at least one of this service's rpcs declares principal
 RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP. That fact alone is what decides whether the service gets
 the generated session-carrying MCP transport; it is never declared.

fields.name: mcp_exposure
fields.description:
mcp_exposure is the derived exposure of that generated carrier: the
 most-permissive (union) exposure of this service's MCP rpcs, so one EXTERNAL
 tool makes the carrier reachable from outside to serve it. Meaningless
 unless mcp is true.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL: reachable only from inside the cluster boundary.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL: reachable from outside the cluster boundary.

types.name: SubscriptionInfo

SubscriptionInfo describes an event-bus topic subscription declared

types.name: TransformationInfo
types.description:
TransformationInfo describes a derived row type produced by a pure typed
 conversion of a source message. Store-neutral: dedup and cardinality_hint are
 semantic intent, not backend DDL. It carries NO retention — retention is
 delivery-side state and lives on TypeInfo.record_retention.

message.name: TransformationFieldInfo

message.name: DedupPolicyInfo

DedupPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.DedupPolicy — the store-neutral
 row identity + duplicate-resolution policy. A downstream materializer maps this
 onto an engine's merge/dedup mechanism.

message.name: FieldInfo

message.name: EnumValueInfo

projection source path from (spec.projection_source), e.g. "agent_id" or "tool_use.tool_name".
 Maps a projection field to a field path on the source event message.

fields.name: timeseries_order_key
fields.description:
Position in the store-neutral sort-key role from (spec.timeseries_column).order_key

fields.name: timeseries_partition_key
fields.description:
True when this column is part of the store-neutral partition role from
 (spec.timeseries_column).partition_key.

fields.name: oneof
fields.description: True when this field is a member of a protobuf oneof group.

fields.name: oneof_name
fields.description: Name of the protobuf oneof group when oneof is true.

fields.name: store_key
fields.description: True when this field is the key field for a service_store message.

fields.name: quorum_write
fields.description: True when writes involving this field require quorum acknowledgement.

fields.name: constraint_infos
fields.description: Machine-readable constraints derived from proto annotations and defaults.

message.name: FieldConstraintInfo
message.description: FieldConstraintInfo describes one machine-readable validation constraint.

fields.name: rule
fields.description: rule is the source annotation or derived rule name, e.g. assert_max_size.

fields.name: target
fields.description: target identifies what the rule constrains: field, element, key, or value.

fields.name: value_kind
fields.description: value_kind is bool, int, float, string, enum, int_list, or float_list.

fields.name: operator
fields.description:
operator carries comparisons such as gt, ge, lt, le, eq, ne, in, not_in,
 or multiple_of for compound numeric annotations.

fields.name: defaulted
fields.description: defaulted is true for compiler-provided default bounds.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: unit is bytes, elements, entries, or another rule-specific unit.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is annotation or default_bound.

fields.name: timeseries_cardinality_hint
fields.description:
Store-neutral distinct-value hint from (spec.timeseries_column).cardinality_hint.
 (Field 25, the spec's suggested number, is already taken by `oneof`.)

fields.name: data_entitlement_mode
fields.description:
data-entitlement mode for this field, from (spec.redact) or inherited from the
 message-level (spec.data_entitlement) default: DROP / PSEUDONYMIZE /
 MAY_REDACT / MAY_ANONYMIZE. UNSPECIFIED = not annotated (never transformed).
 This field's wire number is the field id reported in the sanitize
 redacted-id set and checked by the data-entitlement drift guard.

fields.name: filter_mode
fields.description:
filter_mode is the field's RecordMap filterability, from (spec.query_field).op:
 EQ  -> the generated <T>Filter carries `optional <type> <name>`;
 RANGE -> it carries `optional <type> <name>_from` + `optional <type> <name>_to`.
 UNSPECIFIED = the field carries no (spec.query_field) and is NOT filterable — a
 record type whose fields are all UNSPECIFIED gets no <T>Filter message at all.

fields.description: Timeseries table name from (spec.timeseries_type).name or snake_case of message name.

fields.name: timeseries_table_source
fields.description: Source event FQN from (spec.timeseries_type).source.

fields.name: record_key
fields.description: record_key from (spec.record).key. Event unique identifier field.

fields.name: record_owner
fields.description: record_owner from (spec.record).owner. Event owner/identity field.

fields.name: transformations
fields.description: transformations from (spec.transformation). Derived row types to generate.

message.name: TransformationInfo
message.description:
TransformationInfo describes a derived row type produced by a pure typed
 conversion of a source message. Store-neutral: dedup and cardinality_hint are
 semantic intent, not backend DDL. It carries NO retention — retention is
 delivery-side state and lives on TypeInfo.record_retention.

message.name: TransformationFieldInfo

message.name: DedupPolicyInfo
message.description:
DedupPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.DedupPolicy — the store-neutral
 row identity + duplicate-resolution policy. A downstream materializer maps this
 onto an engine's merge/dedup mechanism.

fields.name: service_store
fields.description: True when this message is annotated as a durable service_store value.

fields.name: service_store_name
fields.description: Durable service_store name. Defaults to the protobuf message name.

fields.name: service_store_label
fields.description: Hosting service labels from (spec.service_store).label.

fields.name: timeseries_dedup
fields.description:
now lives on record_retention (from (spec.record).retention),
 never on a transformation or its compile target. 2026-08-25.
 Store-neutral dedup policy for a standalone (spec.timeseries_type) table, from
 its .dedup. Unset = append-only (no dedup) — the standalone-table default.

fields.name: data_entitlement_default
fields.description:
Message-level data-entitlement default from (spec.data_entitlement): the
 default transform applied to this message's eligible fields, overridden per
 field by (spec.redact). UNSPECIFIED = no message-level default.

fields.name: record_retention
fields.description:
record_retention from (spec.record).retention: the store-neutral row
 retention policy for this record's stored rows. Unset = indefinite.
 Retention is DELIVERY-side state — a transformation is a pure conversion and
 carries none.

message.name: RetentionPolicyInfo
message.description:
RetentionPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.RetentionPolicy — the
 store-neutral row retention policy. A downstream materializer renders this
 into an engine-specific TTL/eviction rule.

rpcs.description:
ManageCert: bidi cert lifecycle. Any authenticated service may open a
 stream — the SecurityInterceptor validates the bearer token before
 the handler runs, and the handler matches the token's location-agnostic
 service path (token.service_path(), derived from sub_type/sub — never a
 raw SPIFFE URI claim) to the requested service_name in the first Init
 message.

services.name: TlsCertService
services.description:
TlsCertService provides automatic TLS certificate lifecycle management.
 The certificate authority service implements the server side. Services with
 auto_tls: true open a bidi stream via the generated ServiceManager.

 Flow:
   1. Service sends Init (identifies itself) + Csr (public key)
   2. Certificate authority signs cert under service's intermediate CA, returns CertDelivery
   3. At half-life, certificate authority sends Renew
   4. Service generates new keypair, sends Csr
   5. Certificate authority signs, returns CertDelivery
   6. Repeat from 3

values.name: JWT_PAYLOAD_TYPE_NAMESPACE
values.description:
--- Namespace (authorization scope) ---
 `namespace` is the caller's authorization-tree scope, e.g. "/" (root),
 "/system/...", "/tenants/acme", or "/tenants/acme/workspaces/dev". It is
 an authorization fact, NOT the subject identity. The subject SPIFFE ID is
 a COMPUTATION over the structured claims (sub_type, sub, namespace,
 service_name) performed by the generated sys/spiffe helper
 (token.subject_spiffe_id); it is never carried as a wire claim. The
 universal level-or-below rule (target_namespace_field) compares namespace
 paths directly via the path-segment-aware is_at_or_below relation.

enums.description: GrantType represents OAuth 2.0 grant types

enums.name: TokenPurpose
enums.description: TokenPurpose distinguishes the purpose of a token in minting requests.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_REFRESH
values.description: Refresh token — long-lived, used to obtain new access tokens.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_ACCESS
values.description: Access token — short-lived, carries entitlements for a specific service.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_SERVICE
values.description: Service token — access token scoped to a specific target service (aud).

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_BOOTSTRAP
values.description:
Bootstrap token — very short-lived, used to bootstrap a child workload.
 Parent mints this via WorkloadMint and passes it to the child process.
 Child exchanges it with the token authority for a real access + refresh pair.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_LOCALITY
values.description:
Locality token — rotated by parent, shared with all children.
 Children present this on refresh to prove they can still reach their parent.

enums.name: TokenUse
enums.description: TokenUse claim values — identifies the purpose of a token in the token_use claim.

values.name: TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL
values.description:
TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL marks a token minted by the token authority for use with an external upstream service.
 Internal service auth middleware rejects any token carrying this token_use value,
 preventing a compromised proxy from replaying an externally-minted credential
 against platform-internal services.

values.name: TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE
values.description:
TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE is the long-lived, identity-only Offline Token (OT) held
 by the client daemon on disk. Carries no entitlements (its long TTL would
 make an embedded entitlement snapshot lie). Used as input to mint AT, and to
 self-renew via TokenMint(input=OT, no aud).

types.name: Config
types.description:
Config configures the JWT token cache used for authentication.
 Controls how tokens and JWK signing keys are cached and refreshed.

fields.name: dynamic_lookup
fields.description:
dynamic_lookup enables automatic JWK fetching from OIDC endpoints.
 When true, JWKs are automatically fetched from token issuer's
 .well-known/openid-configuration endpoint.
 When false, only manually added static keys are used.
 Default: true

fields.name: lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
lifetime_seconds is how long before cached JWK keys are refreshed.
 Default: 604800 (1 week)

fields.name: expire_unused_seconds
fields.description:
expire_unused_seconds is how long before unused JWK keys are evicted.
 Default: 86400 (24 hours)

fields.name: refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_interval_seconds is how often the cleanup goroutine runs.
 Default: 3600 (1 hour)

enum_values.description: Refresh token — long-lived, used to obtain new access tokens.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_ACCESS
enum_values.description: Access token — short-lived, carries entitlements for a specific service.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_SERVICE
enum_values.description: Service token — access token scoped to a specific target service (aud).

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_BOOTSTRAP
enum_values.description:
Bootstrap token — very short-lived, used to bootstrap a child workload.
 Parent mints this via WorkloadMint and passes it to the child process.
 Child exchanges it with the token authority for a real access + refresh pair.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_LOCALITY
enum_values.description:
Locality token — rotated by parent, shared with all children.
 Children present this on refresh to prove they can still reach their parent.

message.name: TraceRound
message.description: TraceRound identifies a single service hop in a traced request.

fields.name: rpc
fields.description:
rpc identifies the specific service and method being traced using the
 generated AccountingMethod enum type. Exactly one field is set to the
 corresponding RPC enum value; all others default to 0.

message.name: AccountingMethod
message.description:
AccountingMethod identifies which RPC an event relates to.
 Only one field will be set — the rest default to 0 (UNSPECIFIED)
 and are not encoded by proto3, so there is no overhead.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: kind classifies where in the request lifecycle this event was emitted.

fields.name: error
fields.description:
error is set on response events when the request failed (auth rejection,
 backend unavailable, handler error, etc.). Empty on success.

types.name: TraceRequest
types.description:
TraceRequest replaces google.protobuf.Empty on the gRPC wire for RPCs with
 empty input types. This ensures every RPC can be traced, even read-only
 endpoints that take no parameters. The handler interface stays arg-free —
 TraceRequest has no user-meaningful fields.

types.name: TraceRound
types.description: TraceRound identifies a single service hop in a traced request.

enums.name: TraceEventKind
enums.description:
TraceEvent is published per-hop to the trace topic when a traced message
 passes through a service. EventBus matches these to active WatchTrace streams
 by trace_id. Ordering is determined by timestamp_ms in TraceRound.
 TraceEventKind classifies the trace event within the request lifecycle.
 External events are emitted by the gateway (edge); internal events are
 emitted by backend services.

types.name: AccountingRecord
types.description:
AccountingRecord is one completed RPC, stored in full by stratum.

 Every service in the fleet is a producer, so the s2s surface is open to all
 service identities. There is no c2s surface: accounting rows are written by
 the chassis, never by a browser client.

fields.name: accounting_id
fields.description: accounting_id is the record key: one row per accounting event.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is THE correlation key — the x-request-id the gateway generates
 and every hop forwards. The EQ query_field is what lets a caller ask "which
 accounting rows belong to the request that wrote this row", which is the
 whole reason this record exists rather than a log line.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process ("{service_id}-{instance_id}"),
 copied verbatim from accounting.Event.source_id.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the RANGE criterion — "everything in this window".

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is carried on the envelope so a consumer can filter without
 inspecting the payload; same reasoning applies to the stored row.

fields.name: method

 owner. Stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token at publish
 time — not populated by clients. (Replaces the former email owner.)

enum_values.description: Session lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TOOL_USE
enum_values.description: Tool use (any tool: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Agent, etc.)

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SUBAGENT_START
enum_values.description: Subagent lifecycle — agent spawned or finished.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TASK_COMPLETED
enum_values.description: Task lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_COMPACT
enum_values.description: Context management.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_PROMPT
enum_values.description: User prompt submitted.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_STOP
enum_values.description: Stop — agent finished responding.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 redo log is partial, so recovery is a union across nodes and the epoch is
 the only clock that resolves it. Without this field the type keeps its

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the author's business clock, the one
 (spec.record).retention measures age from. Two different clocks; only this
 one is store-owned.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session produced this event. It is the tenant half of the identity
 spiffe_id carries the subject half of: spiffe_id names WHO acted, this names
 WHICH TENANT the row belongs to, and the generated egress filter holds a c2s
 read to rows matching the caller's claim by EXACT equality (never the
 level-or-below containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Deliberately NOT projected into any transformation above: adding it there
 would widen four already-explicit column lists, which is a separate call.

 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Deliberately NOT projected into any transformation above: adding it there
 would widen four already-explicit column lists, which is a separate call.

types.name: AgentSessionState
types.description:
AgentSessionState is the CURRENT state of one coding-agent session: one row
 per session, rewritten in place every time the session moves.

 It exists because the fleet had no mutable warm record and two properties of
 the warm tier are only observable on one. AgentEvent (hot) and AccountingRecord
 (warm, append-only) are both write-once by their own nature — an event and a
 completed RPC have no later state — so nothing exercised the store epoch
 REFRESHING, which is the whole reason the epoch is a last-write clock rather
 than a creation stamp.

 A session is the natural carrier for that: it is open for as long as the agent
 is working, its status and counters change while it is open, and once it has
 ended the row is a historical record that ages out of memory exactly like an
 accounting row. Both halves of the warm window apply to it, and unlike the two
 records above it moves while it is resident.

 There is no row-mutating RPC and there is not meant to be one: rows reach the
 store by EventBus publish, so an UPDATE is a republish of the same session_id.
 The generated wrapper restamps store_epoch_ms on that republish, which is what
 puts the row back inside the residency window.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: session_id is the record key: one row per session, not one per transition.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner — the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID,
 stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token, exactly as on
 AgentEvent. The literal field name is load-bearing for that stamping.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the session's business clock, fixed at the first publish and
 NOT rewritten afterwards. It is what retention above measures age from.

 The contrast with store_epoch_ms below is the point of this record: on an
 append-only row the two clocks are written together and never diverge, so
 nothing could tell them apart. Here they diverge on every update.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the session's current state — the mutable field an update carries.

fields.name: tool_use_count
fields.description:
tool_use_count is how many tool invocations the session has made so far.
 Monotonic, but rewritten in place: the row holds the running total, not one
 row per increment.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 On this record it MOVES. Every republish of the same session_id restamps it,
 which resets the row's residency: a session that has aged out of the memory
 window and is then updated is inside the window again, because the window is
 measured from the last write and the row was just written. That is the
 property RESIDENCY_WARM without MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY exists to state, and
 it is why the residency clock cannot be started_at_ms.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session this row tracks, the same value AgentEvent carries for the
 events emitted inside that session. Held to EXACT equality against the
 caller's claim by the generated c2s egress filter.

 MANDATORY on every (spec.record): tacplus fails generation for one that
 declares none (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations).

 Unlike status and tool_use_count, this is NOT a field an update carries: a
 session does not change tenant. It is rewritten with the same value on every
 republish of the same session_id, which is what makes the row's tenant
 stable across the restamping described for store_epoch_ms above.

types.name: EntitlementEvalInput
types.description:
EntitlementEvalInput is the input to the entitlements OPA policy.
 tacplus generates a typed EvalEntitlement RPC on opa from this message.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the IDP-provided identity claims (e.g. email, groups, roles).
 Uses google.protobuf.Struct to preserve native JSON types (arrays, objects, booleans).

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the caller's project namespace (e.g. "/local/dev/drpepper").
 OPA dispatches on it to run that project's policy. Empty = cluster-root policy.

types.name: EntitlementEvalResult
types.description:
EntitlementEvalResult is the output of the entitlements OPA policy.
 The policy returns a TokenEntitlements directly — kernel embeds it in the
 JWT service_entitlements claim without any further expansion.

fields.name: token_entitlements
fields.description: token_entitlements holds the per-service RPC grants returned by OPA.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: all_entitlements
fields.description:
all_entitlements grants unrestricted access to all services and RPCs.
 When true, kernel sets service_entitlements={"all":true} in the JWT,
 and gateway bypasses per-service entitlement checks entirely.
 Intended for admin users only.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the tenant namespace the policy assigns to this caller, as a
 leading-slash absolute path (e.g. "/local/dev/acme"). IDP+OPA live at the
 tenant level, so this is the tenant subtree the caller's issuer/claims map
 to. When empty, kernel falls back to the cluster-root namespace.

fields.name: authorized_projects
fields.description:
authorized_projects are the project leaf names within the tenant that this
 caller may obtain an access token for (e.g. ["prod", "staging"]). The
 minted AT is always scoped to exactly one of these; a project switch
 re-mints against this list without requiring re-login. Leaf segments,
 relative to `namespace`.

fields.name: default_project
fields.description:
default_project is the project the caller is scoped to immediately after
 login, when no explicit project is requested. Must be one of
 authorized_projects. Leaf segment, relative to `namespace`.

services.name: OpaEval
services.description:
Generated by tacplus from spec.opa_eval annotations.
 tacplus:generated-service opaeval

types.name: ProxyPolicyEvalInput
types.description:
ProxyPolicyEvalInput is the input to the proxy policy OPA evaluation.
 tacplus generates a typed EvalProxyPolicy RPC on opa from this message.
 Kernel calls this before minting an external token — the caller's JWT payload
 and opaque routing metadata are the inputs the policy uses to decide.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the caller's JWT payload claims (e.g. sub, email, groups,
 service_entitlements). Uses google.protobuf.Struct to preserve native
 JSON types (arrays, objects, booleans).

fields.name: metadata
fields.description:
metadata is the opaque string from the schematicctl listener config,
 forwarded verbatim by the proxy. The policy uses it to determine which
 upstream is being targeted (e.g. by mapping to a known URL or label)
 and whether the caller is permitted to reach it.

types.name: ProxyPolicyEvalResult
types.description:
ProxyPolicyEvalResult is the output of the proxy policy OPA evaluation.
 Kernel reads this result and either rejects the request (allow = false) or
 mints an external token incorporating the specified mutations.

fields.name: allow
fields.description:
allow indicates whether the request is permitted.
 When false, kernel rejects the ExternalTokenMint call with PERMISSION_DENIED.

fields.name: url
fields.description:
url, if non-empty, is the resolved destination URL for the upstream request.
 Kernel returns this to the proxy in ExternalTokenMintResponse so the proxy
 forwards to the correct destination. Empty means the proxy uses its own
 DEFAULT_API_ENDPOINT for the service.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTP_OR_HTTPS)

fields.name: reason
fields.description:
reason explains the denial. Returned to the proxy in the denial status.
 Empty when allow = true.

fields.name: append_aud
fields.description:
append_aud contains zero or more audience values to append to the minted
 external token's aud claim. The caller's original aud is always preserved —
 OPA may only add audiences, never replace or remove the original.
 Most policies leave this empty. Set it when the upstream requires a specific
 audience value (e.g. an OIDC client ID or SAML SP entity ID) in addition to
 the caller's existing aud.

fields.name: extra_claims
fields.description:
extra_claims contains additional JWT claims to inject into the minted token.
 Kernel merges these into the token payload alongside the standard claims.
 Existing claims on the caller's token are never removed — only additions
 are permitted to prevent privilege escalation via claim stripping.

fields.name: auth_type
fields.description:
auth_type determines the credential format kernel returns to the proxy.
 TOKEN_TYPE_JWT (default): kernel returns a signed JWT in the response.
 TOKEN_TYPE_SAML: kernel returns a SAML assertion in the response.
 Unset is treated as TOKEN_TYPE_JWT.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_JWT
enum_values.description: TokenTypeJwt represents a JWT token

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_SAML
enum_values.description: TokenTypeSaml represents a SAML token

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_SSH
enum_values.description: TokenTypeSsh represents an SSH token

fields.name: token_use
fields.description:
token_use sets the token_use claim on the minted external token.
 Must be TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL or TOKEN_USE_UNSPECIFIED (both result in
 TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL being stamped). Kernel rejects any other value to
 ensure external tokens can never be replayed against internal services.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description:
TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL marks a token minted by the token authority for use with an external upstream service.
 Internal service auth middleware rejects any token carrying this token_use value,
 preventing a compromised proxy from replaying an externally-minted credential
 against platform-internal services.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE
enum_values.description:
TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE is the long-lived, identity-only Offline Token (OT) held
 by the client daemon on disk. Carries no entitlements (its long TTL would
 make an embedded entitlement snapshot lie). Used as input to mint AT, and to

message.name: AccountingRecord
message.description:
AccountingRecord is one completed RPC, stored in full by stratum.

 Every service in the fleet is a producer, so the s2s surface is open to all
 service identities. There is no c2s surface: accounting rows are written by
 the chassis, never by a browser client.

fields.name: accounting_id
fields.description: accounting_id is the record key: one row per accounting event.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is THE correlation key — the x-request-id the gateway generates
 and every hop forwards. The EQ query_field is what lets a caller ask "which
 accounting rows belong to the request that wrote this row", which is the
 whole reason this record exists rather than a log line.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process ("{service_id}-{instance_id}"),
 copied verbatim from accounting.Event.source_id.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the RANGE criterion — "everything in this window".

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is carried on the envelope so a consumer can filter without
 inspecting the payload; same reasoning applies to the stored row.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was accounted for.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the gRPC status code the call completed with.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is the measured call duration.

fields.name: principal_sub
fields.description:
principal_sub is the verified human principal behind the call — the claim
 the Authorizer actually checked, not a caller-written header. Caller-decided
 redaction, the same leg TaskActivity.created_by exercises: redacted by
 default, raw only for a caller holding a matching data grant.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s half:
 (spec.store_principal) is what the generated wrapper filters a user's reads
 down to, and it must name the HUMAN, not spiffe_id below. spiffe_id is the
 emitting service, so filtering on it would narrow every user to the rows it
 emitted itself — which for a human is none. The two annotations disagree on
 purpose and this one wins, exactly as sys/spec.proto describes.

 The row filter runs BEFORE the redaction above, on the raw stored value, so
 a caller without the data grant is still matched against its own principal
 rather than against a redacted string.
 NOT a (spec.query_field), deliberately, and that is a real tension rather
 than an oversight. Making it an EQ criterion is what would carry the row
 filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY RPCs — Get<T>Count returns a number over
 the handle's predicate and no rows, so no egress filter can narrow it — but
 ValidateDataEntitlementAnnotations refuses a field that is both
 (spec.redact) and (spec.query_field), because a filterable field defeats
 redaction. That refusal is right for the S2S half of the plane, where no
 per-caller pin applies and a peer could filter on this field freely.

 So accounting ROWS are filtered to the caller at egress and accounting
 COUNTS are not. Closing that needs a per-surface criterion (c2s-only,
 wrapper-pinned) which does not exist today; it is written up in the item 2
 report rather than bought by weakening the redaction rule.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner: the EMITTING SERVICE's identity, not the end
 user's (the human principal is principal_sub above). The field name is
 load-bearing — eventbus's topic discovery matches the LITERAL name
 "spiffe_id" of string type to decide which topics get publisher-identity
 stamping, so renaming it silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes RESIDENCY_WARM above possible: the residency window is
 measured from this clock, and it is the predicate the memory and disk legs
 partition the query on. RESIDENCY_WARM without it fails generation
 (ValidateResidencyAnnotations VAL-3) rather than silently tiering on the
 wrong clock.

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the emitting service's business clock, the one
 retention above measures age from. Two different clocks; only this one is
 store-owned. On an append-only record they are written together and never
 diverge afterwards — which is a property of THIS record, not of the epoch.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose RPC this row accounts for. (spec.store_namespace) is the tenant twin
 of principal_sub's (spec.store_principal) above — the same egress seam, a
 different boundary. That one answers "are these MY rows"; this one answers
 "is this MY tenant", by EXACT string equality against the caller's claim.

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like every other string field on this message. Not a
 (spec.query_field): the field exists to be the egress boundary, and making
 it a caller-supplied predicate is not what a boundary is.

fields.name: principal_sub_redacted

types.name: AgentCycleFilter
AgentCycleWatchChange

message.name: AgentCycle
message.description:
AgentCycle is one completed loop cycle: what woke it, when, on which
 instance, under which fencing token.

 It is the durable history the design record calls the "Bird's Eye View" —
 "an ordinary generated read surface on that record — no new mechanism". This
 file therefore declares no read RPC for it: the c2s record query plane
 generated from (spec.store_principal) and the query fields below IS that
 surface, and hand-writing a second one would be the drift the typed-contract
 argument exists to prevent.

 Append-shaped by construction: the key carries the cycle number, so a cycle
 is a new row and no cycle ever rewrites another.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 AgentCycleBus with topic ref scottyagent.AgentCycleBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: cycle_id
fields.description: cycle_id is the record key: "<user>/<cycle>".

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is whose agent ran, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL.

 (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's reads of this record to
 their own rows on the c2s query plane, and it is the reason the Bird's Eye
 View needs no filtering code: "my cycles" is the only query the plane will
 answer. `spiffe_id` below is the record's declared owner but holds THIS
 SERVICE's identity (eventbus stamps the publisher), so filtering on that
 would show every user nothing.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the filter into the plane's size-only
 RPCs, which return a number over the handle's predicate and no rows for an
 egress filter to narrow.

fields.name: cycle
fields.description: cycle is this user's monotonic cycle number, the second half of cycle_id.

fields.name: fencing_token
fields.description:
fencing_token is the kernel.FencedLock token this cycle ran under. Carried
 onto the row so the history itself shows the fence: cycles for one user
 must appear in strictly increasing token order, and a row that does not is
 visible evidence of a stale holder that got through.

fields.name: woke_for
fields.description:
woke_for is EVERY event this cycle aggregated, in the order they were
 observed — not just the one that started it. That is the aggregation the
 design record asks for, made legible: "multiple events can land within one
 loop cycle; they are aggregated and processed together".

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_events_per_cycle's ceiling.

message.name: WakeEvent
message.description:
WakeEvent is ONE thing that woke the loop. A cycle carries every event it
 aggregated, not just the first, so "why did you wake" has a complete answer
 even when several arrived at once.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason is the trigger kind.

enum_values.name: WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A messaging.Message arrived on this user's EventBus queue and this
 instance's consumer group took it.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the specific event. For WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE it is the
 messaging.Message's delivery_id — the record key of the one delivery this
 wake is for, not the message_id it shares with its siblings, because the
 delivery is what this consumer group consumed.

fields.name: observed_at_ms
fields.description: observed_at_ms is when this instance took the event off the queue.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the business clock — when the cycle began, which is after
 the lock was granted. It is what retention measures age from, and the RANGE
 criterion because "what did my agent do last week" is the question the
 Bird's Eye View asks.

fields.name: finished_at_ms
fields.description: finished_at_ms is when it ended, before the release.

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id is the instance that ran the cycle. Provenance, not routing —
 see AgentCursor.last_instance_id.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The NAME IS LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off. It holds THIS SERVICE's identity,
 because the publish is s2s; `user` above is where the person is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT. MANDATORY on a (spec.record):
 tacplus's ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations fails generation for any
 record declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record nobody
 remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 Left EMPTY by this service on publish, on purpose. eventbus's
 PublishHandler stamps it from the publishing token's namespace claim and
 REFUSES the publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none —
 stamp-or-refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty, because a row published
 with an empty namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read. A
 value written here would be this service asserting a tenant nothing
 verified. (That the stamp is the SERVICE's namespace rather than the user's
 is the gap AgentCursor.namespace describes.)

message.name: AgentEvent
message.description:
AgentEvent is the top-level event published to EventBus.
 Each event represents one hook firing in one coding-agent session.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
── Identity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 spiffe_id is the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID
 (spiffe://<root>/tenants/<tenant_id>/users/<sub>), the durable EventDB
 owner. Stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token at publish
 time — not populated by clients. (Replaces the former email owner.)

fields.name: event_id
fields.description:
event_id is the globally unique identifier for this event.
 Generated server-side. Not populated by clients.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SESSION_START
enum_values.description: Session lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TOOL_USE
enum_values.description: Tool use (any tool: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Agent, etc.)

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SUBAGENT_START
enum_values.description: Subagent lifecycle — agent spawned or finished.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TASK_COMPLETED
enum_values.description: Task lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_COMPACT
enum_values.description: Context management.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_PROMPT
enum_values.description: User prompt submitted.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_STOP
enum_values.description: Stop — agent finished responding.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes AgentEvent REPLAYABLE in stratum's hot tier: each node's
 redo log is partial, so recovery is a union across nodes and the epoch is
 the only clock that resolves it. Without this field the type keeps its
 in-memory replication and its quorum gate but gets no redo log at all
 (stratum's HotStoreGenerator refuses one it could not safely merge).

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the author's business clock, the one
 (spec.record).retention measures age from. Two different clocks; only this
 one is store-owned.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session produced this event. It is the tenant half of the identity
 spiffe_id carries the subject half of: spiffe_id names WHO acted, this names
 WHICH TENANT the row belongs to, and the generated egress filter holds a c2s
 read to rows matching the caller's claim by EXACT equality (never the
 level-or-below containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Deliberately NOT projected into any transformation above: adding it there
 would widen four already-explicit column lists, which is a separate call.

types.name: AgentSessionStateFilter
AgentSessionStateWatchChange

message.name: AgentSessionState
message.description:
AgentSessionState is the CURRENT state of one coding-agent session: one row
 per session, rewritten in place every time the session moves.

 It exists because the fleet had no mutable warm record and two properties of
 the warm tier are only observable on one. AgentEvent (hot) and AccountingRecord
 (warm, append-only) are both write-once by their own nature — an event and a
 completed RPC have no later state — so nothing exercised the store epoch
 REFRESHING, which is the whole reason the epoch is a last-write clock rather
 than a creation stamp.

 A session is the natural carrier for that: it is open for as long as the agent
 is working, its status and counters change while it is open, and once it has
 ended the row is a historical record that ages out of memory exactly like an
 accounting row. Both halves of the warm window apply to it, and unlike the two
 records above it moves while it is resident.

 There is no row-mutating RPC and there is not meant to be one: rows reach the
 store by EventBus publish, so an UPDATE is a republish of the same session_id.
 The generated wrapper restamps store_epoch_ms on that republish, which is what
 puts the row back inside the residency window.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: session_id is the record key: one row per session, not one per transition.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner — the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID,
 stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token, exactly as on
 AgentEvent. The literal field name is load-bearing for that stamping.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the session's business clock, fixed at the first publish and
 NOT rewritten afterwards. It is what retention above measures age from.

 The contrast with store_epoch_ms below is the point of this record: on an
 append-only row the two clocks are written together and never diverge, so
 nothing could tell them apart. Here they diverge on every update.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the session's current state — the mutable field an update carries.

fields.name: tool_use_count
fields.description:
tool_use_count is how many tool invocations the session has made so far.
 Monotonic, but rewritten in place: the row holds the running total, not one
 row per increment.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 On this record it MOVES. Every republish of the same session_id restamps it,
 which resets the row's residency: a session that has aged out of the memory
 window and is then updated is inside the window again, because the window is
 measured from the last write and the row was just written. That is the
 property RESIDENCY_WARM without MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY exists to state, and
 it is why the residency clock cannot be started_at_ms.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session this row tracks, the same value AgentEvent carries for the
 events emitted inside that session. Held to EXACT equality against the
 caller's claim by the generated c2s egress filter.

 MANDATORY on every (spec.record): tacplus fails generation for one that
 declares none (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations).

 Unlike status and tool_use_count, this is NOT a field an update carries: a
 session does not change tenant. It is rewritten with the same value on every
 republish of the same session_id, which is what makes the row's tenant
 stable across the restamping described for store_epoch_ms above.
