types.name: SampleAccountingRecordRequest
SampleAccountingRecordResponse

message.name: AccountingRecord
message.description:
AccountingRecord is one completed RPC, stored in full by stratum.

 Every service in the fleet is a producer, so the s2s surface is open to all
 service identities. There is no c2s surface: accounting rows are written by
 the chassis, never by a browser client.

fields.name: accounting_id
fields.description: accounting_id is the record key: one row per accounting event.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is THE correlation key — the x-request-id the gateway generates
 and every hop forwards. The EQ query_field is what lets a caller ask "which
 accounting rows belong to the request that wrote this row", which is the
 whole reason this record exists rather than a log line.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process ("{service_id}-{instance_id}"),
 copied verbatim from accounting.Event.source_id.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the RANGE criterion — "everything in this window".

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is carried on the envelope so a consumer can filter without
 inspecting the payload; same reasoning applies to the stored row.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was accounted for.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the gRPC status code the call completed with.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is the measured call duration.

fields.name: principal_sub
fields.description:
principal_sub is the verified human principal behind the call — the claim
 the Authorizer actually checked, not a caller-written header. Caller-decided
 redaction, the same leg TaskActivity.created_by exercises: redacted by
 default, raw only for a caller holding a matching data grant.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s half:
 (spec.store_principal) is what the generated wrapper filters a user's reads
 down to, and it must name the HUMAN, not spiffe_id below. spiffe_id is the
 emitting service, so filtering on it would narrow every user to the rows it
 emitted itself — which for a human is none. The two annotations disagree on
 purpose and this one wins, exactly as sys/spec.proto describes.

 The row filter runs BEFORE the redaction above, on the raw stored value, so
 a caller without the data grant is still matched against its own principal
 rather than against a redacted string.
 NOT a (spec.query_field), deliberately, and that is a real tension rather
 than an oversight. Making it an EQ criterion is what would carry the row
 filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY RPCs — Get<T>Count returns a number over
 the handle's predicate and no rows, so no egress filter can narrow it — but
 ValidateDataEntitlementAnnotations refuses a field that is both
 (spec.redact) and (spec.query_field), because a filterable field defeats
 redaction. That refusal is right for the S2S half of the plane, where no
 per-caller pin applies and a peer could filter on this field freely.

 So accounting ROWS are filtered to the caller at egress and accounting
 COUNTS are not. Closing that needs a per-surface criterion (c2s-only,
 wrapper-pinned) which does not exist today; it is written up in the item 2
 report rather than bought by weakening the redaction rule.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner: the EMITTING SERVICE's identity, not the end
 user's (the human principal is principal_sub above). The field name is
 load-bearing — eventbus's topic discovery matches the LITERAL name
 "spiffe_id" of string type to decide which topics get publisher-identity
 stamping, so renaming it silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes RESIDENCY_WARM above possible: the residency window is
 measured from this clock, and it is the predicate the memory and disk legs
 partition the query on. RESIDENCY_WARM without it fails generation
 (ValidateResidencyAnnotations VAL-3) rather than silently tiering on the
 wrong clock.

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the emitting service's business clock, the one
 retention above measures age from. Two different clocks; only this one is
 store-owned. On an append-only record they are written together and never
 diverge afterwards — which is a property of THIS record, not of the epoch.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose RPC this row accounts for. (spec.store_namespace) is the tenant twin
 of principal_sub's (spec.store_principal) above — the same egress seam, a
 different boundary. That one answers "are these MY rows"; this one answers
 "is this MY tenant", by EXACT string equality against the caller's claim.

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like every other string field on this message. Not a
 (spec.query_field): the field exists to be the egress boundary, and making
 it a caller-supplied predicate is not what a boundary is.

fields.name: principal_sub_redacted

types.name: SampleAgentCycleRequest
SampleAgentCycleResponse

message.name: AgentCycle
message.description:
AgentCycle is one completed loop cycle: what woke it, when, on which
 instance, under which fencing token.

 It is the durable history the design record calls the "Bird's Eye View" —
 "an ordinary generated read surface on that record — no new mechanism". This
 file therefore declares no read RPC for it: the c2s record query plane
 generated from (spec.store_principal) and the query fields below IS that
 surface, and hand-writing a second one would be the drift the typed-contract
 argument exists to prevent.

 Append-shaped by construction: the key carries the cycle number, so a cycle
 is a new row and no cycle ever rewrites another.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 AgentCycleBus with topic ref scottyagent.AgentCycleBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: cycle_id
fields.description: cycle_id is the record key: "<user>/<cycle>".

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is whose agent ran, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL.

 (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's reads of this record to
 their own rows on the c2s query plane, and it is the reason the Bird's Eye
 View needs no filtering code: "my cycles" is the only query the plane will
 answer. `spiffe_id` below is the record's declared owner but holds THIS
 SERVICE's identity (eventbus stamps the publisher), so filtering on that
 would show every user nothing.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the filter into the plane's size-only
 RPCs, which return a number over the handle's predicate and no rows for an
 egress filter to narrow.

fields.name: cycle
fields.description: cycle is this user's monotonic cycle number, the second half of cycle_id.

fields.name: fencing_token
fields.description:
fencing_token is the kernel.FencedLock token this cycle ran under. Carried
 onto the row so the history itself shows the fence: cycles for one user
 must appear in strictly increasing token order, and a row that does not is
 visible evidence of a stale holder that got through.

fields.name: woke_for
fields.description:
woke_for is EVERY event this cycle aggregated, in the order they were
 observed — not just the one that started it. That is the aggregation the
 design record asks for, made legible: "multiple events can land within one
 loop cycle; they are aggregated and processed together".

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_events_per_cycle's ceiling.

message.name: WakeEvent
message.description:
WakeEvent is ONE thing that woke the loop. A cycle carries every event it
 aggregated, not just the first, so "why did you wake" has a complete answer
 even when several arrived at once.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason is the trigger kind.

enum_values.name: WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A messaging.Message arrived on this user's EventBus queue and this
 instance's consumer group took it.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the specific event. For WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE it is the
 messaging.Message's delivery_id — the record key of the one delivery this
 wake is for, not the message_id it shares with its siblings, because the
 delivery is what this consumer group consumed.

fields.name: observed_at_ms
fields.description: observed_at_ms is when this instance took the event off the queue.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the business clock — when the cycle began, which is after
 the lock was granted. It is what retention measures age from, and the RANGE
 criterion because "what did my agent do last week" is the question the
 Bird's Eye View asks.

fields.name: finished_at_ms
fields.description: finished_at_ms is when it ended, before the release.

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id is the instance that ran the cycle. Provenance, not routing —
 see AgentCursor.last_instance_id.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The NAME IS LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off. It holds THIS SERVICE's identity,
 because the publish is s2s; `user` above is where the person is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT. MANDATORY on a (spec.record):
 tacplus's ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations fails generation for any
 record declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record nobody
 remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 Left EMPTY by this service on publish, on purpose. eventbus's
 PublishHandler stamps it from the publishing token's namespace claim and
 REFUSES the publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none —
 stamp-or-refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty, because a row published
 with an empty namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read. A
 value written here would be this service asserting a tenant nothing
 verified. (That the stamp is the SERVICE's namespace rather than the user's
 is the gap AgentCursor.namespace describes.)

types.name: SampleAgentEventRequest
SampleAgentEventResponse

message.name: AgentEvent
message.description:
AgentEvent is the top-level event published to EventBus.
 Each event represents one hook firing in one coding-agent session.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
── Identity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 spiffe_id is the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID
 (spiffe://<root>/tenants/<tenant_id>/users/<sub>), the durable EventDB
 owner. Stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token at publish
 time — not populated by clients. (Replaces the former email owner.)

fields.name: event_id
fields.description:
event_id is the globally unique identifier for this event.
 Generated server-side. Not populated by clients.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SESSION_START
enum_values.description: Session lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TOOL_USE
enum_values.description: Tool use (any tool: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Agent, etc.)

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SUBAGENT_START
enum_values.description: Subagent lifecycle — agent spawned or finished.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TASK_COMPLETED
enum_values.description: Task lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_COMPACT
enum_values.description: Context management.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_PROMPT
enum_values.description: User prompt submitted.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_STOP
enum_values.description: Stop — agent finished responding.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes AgentEvent REPLAYABLE in stratum's hot tier: each node's
 redo log is partial, so recovery is a union across nodes and the epoch is
 the only clock that resolves it. Without this field the type keeps its
 in-memory replication and its quorum gate but gets no redo log at all
 (stratum's HotStoreGenerator refuses one it could not safely merge).

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the author's business clock, the one
 (spec.record).retention measures age from. Two different clocks; only this
 one is store-owned.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session produced this event. It is the tenant half of the identity
 spiffe_id carries the subject half of: spiffe_id names WHO acted, this names
 WHICH TENANT the row belongs to, and the generated egress filter holds a c2s
 read to rows matching the caller's claim by EXACT equality (never the
 level-or-below containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Deliberately NOT projected into any transformation above: adding it there
 would widen four already-explicit column lists, which is a separate call.

message.name: SessionEvent
message.description: SessionEvent captures session start/end metadata.

message.name: ToolUseEvent
message.description: ToolUseEvent captures a single tool invocation.

message.name: FileEvent
message.description: FileEvent captures a file operation.

message.name: SubagentEvent
message.description: SubagentEvent captures subagent spawn/stop.

message.name: PromptEvent
message.description: PromptEvent captures a user prompt submission.

message.name: StopEvent
message.description: StopEvent captures why the agent stopped responding.

types.name: SampleAgentSessionStateRequest
SampleAgentSessionStateResponse

message.name: AgentSessionState
message.description:
AgentSessionState is the CURRENT state of one coding-agent session: one row
 per session, rewritten in place every time the session moves.

 It exists because the fleet had no mutable warm record and two properties of
 the warm tier are only observable on one. AgentEvent (hot) and AccountingRecord
 (warm, append-only) are both write-once by their own nature — an event and a
 completed RPC have no later state — so nothing exercised the store epoch
 REFRESHING, which is the whole reason the epoch is a last-write clock rather
 than a creation stamp.

 A session is the natural carrier for that: it is open for as long as the agent
 is working, its status and counters change while it is open, and once it has
 ended the row is a historical record that ages out of memory exactly like an
 accounting row. Both halves of the warm window apply to it, and unlike the two
 records above it moves while it is resident.

 There is no row-mutating RPC and there is not meant to be one: rows reach the
 store by EventBus publish, so an UPDATE is a republish of the same session_id.
 The generated wrapper restamps store_epoch_ms on that republish, which is what
 puts the row back inside the residency window.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: session_id is the record key: one row per session, not one per transition.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner — the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID,
 stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token, exactly as on
 AgentEvent. The literal field name is load-bearing for that stamping.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the session's business clock, fixed at the first publish and
 NOT rewritten afterwards. It is what retention above measures age from.

 The contrast with store_epoch_ms below is the point of this record: on an
 append-only row the two clocks are written together and never diverge, so
 nothing could tell them apart. Here they diverge on every update.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the session's current state — the mutable field an update carries.

fields.name: tool_use_count
fields.description:
tool_use_count is how many tool invocations the session has made so far.
 Monotonic, but rewritten in place: the row holds the running total, not one
 row per increment.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 On this record it MOVES. Every republish of the same session_id restamps it,
 which resets the row's residency: a session that has aged out of the memory
 window and is then updated is inside the window again, because the window is
 measured from the last write and the row was just written. That is the
 property RESIDENCY_WARM without MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY exists to state, and
 it is why the residency clock cannot be started_at_ms.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session this row tracks, the same value AgentEvent carries for the
 events emitted inside that session. Held to EXACT equality against the
 caller's claim by the generated c2s egress filter.

 MANDATORY on every (spec.record): tacplus fails generation for one that
 declares none (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations).

 Unlike status and tool_use_count, this is NOT a field an update carries: a
 session does not change tenant. It is rewritten with the same value on every
 republish of the same session_id, which is what makes the row's tenant
 stable across the restamping described for store_epoch_ms above.

types.name: SampleMailboxEntryRequest
SampleMailboxEntryResponse

message.name: MailboxEntry
message.description:
MailboxEntry is ONE DELIVERY'S mailbox state, keyed by the SAME delivery_id
 as the `messaging.Message` it tracks.

 Joinable by identity, not by a second lookup: an entry and its message share
 a key, so "fetch the body of the mail I was just told about" is one Message
 read with an id the client already holds.

 IT HOLDS NO BODY. `messaging.Message.text` is never copied here — that is the
 decision doc's rejected alternative ("Mailbox stores full message content"),
 and it stands. What IS carried is the inbox SUMMARY LINE the doc's own
 ListHeldMail spec enumerates (sender, subject, sent_at_ms): a mail client
 renders a list before anything is opened, and those three fields are the only
 way to serve that list without a second round trip per row. A summary line is
 not a second copy of the message, and the field that would make it one —
 `text` — is absent, as are `recipients` and `ticket_id`.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.description:
delivery_id is the record key and messaging.Message.delivery_id verbatim.
 Bounded identically (512) — a shorter bound here would silently drop the
 deliveries whose recipient subject is long.

fields.name: message_id
fields.description:
message_id groups the N entries of one submission, the same way it groups
 the N Messages. EQ-filterable for the same reason it is there.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is whose mailbox this is, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL — the
 same field, carrying the same annotation, as messaging.Message.recipient.
 The generated egress filter holds a caller's reads to their own rows, so
 ListHeldMail cannot return one person's mail to another even if this
 service's own predicate were wrong.

 spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 mailbox's own service identity, stamped by eventbus — so it is the wrong
 field to filter a user's reads on, exactly as it is on Message.

enum_values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_HELD
enum_values.description:
HELD: the delivery arrived on the topic and nobody has pulled it. The row
 must not be evicted in this state at any age — an unread message aging out
 defeats the entire point of a mailbox.

enum_values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_RETRIEVED
enum_values.description:
RETRIEVED: the recipient acknowledged pulling it. This is what starts
 eviction eligibility, and nothing else does.

fields.name: held_since_ms
fields.description:
held_since_ms is when this consumer group's copy landed — the residency
 clock in the doc's phrasing, and the timestamp retention above measures
 from. It is NOT what eviction eligibility counts from; see retrieved_at_ms.

 RANGE-filterable because "what has been sitting in my mailbox since last
 week" is a question about this field.

fields.name: retrieved_at_ms
fields.description:
retrieved_at_ms is unset until retrieved, and is the point eviction
 eligibility starts counting from. The decision doc rejects held_since_ms
 for this in as many words: "a message nobody has pulled yet must not be
 evicted just because it is old."

fields.name: sender
fields.description:
sender is messaging.Message.sender — the authenticated principal that sent
 it, never a caller-written string on either side.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: subject is the subject line. Bounded identically to Message.subject.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is the sender's clock, carried through so an inbox can sort by
 when a message was SENT rather than by when this consumer group happened to
 process it. The two differ by broker latency and by any replay.

fields.name: ejectionable
fields.description:
ejectionable is item 4's marker and this record's whole reason to exist —
 the first per-row use of it in the fleet.

 The values are not decoration and are not derivable from `status` by the
 store: the store does not know what HELD means, and UNSPECIFIED is defined
 as never-evict precisely so a marker an author forgets keeps the row.

   HELD      -> EJECTIONABLE_NEVER   (explicitly, not left at UNSPECIFIED:
                the row is stating a policy, not omitting one)
   RETRIEVED -> EJECTIONABLE_WINDOW  (set by UpdateHeldMail inline, or by
                the sweep when a grace period deferred it)

 WHAT "EVICT" DOES, stated plainly because the decision doc left it open:
 it evicts the row FROM MEMORY. It does not delete it. `Residency`'s own
 definition — "a warm row evicted from memory is still complete and
 queryable on disk" — is the semantics, and deletion is retention's job
 above, ninety days from arrival. There is deliberately no EVICTED status
 and no delete path here: a status this service wrote would be a claim about
 the store's memory that this service cannot observe.

enum_values.name: EJECTIONABLE_NEVER
enum_values.description:
NEVER: the residency window does not apply to this row. It stays resident
 for as long as the type's rows are retained at all. The explicit spelling
 of an absent value, the same way RetentionPolicy.forever is.

enum_values.name: EJECTIONABLE_WINDOW
enum_values.description:
WINDOW: the residency window applies to this row as declared — it is
 evicted from memory once its (spec.store_epoch) is older than the window,
 and served from disk thereafter.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is the row's LAST WRITE, stamped by the generated wrapper
 and never by this service. It is what the residency window is actually
 measured against, which is why marking a row WINDOW is a WRITE: the mark
 and the clock it starts are the same event.

 RANGE per (spec.store_epoch)'s own contract — it is the predicate a
 two-leg memory/disk query partitions on.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner, and the name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's
 topic discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type
 when deciding which topics get publisher-identity stamping.

 It holds MAILBOX'S OWN service identity — this service is the publisher.
 `recipient` above is where the person is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by EXACT string equality against the
 caller's namespace claim. MANDATORY: tacplus fails generation for any
 (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record
 nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 Its value is copied from the Message that produced this entry rather than
 resolved again: the tenant of a mailbox entry IS the tenant of the delivery
 it tracks, and re-deriving it from mailbox's own service token would stamp
 the SERVICE's tenant onto a USER's row.

 Not a (spec.query_field): the field exists to be the egress boundary, and a
 boundary a caller can name in a predicate is not one.

types.name: SampleMessageRequest
SampleMessageResponse

message.name: Message
message.description:
Message is ONE DELIVERY: one message, to one recipient.

 It is NOT one row per submission. A submission naming three recipients
 becomes three `Message` rows sharing a `message_id`, differing in
 `delivery_id` and `recipient`, each independently consumable and
 independently ACKable. See the fan-out note at the top of this file for why
 EventBus cannot do that split itself.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 MessageBus with topic ref messaging.MessageBus.stream. Do NOT hand-write that
 wrapper.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.description:
delivery_id is the record key: "<message_id>/<recipient>". One per
 (message, recipient) pair, which is what makes the N publishes of one
 submission N separately-keyed records rather than N copies of one.

 Derived rather than random ON PURPOSE: the value a caller would need to
 reconstruct to ACK a delivery is exactly (which message, for whom), so
 deriving it means an agent that knows both never has to have been told the
 id. It is also what makes the fan-out replay-safe — a retried submission
 regenerates the same delivery ids rather than a second set of rows.

fields.name: message_id
fields.description:
message_id groups the N deliveries of ONE submission. EQ-filterable,
 because "every delivery of the message I sent" is the question a sender
 asks, and it is the only way back from a delivery to its siblings.

fields.name: sender
fields.description:
sender is who sent it — the authenticated principal subject bound by the
 (spec.principal) field on SendMessageRequest below, never a caller-written
 string.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is THE recipient this delivery is for — one of `recipients`
 below, and the half of delivery_id that varies across the fan-out.

 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s
 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 eventbus stamps messaging's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. `sender` is the
 other candidate and is the wrong one: a mailbox read is "messages addressed
 to me", so the field the generated egress filter holds a caller's reads to
 must be the addressee.

 The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a SENDER cannot read their own
 sent messages through this record's c2s plane, because only one field may
 carry (spec.store_principal) and this is it. Sent-items is a mailbox
 concern and the mailbox service is Phase 1 item 8, undesigned; inventing a
 second read path for it here would be inventing that service's shape.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: recipients
fields.description:
recipients is the full To: line — every recipient of the submission, the
 SAME list on all N deliveries. `recipient` above says which one this row is
 for; this says who else got it.

 Carrying it is not redundancy. Without it a recipient cannot see who else
 was addressed, which is information the sender chose to disclose by
 addressing them together — the same reason a To: header exists and a Bcc:
 one does not. (This file models no Bcc; nothing has asked for one.)

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_recipients' ceiling above.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: subject is the message's subject line.

fields.name: text
fields.description: text is the message body. Free text, and nothing parses it — see ticket_id.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
ticket_id OPTIONALLY references the ticket this message pertains to.

 A dedicated field, never a value embedded in `text`. Routing and status
 display have to associate a message with its ticket to act, and the
 standing rule is that anything that must be parsed to be acted on should
 have been a field. Optional because most messages pertain to no ticket, and
 EQ-filterable because "every message about this ticket" is the question the
 field exists to answer.

 This is the ONLY ticket-shaped thing on Message, and it is an opaque id.
 Ticket's own churn — advice sealing, decision chains, amend/reconsider —
 stays entirely inside Ticket. That is what keeps this type stable.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is the business clock — when the sender submitted — and the
 RANGE criterion, because "my messages from last week" is the question a
 mailbox asks. It is what retention above measures age from.

 Identical across all N deliveries of one submission: they were one act.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off.

 It holds MESSAGING'S OWN service identity, not the sender's, because the
 publish is s2s from this service — that is the direct consequence of the
 SUPERSEDED ruling. `sender` above is where the human is.

fields.name: spiffe_actor
fields.description:
spiffe_actor is the ORIGIN signal: the delegate that made the call, stamped
 by EventBus from the publishing token's `act` claim at publish time.

   "a message is marked as originating from the user directly or from the
    user's Scotty acting on their behalf... A message sent by
    Scotty-for-Dennis carries `act` populated; one Dennis sends directly
    doesn't." — decisions/messaging-vs-ticketing-2026-08-31.md

 written here would be a claim about identity that nothing verified.
 Provenance only — sys/spec.proto forbids wiring it into a principal.

 GAP, STATED NOT PAPERED OVER. That quote describes the pre-supersession
 model, where the user published to EventBus DIRECTLY and EventBus saw the
 user's own delegated token. Under the corrected model the publish is s2s
 from messaging, so the token EventBus stamps from is messaging's own
 service token and carries no `act` claim at all — this field will be empty
 in the ordinary case, including for a genuine Scotty-for-Dennis send. The
 annotation is declared anyway, and correctly: the seam is the right one and
 the field is where the value belongs the moment the delegated-publish path
 exists. Closing it needs an s2s publish that carries the caller's exchanged

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that sent
 this message" is one predicate asked of two record types.

 Empty is legitimate: a call with no authenticated Caller has none to read.

fields.name: agent_received
fields.description:
agent_received is the delivery ACK, written by the consuming agent after it
 processes this delivery. Unset at publish — this service never writes it.

message.name: AgentReceivedReceipt
message.description:
AgentReceivedReceipt is the delivery ACK — the agent (scotty, the mailbox
 service) took the record off the topic and processed it. Written by the
 consumer, never by the sender or by this service.

 It is the ACK, not a copy of it: there is one event here, not a delivery ACK
 plus a receipt derived from it.

fields.name: received_at_ms
fields.description:
received_at_ms is when the consuming agent completed processing — the same
 instant it commits its consumer-group offset, since committing before
 processing is exactly the discipline the queue semantics forbid.

fields.name: received_by
fields.description: received_by is the SPIFFE identity of the consuming agent instance.

fields.name: human_viewed
fields.description:
human_viewed is the separately-typed human signal. Unset at publish, and
 unset for as long as the person has not looked, which is the normal state
 of a delivered message.

message.name: HumanViewedReceipt
message.description:
HumanViewedReceipt fires when the actual person looked at the message. A
 distinct signal from AgentReceivedReceipt above: an agent can have ACKed a
 message hours before a human sees it, and business-hours-deferred
 presentation makes that gap the normal case rather than the exception.

 Presentation is a passive pull label — the reader is told "viewed", never
 pushed a notification. That is the design already built for tickets
 (decisions/ticket-read-receipts-2026-08-30.md), relocated to where it
 belongs.

fields.name: viewed_at_ms
fields.description: viewed_at_ms is when the person actually looked.

fields.name: viewed_by
fields.description:
viewed_by is the principal subject of the person who looked. It is normally
 equal to Message.recipient — a delivery is viewed by its addressee — but it
 is stored rather than assumed, because a delegate viewing on someone's
 behalf is a real case and an inferred value could not tell the two apart.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by EXACT string equality against the
 caller's namespace claim (never the level-or-below containment the
 administrative namespace rule uses). It is the tenant half of the identity
 `recipient` carries the subject half of: that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant".

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 TWO DIFFERENT ENFORCEMENTS, and they are not the same failure:
   - WRITE (this record's publish path). eventbus's PublishHandler stamps
     this field from the publishing token's namespace claim and REFUSES the
     publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none. Stamp-or-
     refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty: a row published with an empty
     namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read.
   - READ (stratum's record query plane, c2s half). The generated egress
     filter holds every row to the reader's own claim, and a row that fails
     the comparison HALTS THE JVM rather than failing the one call — the
     filter is the backstop behind the store's own query, so it firing means
     that query is broken.

 Bounded like every other string here. Not a (spec.query_field): the field
 exists to be the egress boundary, and making it a caller-supplied predicate
 is not what a boundary is.

message.name: ScottyActivity
message.description:
ScottyActivity is the ARTIFACT left by every write into knowledge.

 §1: "Nothing reaches knowledge without leaving an artifact. Authored facts —
 a phone number, a written policy, a stated deadline — are not distilled from
 anything, so if current state could change with no immutable record, the
 authored half is unrecoverable." ScottyState's requires_artifact_on_write
 enforces that this type exists; this is that type.

 §4 is the reason it is a generated RECORD rather than something the service
 writes for itself: "Scotty must not be the writer of the accounting. If it
 were, 'doesn't rat Dennis out' becomes 'can omit'... Accounting is a
 byproduct of the call path, stamped at the generated seam." The neutral
 auditor reads THIS, and this carries what was DONE — entity kind, entity id,
 principal, request id — never what was said.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 ScottyActivityBus with topic ref scotty.ScottyActivityBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: activity_id
fields.description: activity_id is the record key: one row per WRITE, not one per entity.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.description:
entity_kind and entity_id name what was written. EQ-filterable, because
 "every artifact for this ticket" is the question provenance has to answer.

enum_values.name: SCOTTY_ENTITY_KIND_TICKET_CHAIN
enum_values.description:
A TICKET_CHAIN artifact is left ONCE per chain, on the hop that reaches
 Config.max_chain_hops — the moment Scotty stops mediating. entity_id is the
 chain_id. It records that AI mediation hit its limit, which is a thing that
 was DONE and therefore belongs in the auditor's store; no ticket is decided
 by it.

fields.name: occurred_at_ms
fields.description:
occurred_at_ms is the RANGE criterion — "what happened between D1 and D2"
 is the auditor's own question.

fields.name: acted_by
fields.description:
acted_by is the principal on whose behalf the write happened. NOT redacted:
 §4 says a finding is a citation naming "action A by principal X at T", and
 a citation whose principal egress clears is not a citation.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s
 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER
 — eventbus stamps scotty's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. acted_by is the
 authenticated human the write happened for, taken from the verified token
 (service.rs `principal()`) or from the written row's own (spec.principal)
 field, never from anything the caller writes. That is the value the
 generated wrapper's row filter must compare against.
 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query, and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that wrote
 this row" and "which row did that request write" are one predicate asked of
 two record types. Without it provenance stops at the accounting plane's
 edge, which is precisely where §4's auditor starts.

 Empty is legitimate, not an error: an unauthenticated path has no Caller to
 read one from, so a required-and-absent field would fail the publish rather
 than record the gap.

fields.name: spiffe_actor
fields.description:
spiffe_actor is the DELEGATE that made the call, stamped by EventBus from
 the token's `act` claim at publish time — the agent acting for the person
 in acted_by, unset in the ordinary non-delegated case. Provenance only: it
 is never the principal, and sys/spec.proto forbids wiring it into one.

 The service does not set it and must not: like spiffe_id above, a value
 written here would be a claim about identity that nothing verified.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose write this artifact records. It is the tenant half of the identity
 acted_by carries the subject half of — that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant", by EXACT
 string equality against the caller's claim (never the level-or-below
 containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over EVERY record in
 the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of them for this
 type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than the caller's
 halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like acted_by.

 AN EQ (spec.query_field), and it did not used to be. The reasoning that kept
 it off was that a boundary is not a caller-supplied predicate — which is
 right about the CALLER and wrong about the SERVER. The client-facing read
 plane pins this field to the caller's verified namespace claim BEFORE the
 store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into; the record
 store evaluates only the criteria a record annotates, so without this line
 the pin is generated and silently ignored, leaving the aborting egress
 filter as the only tenant boundary. tacplus refuses (spec.record).c2s_read
 on a record whose namespace field is not EQ-queryable, for exactly that
 reason.

 It stays uncallable by clients, which is the part the old comment cared
 about: the emitted GetScottyActivityRequest and ListScottyActivityRequest
 carry no namespace field, and ScottyActivityReadFilter — the only filter a
 c2s caller supplies — is generated without one.

# tacplus Registry

This file is embedded in `registry.json` and describes how to navigate it.

## Overview

This registry describes a tacplus-generated service mesh with:
- **1099** message types across **66** packages
- **708** RPCs across **64** gRPC services
- **68** state boundaries

## Structure

The registry is a recursive `PackageNode` tree. Each node has:
- `name` — short package name
- `full_path` — slash-separated path from root
- `children` — sub-packages
- `proto_packages` — declared protobuf package names represented by a leaf node
- `vservices` — virtual service identities declared by proto files in a leaf node
- `client_dependencies` — declared `grpc_*_client` edges with `surface_kind`
- `types` — message type descriptors (`TypeInfo`)
- `rpcs` — RPC descriptors (`RpcInfo`)
- `boundaries` — state boundary descriptors (`BoundaryInfo`)

Navigate by traversing `children` to reach any package. Directory paths are navigation
labels; use `proto_packages`, `TypeInfo.package`, and `ServiceInfo.package` for
declared protobuf identity.

## Self-Description

The `$schema` field points to `registry.schema.json` (JSON Schema format).
The type definitions under `sys/tacplus` describe this document's own structure:
`PackageNode`, `TypeInfo`, `FieldInfo`, `RpcInfo`, `BoundaryInfo`, `EnumValueInfo`.

## Field Metadata

`FieldInfo` includes protobuf oneof grouping:
- `oneof` — true when the field is a member of a protobuf oneof group
- `oneof_name` — the declared oneof group name

`FieldInfo.constraint_infos` contains machine-readable validation constraints
derived from proto annotations and compiler default bounds. Prefer
`constraint_infos` over parsing the legacy prose strings in `constraints`.

Durable `service_store` messages are surfaced in metadata:
- `TypeInfo.service_store` / `service_store_name` / `service_store_label`
- `FieldInfo.store_key` — the key field for a service_store value
- `FieldInfo.quorum_write` — field writes require quorum acknowledgement

## VService Metadata

`PackageNode.vservices` lists file-level `(spec.vservice)` identities with
`name`, `id`, and declaring `package`. Hosted vservice RPC surfaces expose their
hosting label on `ServiceInfo.host_label`.

## Client Dependencies

`PackageNode.client_dependencies` lists file-level `grpc_s2s_client`,
`grpc_c2s_client`, `grpc_w2s_client`, and `all_grpc_s2s_clients` declarations.
Each edge includes `source_package`, `surface_kind`, `service`,
`target_package`, `target_service`, and `wildcard`.

## Event Topology

`PackageNode.event_publishes` and `PackageNode.event_watches` list validated
actor bindings from `(spec.event_publish)` and `(spec.event_watch)`. Each entry
includes the actor package/message, canonical `topic_ref`, resolved
`event_type_fqn`, broker label, RPC stem, and derived auth shape.

## RPC Surfaces

`RpcInfo.auth_model` is the primary annotated service model (`s2s`, `c2s`, or
`c2d`). `RpcInfo.surfaces` lists every generated transport/auth surface for an
RPC. Use it when you need additive exposure such as W2S gRPC-over-REST:
`surface_kind` / `auth_model` may be `w2s`, `transport` is `grpc_over_rest`,
and the row carries the W2S HTTP route plus namespace/auth metadata.

## RPC Classification

Every RPC may carry classifier metadata derived from the governed verb registry:
- `auth_model` — primary annotated service model: `s2s`, `c2s`, or `c2d`
- `verb_status` — `classified`, `unclassified`, or `exempt`
- `rpc_verb` / `rpc_noun` — the canonical `Verb<Noun>` split when classification succeeds
- `method_pattern` — the static shape (`GET`, `LIST`, `WATCH`, `CREATE`, `UPDATE`,
  `DELETE`, `ACTION`, `CLIENT_STREAM`, or `BIDI`)
- `access_kind` — `READ` or `WRITE`
- `verb_class` — `core`, `action`, or `agent`
- `entitlement_scopes` — grant scopes that admit the method, ordered broad to narrow
- `retry_policy` — semantic retry/idempotency posture
- `capability_scope` — primary package capability bucket for capability-any expansion
- `verb_definition`, `verb_boundary`, `audit_meaning` — governed dictionary metadata
- `rejected_verbs` — non-canonical verbs that fold to the canonical verb and are rejected
- `folded_to_verb` — canonical verb for a rejected leading synonym, when known
- `allowed_patterns` — patterns this canonical verb may resolve to
- `handler_shape` — `UNARY`, `SERVER_STREAM`, `CLIENT_STREAM`, or `BIDI`

The legacy `category` field is also present for older policy code:
- **ACCESSOR** — read/observe operations (Get, Watch, Query, KeySet, Size, ContainsKey, List, Peek, Subscribe)
- **MUTATOR** — write/modify operations (Set, Put, Delete, Remove, Clear, Publish, Offer, Reload)
- **EXECUTOR** — action/command operations (Assist, Authenticate, Authorize, Evaluate, Exchange, etc.)

Per-service aggregate enum values (`ALL_ACCESSORS`, `ALL_MUTATORS`, `ALL_EXECUTORS`) are available for security policy rules.

## Security Metadata

Each `BoundaryInfo` carries:
- `boundary_callers` — which services can call this boundary cross-namespace

Each `RpcInfo` carries:
- `auth_disabled` — whether authentication is bypassed
- `auth_services` — S2S caller service allowlist when applicable
- `auth_entitled_users` — C2S entitlement-checked user access
- `auth_any_user` — C2S authenticated-user access without entitlement checks
- `auth_model` — primary annotated service model (`s2s`, `c2s`, or `c2d`)
- `target_namespace_field`, `subject_namespace_source`,
  `target_namespace_source`, `target_namespace` — namespace authorization inputs
- `surfaces` — per-transport auth metadata, including derived W2S rows
- `category` — legacy accessor/mutator/executor classification
- `rpc_verb`, `rpc_noun`, `method_pattern`, `access_kind`, `verb_class`,
  `entitlement_scopes`, `retry_policy`, `capability_scope`, `verb_definition`,
  `verb_boundary`, `audit_meaning`, `rejected_verbs`, `allowed_patterns`,
  `handler_shape` — governed verb/pattern metadata when classification succeeds
